Information extraction uses keyphrase and keyword ranking, semantic relatedness with Personalized PageRank, graph-based features, denoising, and neural categorization. Emergency systems employ interactive learning, active-learning-based annotation, alert ranking, ontologies, and multimodal datasets. Privacy-preserving summarization uses secure binary embeddings.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal crisis data, quantified confidence and standardized evaluation, bias-aware annotation, interactive user feedback, population and out-of-sample validation, workload-aware alert prioritization, and richer semantic interpretation of urban activity.

ab7e42a6705b1d4d985292a4de52e26930bf60b2.text:
### Graph-Aware Recommendation and Dynamic User Modeling

This community centers on recommender systems and representation learning for complex, evolving networks. Core themes include collaborative filtering, sequential and session-based recommendation, playlist and news continuation, social and trust-aware recommendation, and link or relationship prediction. Researchers address practical challenges such as sparse feedback, cold-start users and items, long-tail content, missing modalities, shared accounts, multiple domains, unreliable ratings, and fraudulent reviews.

Typical methods combine matrix factorization, Markov chains, slope-one predictors, latent-variable models, metric learning, ontologies, and content-based or hybrid approaches. Neural methods increasingly dominate, including variational autoencoders, nonlinear latent-factor models, convolutional review models, recurrent/session models, graph neural networks, and multimodal embeddings. Network representation learning and graph clustering integrate topology with node content, while metapaths and cross-modal embeddings support heterogeneous urban and social networks. Link prediction is studied through clustering, dynamic embeddings, and continuous-time models.

Recent trends emphasize temporal robustness and changing graph structure, richer modeling of diverse user tastes, anonymous-session behavior, missing information, and cross-domain interactions. Optimization is also becoming sequential and interactive, as shown by reinforcement learning for advertising, while evaluation increasingly considers real-world effects, user experience, security, and online production performance.

d0fc387b501c0675f0400c1d78d34c1990ecadaf.text:
## Neural and Semantic Information Retrieval

This community centers on improving search and ranking across heterogeneous information needs. Core themes include learning-to-rank and document/passage retrieval, query understanding and clustering, expert and entity search, dataset and app discovery, web quality and spam detection, and retrieval for question answering. Several works address temporal, cross-lingual, personal-memory, and non-factoid retrieval.

Typical methods combine traditional retrieval structures with machine learning: probabilistic or fielded models, bipartite and k-nearest-neighbor graphs, kernel methods, support-vector machines, and ensemble ranking. Neural approaches use word and query embeddings, semantic hashing, entity-aware representations, multi-task learning, and deep scoring functions that model local relevance, groupwise or cross-document interactions, and permutation-invariant rankings. Re-ranking and multi-stage architectures are recurring strategies for balancing effectiveness and latency. Other work emphasizes axiomatic regularization, post-hoc interpretability, dependency graphs, and benchmark collections.

Recent trends show a strong shift toward pretrained language models, especially BERT and multilingual BERT, applied to passage and document ranking, entailment-based filtering, and zero-shot cross-lingual transfer. Large labeled datasets and TREC-style evaluation support deep learning at scale, while research increasingly incorporates schema semantics, temporal signals, dynamic user intent, and explainability.

d19edcd8b18b66e41ac60f9b56662d5465f4a8a3.text:
### Scholarly Information Retrieval, Linked Data, and Research Infrastructures

This community studies how digital libraries and scholarly information systems can improve discovery, access, and evaluation. Major themes include domain-specific search and interactive query expansion; knowledge organization systems (KOS), thesauri, classifications, and their representation in SKOS and the Semantic Web; and bibliometric-enhanced retrieval using citations, co-authorship, co-word structures, Bradfordizing, and informetric analysis.

Typical methods combine controlled-vocabulary mapping, Linked Data and ontology-based enrichment, citation and network analysis, large-scale text mining, and distributed processing with Hadoop. User-centered work analyzes search sessions, task types, mouse fixations, relevance judgments, and visual or map-based interfaces. Evaluation commonly uses standardized topics, retrieval test collections, user studies, and agreement measures such as Fleiss’ Kappa and Krippendorff’s Alpha.

A strong strand addresses scholarly data infrastructure: dataset citation and attribution, automatic detection of dataset references and author contributions, semantic publication quality assessment, and integrated research-data libraries. Recommender systems increasingly appear as deployable services for digital libraries and reference managers. Recent directions emphasize open and reproducible science through Jupyter notebooks, linked open data, data stewardship and privacy, neural title simplification, and scalable mining of scientific publications.

f82f48cc682d84921557a8f301f39163af802e93.text:
## Recommender Systems, Bias, and Dynamic Network Intelligence

This community centers on recommender systems that balance accuracy with diversity, fairness, novelty, and commercial or social objectives. A major theme is popularity bias: multiple studies seek greater exposure for long-tail items through personalized, temporal, or diversity-aware re-ranking, while also examining its unequal effects on users and content providers. Fairness research measures protected-attribute representation and mitigates bias through constrained re-ranking, fairness-aware MMR, hybrid models, and “antidote” data. Other work optimizes revenue, user utility, push delivery, and recommendations tailored to age, social context, location, or product categories.

Typical methods include random walks and diffusion on user–item or signed bipartite networks, collaborative filtering, Poisson factorization, greedy utility maximization, iterative reputation/ranking algorithms, simulation, and offline or online user studies. Cognitive models such as ACT-R guide tag recommendation and analyses of frequency, recency, semantic context, and forgetting.

A complementary systems strand addresses hidden-database crawling, third-party query re-ranking, scalable experimentation, and streaming similarity joins using sliding windows, time-dependent similarity, sketches, and sublinear-space estimation. Recent trends emphasize temporal evaluation, evolving-network emergence, robustness to sparse or noisy feedback, reproducibility, and socially responsible recommendation.

388cdd1ebb963ca5482496724b59b96a3f494533.text:
**Scalable Graph, Database, and Data-Science Systems**

This community studies efficient representation, querying, and analysis of relational, RDF, graph, temporal, and streaming data. Core themes include SPARQL optimization—OPTIONAL patterns, federated query reordering, fuzzy and incomplete information, preferences, and relational-to-RDF/OWL mappings—as well as conjunctive-query evaluation, join ordering, inequalities, and parallel communication complexity.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with practical systems techniques: MILP-based plan optimization, worst-case-optimal and multiway joins, indexing for reachability and distance queries, graph-to-relational translations, and high-level graph engines such as Gremlin, EmptyHeaded, and TrieJax. Distributed and in-memory architectures emphasize replication consistency, parallel recovery, OLTP execution, and extreme streaming-update throughput using Accumulo and D4M.

A second major strand addresses data management beyond query execution: provenance graphs, workflow reproducibility, dataset version control, concise object summaries, and automated data-structure design. Integrated analytics and machine learning increasingly connect relational feature extraction, sparse tensors, declarative modeling, and end-to-end data-science lifecycles.

Recent work extends database ideas to blockchains and cross-chain atomicity, lightweight blockchain emulation, temporal graphs, and collaborative data platforms, while emphasizing specialized indexing, hardware-conscious execution, scalable distributed processing, and usability without sacrificing performance.

df09b4bc146a9508898b78762a07a4600b3cf55f.text:
## Network Dynamics, Social Influence, and Content-Aware Graph Analysis

This community studies how network structure shapes visibility, information, opinions, and collective behavior. Major themes include opinion dynamics under social influence, bounded confidence, susceptibility, interpersonal biases, antagonistic or signed ties, polarization, consensus, and multiple correlated topics. Closely related work examines social power, centrality, PageRank, node discoverability, strategic link formation, and recommendation-driven feedback loops.

A second theme is mining real-world interaction networks. Studies analyze Twitter controversy, student and political networks, traffic activity, temporal communication events, social-media user “genotypes,” and online abuse. Narrative analysis represents characters and conversations in books, films, and television as static, temporal, or multilayer graphs for classification, summarization, and role analysis.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic measures (centrality, assortativity, community roles, structural balance), dynamical-systems and control analysis, game theory, mean-field and asymptotic results, optimization, and stochastic interaction models. Empirical work uses voting records, social-media text, movie scripts, and communication traces, alongside unsupervised inference, vocabulary-based detection, feature extraction, and experiments on real networks.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and multilayer networks, content- and topic-aware interactions, temporal event discovery, semantic opinion models, automated moderation, and explicit feedback between evolving user beliefs and personalized recommendations.

33e295482b7d4c6dc13bff5e7321051df2f28b26.text:
## Adaptive Data Management for Complex and Streaming Information

This community studies scalable organization, querying, analysis, and optimization of heterogeneous data. A dominant theme is XML and complex data warehousing: XML query patterns, structural preferences, XOLAP rollups, summarizability, fragmentation, benchmarks, and materialized-view selection. Related work addresses complex medical, archaeological, multimedia, multisource, and multiversion data.

Typical methods are workload-aware and data-mining-based. Frequent-itemset mining, query clustering, affinity analysis, and k-means guide index, view, and fragmentation decisions; pattern trees support XML matching and OLAP operators. Researchers also use simulation to evaluate object clustering, dynamic access patterns, and database performance, alongside benchmark construction for XML warehouses, text classification, and top-*k* processing.

A second theme concerns large-scale text and social streams: scalable document architectures, extreme multi-class classification, temporal community formation, and real-time event detection. These approaches exploit mention anomalies, entity clustering, and deep reinforcement learning for hierarchical label assignment.

Recent trends emphasize automation and adaptation: dynamic physical design, workload evolution, distributed XML storage, complex hierarchies, real-time stream processing, and unified platforms for irregular or multimodal data. Evaluation increasingly relies on dedicated benchmarks and configurable simulations rather than static workloads.

f2b356412d8fc8aec506c3c91d832507697ae50b.text:
### Social Network Structure, Inference, and Diffusion

This community studies online and human social networks as both structured systems and sources of behavioral intelligence. Core themes include network structure—homophily, assortative and multiscale mixing, rich-club organization, heavy-tailed degree distributions, friendship paradoxes, spatial mobility, and network growth—as well as dynamics of interaction, information diffusion, social learning, and contagion.

Typical methods combine large-scale platform data (Facebook, Twitter, YouTube, mobile calls, transactions, games, and community question answering) with graph statistics, power-law and sampling analysis, embeddings, supervised learning, maximum-likelihood estimation, Hawkes processes, agent-based simulation, and analytical models of influence and polling. Studies also use found experiments around disasters, emergencies, emotional bots, and online interventions.

Applied work addresses demographic prediction, fake-account and money-laundering detection, disaster damage assessment, epidemic monitoring, suicide ideation, privacy exposure, search, polling, marketing, and engagement optimization. Several papers emphasize that network structure can improve monitoring while reducing sampling costs, but also creates bias, overload, privacy risks, and asymmetric influence.

Recent directions favor multiplex and weighted networks, latent or hidden agents, temporal and spatial dynamics, interpretable controls, and network-aware inference rather than isolated-user analysis. Simulation tools and scalable methods increasingly complement empirical studies of massive, evolving platforms.

ba52c42d4535dbbf59e2e3b9e0414191b12d2b81.text:
### Collaborative Web Knowledge and Social Search

This community studies how user-generated web content can be structured, searched, and exploited as collective knowledge. Major themes include Wikipedia and Wiktionary mining; collaborative tagging and folksonomies; semantic annotation, ontology matching, and knowledge-base construction; and social, professional, and location-aware search.

Typical methods combine graph analysis with statistical modeling and machine learning. Researchers analyze links, categories, tags, clickstreams, and user networks using centrality, HITS/PageRank-like ranking, clustering, power-law and growth models, and measures of semantic similarity. Other work develops parsers and relational transformations for Wiktionary, SKOS encodings, entity linking and disambiguation pipelines, and learning-to-rank or matrix-factorization systems for personalized search and expertise discovery. Interfaces such as semantic navigation, knowledge maps, and interactive synonym graphs make these structures usable.

Recent directions emphasize scale, multilinguality, and operational applications. Large densely annotated Wikipedia datasets and high-throughput, language-agnostic entity linking support broader language coverage. Professional-network research applies collaborative filtering, homophily, and learning-to-rank to talent search and analyzes job-hop flows. Social search is increasingly modeled as a collaborative process rather than an individual activity, while tagging research continues to examine vocabulary growth, heterogeneity, network structure, and the integration of folksonomies with hierarchical semantic resources.

cedb268af045e486408e95e045b3b694fabd6d95.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing and Analysis

This community focuses on releasing and analyzing sensitive data while balancing formal privacy, utility, scalability, and fairness. Differential privacy is the dominant framework, applied to histograms, sparse and hierarchical data, range and statistical queries, marginal release, clustering, classification, frequent-itemset mining, search logs, mobility data, recommendations, and data exploration. Other themes include k-anonymity and its extensions, slicing and set-valued anonymization, provenance and graph protection, outsourced and federated databases, secure querying, and adversarial disclosure analysis.

Typical methods add calibrated noise, use hierarchical decompositions, wavelet transforms, matrix mechanisms, or learned query strategies. Data- and workload-aware partitioning, adaptive strategy selection, local differential privacy, trusted hardware, secure multiparty computation, perturbation, surrogate graph elements, and synthetic data are also prominent. Several works provide approximation algorithms, error bounds, privacy proofs, or empirical evaluations.

Recent trends emphasize high-dimensional and workload-specific query answering, scalable exploration interfaces, local privacy for personalized services, and privacy-aware machine learning and recommendation. The literature increasingly addresses realistic adversaries and background knowledge, sparse and structured data, federated settings, and societal objectives such as fairness and demographic bias, while seeking stronger utility guarantees rather than privacy alone.

6899dbc06fb4c2f858f900f5c62ca263c9e7d63c.text:
### Learning and Approximation for Interactive Data Systems

This community focuses on making large-scale data analysis faster, more adaptive, and accessible across relational, graph, RDF, visual, sensor, video, and spatiotemporal data. A central theme is approximate query processing: sampling algebras, maximum-entropy summaries, deep generative models, adaptive aggregate learners, deterministic error guarantees, sequence representations, and distributed quantile algorithms reduce computation while controlling accuracy. Interactive exploration is another emphasis, including insight recommendation, provenance-aware visualization, IDE benchmarking, fast-stream anomaly explanation, and transparent scaling of browser applications.

Machine learning is increasingly embedded in database internals. Deep models estimate correlated join cardinalities, generate query plans, represent workloads as vectors, learn indexes, and optimize ML inference. Learned and adaptive techniques also appear in partitioning, resource sharing, and workload-aware analytics. Typical methods combine neural networks or embeddings with query plans, sketches, reservoir sampling, probabilistic models, cost models, and online adaptation.

A further strand addresses expensive multimodal analytics: hierarchical predicates and approximate filters accelerate CNN-based image and video queries, including aggregation, limits, spatial relationships, and autonomous IoT-camera processing. Data integration and access remain important, using local relational embeddings, heterogeneous-data tunneling, semantic-web view selection, keyword diversification, and natural-language query logs. Overall, the papers trend toward autonomous, statistically aware systems that co-design query processing, learning, visualization, and constrained distributed execution.

38b6712c561bef574981e59eda34e7f811745860.text:
### Scalable Data Management, Indexing, and Compression

This community focuses on making large-scale data systems faster, smaller, and more scalable. Major themes include database indexing and query processing; compressed representations for inverted lists, bitmap indexes, multidimensional data, and key-value stores; spatial and scientific data management; and high-throughput analytics and transactions.

Typical methods combine algorithmic design with hardware-conscious optimization. Researchers develop cache-aware set-intersection and bitmap algorithms, B-tree and relational spatial indexes, zone and multidimensional indexing schemes, and adaptive predicate evaluation. Compression is central: variable-byte, Huffman, difference, run-length, and frame-of-reference methods are redesigned for fast decoding and direct processing of compressed data. SIMD vectorization, bit-parallel operations, and carefully ordered data improve both compression and query execution. Hashing and synchronization receive rigorous analyses alongside practical implementations.

Recent trends emphasize exploiting modern hardware and distributed infrastructures. GPU/CPU hybrids accelerate spatial comparison and OLTP, while distributed in-memory dataflows support graph mining and scientific workloads. Systems increasingly target petabyte-scale astronomy, metadata, arrays, and social-network data, with relational databases serving as integrated platforms. Work also addresses index update cost, storage overhead, query batching, and portable implementations, reflecting a shift from isolated algorithms toward end-to-end, data-intensive systems.

0e87154bac4da0c0b3e5bcea264d89fab59ff622.text:
### Categorical and Algebraic Foundations for Data Integration

This community develops mathematically principled models for databases, schemas, mappings, and data transformation. A central theme is **functorial data migration**: schemas are categories (often finitely presented graphs with path equations), instances are set-valued functors or algebraic theories, and schema morphisms induce adjoint migration operations corresponding to projection, union, joins, and related queries. The Categorical Query Language (CQL) and FQL provide executable, graphical, and open-source tooling.

A second theme concerns semantics for heterogeneous and view-based integration. The database category **DB** models instances as relational tables and mappings as structured query computations rather than ordinary functions; sketches, monads, and Kleisli constructions extend this framework to generalized values, nulls, and exceptions. Simplicial databases, operads of wiring diagrams, and algebraic property graphs offer geometric, compositional, and graph-oriented representations.

Typical methods combine category theory, equational logic, algebraic data types, monads, adjunctions, sketches, and formal query semantics. Applications and newer directions emphasize guaranteed integrity during migration, computational-science data sharing, supply-chain and enterprise integration, and mappings between relational, graph, streaming, and microservice data.

4cb5b4d7397dab1ff30d054c371d6dabf9340df9.text:
## Uncertainty, Privacy, and Explainable Graph Analytics

This community centers on reasoning over imperfect, evolving, and privacy-sensitive graph data. A major theme is uncertain-graph reliability: estimating s–t reachability, maximizing reliability by adding edges under a budget, and extending reliability to multiple terminals or externally conditioned edge probabilities. Related work addresses node classification when links are unreliable and similarity search over uncertain time series.

A second theme is privacy-preserving social graphs. Proposed approaches inject uncertainty into graphs, use uncertain adjacency matrices while preserving expected degrees, and enable users to exchange noisy link information to construct local views. These works emphasize privacy protection without eliminating analytical utility.

The community also studies semantic and explanatory graph search. Methods include relationship explanation for entity pairs, relaxing relationship queries when exact semantic associations fail, weakly supervised contextualization of knowledge-graph facts, and explanations of how user actions influence social-media feeds. News-story analysis similarly seeks hidden relationships among events beyond simple similarity search.

Typical methods combine complexity and approximation analysis, scalable sampling or indexing for #P-hard reliability estimation, probabilistic modeling, anonymization schemes, graph search, and weak supervision. Recent trends move toward conditional uncertainty, budget-aware optimization, user-facing explainability, and privacy mechanisms based on uncertainty semantics.

ca40bda1e73510f871487bc4644fb4a06094b616.text:
### Recommender Systems: Context, Ranking, and Scalable Personalization

This community studies personalized recommendation, with a strong emphasis on points of interest (POIs) and venues in location-based social networks. Core themes include improving collaborative filtering (CF) and matrix factorization under sparse interaction data, modeling geographic proximity, temporal activity, popularity, and contextual appropriateness, and producing high-quality ranked lists rather than merely predicting ratings. Broader work addresses recommendation scalability, web-navigation subgraphs, privacy, and nearest-neighbor search.

Typical methods include latent-factor models—extended through metric, logistic, and geographically or temporally regularized factorization—alongside collaborative ranking and top-\(N\) optimization for graded relevance. Researchers also use probabilistic mappings between tags and location tastes, content and review features, social-centric relevance scores, and multiple location-based similarities. Parallel and distributed CF implementations and multi-GPU \(k\)-nearest-neighbor algorithms target efficiency.

Recent trends move toward richer context-aware POI recommendation and neural representation learning. Joint geographic-temporal models capture changing spatial influence, while category-aware location embeddings combine sequential and categorical information. Privacy-preserving CF and scalable infrastructure reflect growing practical concerns alongside accuracy improvements.

8523b94ee09b64d5b99000465249d09086f04a24.text:
### Data-Driven Personalization for Online Fashion

This community focuses on improving fashion e-commerce through personalized recommendations, product understanding, and demand-aware assortment planning. Key tasks include recommending complementary items within browsing sessions, modeling changing customer preferences, mapping articles to an interpretable “Fashion DNA” space, and predicting footwear size—particularly for users without purchase history.

Typical methods combine transactional sales and behavioral data with product content such as images and tags. Neural architectures are central: an LSTM-based dynamic customer model addresses changing inventories, trends, and shopping behavior, while a deep network learns product and customer-style vectors whose interactions estimate purchase likelihood. Session-based recommendation also uses tailored sampling strategies when interaction data are noisy or unsuitable for direct training. For assortment decisions, customer demand is decomposed into a style or fashionability quotient separate from commercial factors, with backtesting used to evaluate prediction errors.

Recent trends emphasize production-ready systems, cold-start support, dynamic personalization, and the integration of visual/content signals with sales data. The research increasingly connects recommendation quality with practical retail concerns including complementary purchasing, style breadth and depth, stock turnover, fit, and customer experience.

3cb9c3537d05cab977570eec162dc4d4de351f55.text:
### Keyphrase Extraction, Summarization, and Semantic Document Access

This community centers on extracting and organizing salient information from documents, especially keyphrases, keywords, titles, passages, and summaries. Applications span scientific and biomedical literature, news aggregation and broadcast monitoring, scholarly repositories, social tagging, and news-popularity prediction.

Typical methods combine lexical statistics—term frequency, inverse document frequency, position, readability, and stylometry—with supervised machine learning, neural networks, topic clustering, and ranking models. Graph-based approaches are prominent: PageRank variants, graph-of-text models, multipartite graphs, dependency trees, and folksonomy graphs capture relations among words, concepts, topics, users, items, and tags. Text denoising reduces documents to information-rich sentences, supporting indexing, relation extraction, and summarization. Hierarchical combinations of single-document summaries address multi-document settings, while relevance–diversity objectives formalize result selection.

A notable trend is the move from surface-level extraction toward semantic modeling, including semantic relatedness, semantic roles, contextual connectivity, and topic–keyphrase reinforcement. Neural and hybrid systems increasingly complement established statistical techniques. Another emerging direction is privacy-preserving retrieval and summarization: Secure Binary Embeddings enable approximate computation over protected document representations. Overall, research emphasizes domain adaptation, scalable real-time systems, richer conceptual representations, and improved integration of extraction with retrieval, recommendation, and scholarly communication services.

20eb189cd526dfc27d1e90ddf344901f04707194.text:
**Network Diffusion, Influence, and Epidemic Dynamics**

This community studies how information, influence, infections, and failures spread through complex, social, temporal, and interdependent networks. Major themes include influence maximization and seed selection; epidemic containment and economic cost; source localization and network-structure recovery from partial cascades; dynamic PageRank and popularity prediction; and diffusion-based applications such as worker recruitment, advertising, conservation, and product adoption.

Typical methods combine probabilistic cascade models (independent cascade, susceptible-infected, linear threshold, Bass, and continuous-time Markov models) with graph algorithms and optimization. Submodularity and adaptive submodularity support approximation guarantees for greedy or adaptive policies, while mixed-integer programming addresses network design and stochastic cascade control. Other approaches use Jordan centers/covers, random walks, message passing, random matrix theory, particle-swarm heuristics, soft thresholding, diffusion distances, and optimization-based inference. Simulations on social, real-world, random, and evolving networks are common.

Recent directions emphasize realistic dynamics: temporal and adaptive topologies, evolving external interests, myopic feedback, mobile agents, non-submodular contagion, and resource constraints. Research also increasingly addresses incomplete observations, multiple sources, hidden structures, aggregate data, economic outcomes, and learning-based cascade modeling, including contrastive training over partially ordered infections.

2e9ce58c787737ca7d86b2b9731a4ba359c48ff1.text:
### Scientometric Mapping, Evaluation, and Scholarly Networks

This community focuses on measuring and mapping science through bibliometric, altmetric, and network-based methods. Major themes include field and technology delineation, institutional and journal mapping, citation and co-citation structures, academic reputation, collaboration, and research impact assessment. Considerable attention is given to improving evaluation through field-normalized indicators, percentiles, fractional citation counting, PageRank, centrality measures, and new author- and journal-level metrics. Studies also examine the validity, universality, and limitations of these indicators, including journal impact factors, SNIP, I3, and citation-based researcher assessment.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, Altmetric, F1000, DBLP, patent, web, library-loan, and social-media data. Network analysis, similarity measures, fuzzy matching, author-name disambiguation, clustering, regression, principal-component and factor analysis, and precision/recall validation are common.

Recent trends emphasize alternative and societal impact measures, while highlighting altmetric heterogeneity, data quality, and dependence among sources. Research increasingly addresses digital-era changes weakening journal-level proxies, compares emerging databases, recommends venues using dynamic interests, and studies diversity, international collaboration, conference publishing, and online scholarly communication.

700dfeb6461474343cff89afdaeaccc1d456fbfc.text:
### Text Mining and Mathematical Information Retrieval

This community centers on intelligent organization, classification, and retrieval of textual and mathematical content. Core themes include unsupervised document clustering, automated and multilingual text categorization, authorship and opinion-spam detection, feature selection, topic diversity, and classification under class imbalance. A major strand addresses mathematical information retrieval: combining keywords with formulae, comparing presentation- and content-based search, formula similarity, semantic enrichment, mathematical-language processing, and digital repositories.

Typical methods include probabilistic mixture and topic models, vector-space representations, term/class relevance weighting, association-rule mining, k-nearest-neighbor and k-medoids classifiers, genetic feature optimization, dependency and hypernym-based features, graph propagation, and tree or hypergraph similarity. Evaluation commonly uses precision, recall, Bpref, and classification accuracy. Systems are implemented in practical digital-library and web infrastructures, including Lucene-based search, faceted interfaces, MathML/LaTeX processing, and scalable rendering.

Recent work shifts toward richer semantic and neural representations: formula embeddings, symbol2vec, joint topic–equation models, deep regression for indexing quality, and content-based rather than purely presentation-based formula search. Other trends include combining textual and mathematical evidence, semantic LaTeX enrichment, improved scalability, robust similarity metrics, and user-oriented search interfaces.

0f58808114b501fb55cf040e399e14931bfdf950.text:
### Topic Modeling and Real-Time Social Sensing

This community centers on extracting latent structure, events, and actionable signals from large, heterogeneous data collections. A major theme is topic modeling: extensions of LDA and PLSA address hyperlinks, temporal evolution, bibliographic networks, multi-grain opinions, scientific-article bundling, and creative cross-domain discovery. Dynamic and clustered models focus on changing topic birth, death, popularity, and scalable learning.

A second theme is social-media analytics. Twitter and other platforms are treated as real-time sensors for sports, disasters, disease outbreaks, misinformation, tourism, and public sentiment. Work develops event detection, sub-event recognition, representative summarization, burst-region detection, timeline generation, and popularity or revisitation models. Spatial and temporal information is repeatedly integrated for event retrieval, visualization, and location-based services.

Typical methods include probabilistic generative models, Bayesian nonparametrics, topic and network analysis, density-based clustering, neural networks and character embeddings, ontology similarity with fuzzy logic, query expansion, information extraction, and optimization algorithms. Systems are evaluated through retrieval, prediction, clustering, accuracy, and operational case studies.

Recent trends emphasize scalability and near-real-time processing, including parallel topic modeling, document summarization, heterogeneous evidence integration, and decision-support tools for emergency response and global disease forecasting.

0660a19a054db19b3a8f3de87d1a66741bad9e06.text:
### Durable, Temporal, and Semantic Web Knowledge

This community studies how digital artifacts, web resources, and scientific information can remain interpretable, discoverable, and trustworthy over time. Major themes include digital-object and repository architectures (Fedora, aDORe), preservation of evolving Linked Open Data, provenance and versioning, and semantic modeling of scientific claims, mechanisms, activities, and cultural objects. Web archiving is especially prominent: researchers examine collection quality, topical drift, memento acquisition, temporal search, missing and orphaned resources, archive usage, and long-term changes in domains and page titles.

Typical methods combine standards-based data models and ontologies (RDF, PROV-O, Open Annotation, SharedCanvas, MPEG-21, nanopublications), persistent identifiers, SPARQL and query languages, and repository or aggregation architectures. Empirical studies use large crawl, archive, access-log, annotation, tweet, and bookmarking datasets; systems apply caching, federated search, focused crawling, timeline generation, entity linking, summarization, and machine-learning or neural models.

Recent directions emphasize integrating social media with web crawling and temporal retrieval, improving archive freshness and response times, preserving scholarly “orphans” and evolving datasets, and supporting richer machine-readable scientific communication. Large public RDF corpora, character-based tweet embeddings, time-aware entity relatedness, and interoperable annotation frameworks illustrate a shift toward scalable, context-sensitive knowledge services.

508a5255f4ddb5565a6e670b1cac281b57235f9c.text:
### Scientometrics, Citation Networks, and Fair Research Evaluation

This community focuses on measuring and mapping science through bibliometric data. Major themes include the validity and normalization of citation indicators; evaluation of researchers, journals, institutions, countries, and R&D programs; technology and disciplinary mapping; and the emergence, structure, and historical roots of research fields.

Typical methods include citation, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, co-authorship, and journal–journal networks; network centrality and PageRank; community detection and network overlays; text analytics; and reference publication year spectroscopy (RPYS). Researchers develop or compare indicators such as the h-index, K-index, weighted indices, percentiles, integrated impact measures, SNIP, Crown indicators, and fractional-counting approaches. Statistical distributions, Gini and diversity measures, similarity-adapted publication vectors, and MeSH-based representations are also used.

Recent trends emphasize field- and citation-normalized evaluation, percentile and top-paper approaches, correction of aggregation and counting biases, and fairer treatment of collaboration and author contributions. Studies also question journal impact factors, statistical inference, and national assessment exercises. Digital scholarship is weakening the link between journal impact factors and individual paper impact, while new databases such as Dimensions and interactive tools such as RPYS i/o expand data sources and exploratory historiography.

dd6b155661765c238f1a9d1e51111b4416cc6585.text:
## Community Detection in Complex and Dynamic Networks

This community centers on defining, detecting, and evaluating communities in complex networks. A major theme is the lack of a universal community definition, motivating multi-criteria evaluation, context-sensitive quality functions, comparisons of modularity variants, and benchmarks for overlapping detection. Methods include modularity optimization (including multislice and adaptive signed-edge formulations), stabilized label propagation, density-based clustering with manifold learning, clique percolation, core detection, and spectral approaches based on graph spectra, local expansion, Krylov subspaces, and personalized PageRank. Theoretical work studies detectability limits, localization, conductance, and the conditions under which neighborhoods form good communities.

Increasing attention is given to realistic network structure: overlapping and multiple membership, node and edge attributes, weighted and two-mode graphs, multiplex networks, and latent group models. Dynamic settings motivate regularized layouts, evolving bibliometric classifications, real-time dense-cluster discovery, and latent models for co-evolving networks. Algorithm selection based on network parameters and scalable local methods address very large graphs.

Applications examine peer influence in churn and technology adoption, risky behavior, social activity organization, Web-service interactions, event detection, and biological or scientific networks. Overall, the field is trending toward scalable, local, dynamic, attributed, and overlapping community analysis, paired with more systematic evaluation.

d091c490491bfb24367033a4649d6814b1c79866.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Discovery, and Digital Communication

This community examines how scholarly impact, visibility, and communication are changing through online platforms, repositories, and alternative metrics. Major themes include validating altmetrics against peer assessments, citations, teaching or societal-interest labels, and distinguishing Twitter, Mendeley, readership, downloads, hyperlinks, and citations. Studies also address data quality, heterogeneity, disciplinary dependence, and the interpretation of digital traces.

A second theme is scholarly discovery and evaluation: recommendation systems for articles and venues, knowledge-domain visualizations, conference and reviewer classification, paper–reviewer matching, and rankings of publishers, books, and conferences. Particular attention is given to books and humanities and social-science outputs, where conventional citation coverage is limited.

Typical methods are large-scale bibliometric and webometric analyses; correlation, regression, principal-component and factor analysis; citation, download, loan, review, and social-media data mining; expert interviews and qualitative comparisons; and machine-learning methods for hyperlink classification, bibliographic reference resolution, recommendation, and reviewer assignment. Integer programming is used for optimized matching.

Recent trends emphasize open access, arXiv and disciplinary repositories, early dissemination, and real-time reactions to preprints. The literature increasingly treats scholarly communication as a networked, computerized process while seeking more robust, multifaceted indicators and improved tools for navigating information overload.

dcbf8b92182794912eae3aa8c8669b6e36c5287f.text:
## Social Networks: Structure, Diffusion, Influence, and Risk

This community studies how online and other complex networks form, evolve, and shape behavior. Major themes include community structure and tie strength; information, rumor, product, and meme diffusion; popularity, engagement, and virality; anomaly, malicious-URL, fraud, and fake-news detection; privacy exposure and social risk; and influence in commercial, scholarly, financial, and gaming networks.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic measures—betweenness, pair-dependency, modularity, centrality, fractal dimension, structural balance, and heavy-tailed distribution analysis—with threshold diffusion models, cascade analysis, and competing-product games. Statistical and machine-learning approaches predict popularity, gender, sports outcomes, hot research topics, video engagement, and malicious behavior. Other work uses multivariate Hawkes processes and dynamic programming to model or control endogenous and exogenous activity, while visual analytics supports financial risk management. Large-scale studies draw on Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Yelp, citation databases, and online games.

Recent trends emphasize richer signals beyond network topology: mass media and absent nodes in diffusion, content and sentiment, visual memes, crowd flags, social ties, user heterogeneity, and engagement rather than views alone. Research also increasingly targets intervention—fact-checking selection, campaigning, incentives, privacy controls, and influence measurement—alongside scalable analysis of massive, evolving networks.

29ac5044c343f4a5c0f01aa8c10dfbacc7fc4f8a.text:
## Computational Analysis of Social Media, Politics, and Misinformation

This community studies how online social networks shape political opinion, public discourse, identity, and information reliability. Major themes include political communities and polarization, voter-preference and demographic inference, misinformation and rumor propagation, extremist and state-sponsored influence campaigns, platform bias, and security threats from bots, Sybils, spam, and crowdturfing. Other work examines public-health interventions, food culture, application privacy, and inequalities in visibility by gender and race.

Typical methods combine large-scale data collection from Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, Gab, and search systems with network analysis, crawling, surveys, and controlled experiments. Machine-learning approaches include nonnegative matrix factorization for community detection, sparse learning and regression for preference inference, latent Dirichlet allocation and embeddings for topic and user modeling, supervised and semi-supervised classification for spam, stance, rumor, and extremism detection, and image-based demographic classification. Formal bias measures, graph-walk adjustment, propagation features, and temporal analysis address sampling and platform effects.

Recent trends emphasize cross-platform analysis of echo chambers and coordinated influence, fine-grained modeling of narratives and emotional dynamics, detection of automated or crowd-assisted manipulation, and interventions such as social bots for smoking cessation or fact checking. The papers also increasingly stress methodological validity, including evaluation bias, selective digital traces, and distinctions between data-induced and ranking-induced bias.

06a7b45ae928555ecc5e0e69a6ebacd0f0a2ae9d.text:
## Information Retrieval, Ranking, and Search Infrastructure

This community centers on improving information retrieval (IR) through better relevance modeling, scalable indexing, and richer understanding of queries, documents, and entities. A major theme is neural learning to rank: DeepRank, Match-Tensor, K-NRM, and related models use local matching, recurrent networks, translation matrices, kernel pooling, and end-to-end pairwise learning. Word embeddings support query expansion, query clustering, document–query similarity, entity salience estimation, and short-text classification, while binary hashing and signatures enable fast large-scale similarity search.

Other work addresses practical search quality and data integration: web-spam detection, content-quality ranking, entity resolution and consolidation, syntactic pattern discovery, wrapper robustness, entity-focused tables, and entity-relationship retrieval. Similarity joins and time-series indexing emphasize partitioning, hashing, and adaptive pruning for massive datasets.

Evaluation is another strong theme, including LETOR benchmarks, relevance and credibility measures, dynamic retrieval theory, interaction modeling, online learning to rank, multileaving, and dueling-bandit ranker comparison. Recent directions favor deep semantic matching combined with traditional signals, real-time entity and news processing, scalable online experimentation with user feedback, and explainable or credibility-aware search.

949d0e2797b067d07a4afb0912b876cdaca8a076.text:
### Multiplex Social Networks: Dynamics, Diffusion, and Online Identity

This community focuses on analyzing social systems as multiplex or multilayer networks, where users may be connected through friendship, communication, professional, semantic, online, and offline ties. Major themes include multilayer centrality and structural measures; community detection, group evolution, and prediction; influence, information diffusion, and epidemic spreading; and cross-platform identity, privacy, and link prediction.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic analysis with empirical datasets from Facebook, Twitter, blogs, email, Foursquare, Web 2.0, and cellular mobility. Researchers develop multilayer extensions of degree, reciprocity, motifs, clustering, and similarity measures; compare GED and SGCI for detecting group changes; and adapt Louvain and Infomap for dynamic graphs. Diffusion studies use independent-cascade, branching-process, epidemic, spectral, and dynamical models, while recommendation and identity tasks employ weighted relational layers, feature engineering, negative sampling, and predictive models. Topic modeling, sentiment classification, fact-check retrieval, and generative models support content analysis.

Recent directions emphasize unified theories of multiplex processes, scalable analysis of changing networks, heterogeneous sampling and missing-data effects, synthetic network generation, cross-device and cross-platform matching, and applications to misinformation, public-health campaigns, recommendations, and organizational talent discovery.

d37dc3652093a9913da12af99562121118c1bc22.text:
## Network Representation and Analysis in Dynamic, Complex Graphs

This community studies how to represent, sample, model, and mine large social, information, semantic, and affiliation networks. Major themes include community detection and clustering; link and relationship prediction; knowledge-graph fact checking and triple scoring; node similarity and representation learning; centrality, dense-subgraph, triangle, and anomaly analysis; and signed, uncertain, and multilayer networks.

Typical methods combine statistical graph models—stochastic blockmodels, maximum-likelihood inference, Markov chains, random walks, and possible-world semantics—with scalable algorithms such as MapReduce, wedge sampling, graph crawling, peeling, and external-memory distributed generation. Machine-learning approaches use ensembles, discriminative predicate paths, deep embeddings, structural-identity representations, citation-context representations, and content–structure integration.

Recent work increasingly addresses networks as evolving, heterogeneous, multiplex, and temporally uncertain objects. Examples include continuous-time relationship prediction, dynamic embeddings, coevolving multilayer link prediction, hierarchical change-point detection, and temporal diffusion through indirect co-location links. Another trend is improving reliability and scalability: sampling methods gain quality guarantees or exploit auxiliary graphs, while approximate centrality and triangle estimation reduce computational cost. Applications span privacy advice, insider-trading and criminal-network analysis, semantic search, scholar recommendation, and social-network exploration.

4f97e067995d609c38f742c54bf824e02ed6ab8a.text:
## Geospatial Social Media for Urban Intelligence

This community studies how user-generated and mobile data reveal human behavior, urban structure, and place experience. Major themes include mobility and migration (Twitter trajectories, international travel, home locations, commuting, group colocation), urban functional regions and boundaries, and dynamic neighborhood characterization. Other work examines sensory and emotional geographies—soundscapes, smellscapes, beauty, quietness, happiness, park-related affect—and socioeconomic conditions such as deprivation and post-disaster economic recovery.

Applications span business intelligence and recommendation, including restaurant-location and business-zone selection, special offers, event participation, route recommendation, review-based rating prediction, and daily-deal diffusion. Disaster and collective-action studies use social media for situational awareness, event detection, and workload-aware alert ranking.

Typical methods combine geotagged Twitter, Flickr, Foursquare, Facebook, mobile-network, transaction, and multimodal disaster data with sentiment and semantic analysis, spatial-temporal modeling, network reconstruction, low-rank and tensor factorization, Gaussian-mixture inference, machine learning, recommender systems, visualization, and objective-function optimization. Researchers increasingly quantify uncertainty in geolocation and trajectories and exploit non-geotagged content.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal imagery and text, finer-grained and dynamic urban inference, scalable global datasets, affective and sensory mapping, and operational decision support for planning, commerce, and emergency response.

54dc31f65830d8b063d4bd16f223390decdf2b06.text:
## Advances in Personalized Recommender Systems

This community centers on improving personalized recommendation under sparse, implicit, noisy, heterogeneous, and rapidly changing user–item data. Core themes include collaborative filtering, personalized ranking, sequential and session-based recommendation, content and multimodal modeling, social/network-based recommendation, and interpretable systems.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, slope-one predictors, neighborhood models, Bayesian Personalized Ranking, co-clustering, Markov chains, and graph algorithms to neural approaches such as autoencoders, autoregressive models, recurrent networks, nonlinear latent-factor models, and list-wise deep architectures. Hybrid and collective models combine ratings, content, social information, and multiple item relationships. Other work addresses signed preference networks, substitutes and complements, reputation, shilling attacks, and privacy.

Recent trends emphasize neural and multimodal recommendation, including visual, textual, auditory, and educational signals; robustness to missing modalities and cold-start users or items; and modeling temporal behavior across and within sessions, including anonymous users. Researchers also increasingly represent diverse user interests with mixture models, exploit non-IID coupling among users and items, and seek interpretable, scalable methods. Active learning, automatic recommender-algorithm selection, filter-bubble analysis, and transfer learning further broaden system adaptability and reliability.

a895619b4f1f23fcfee159261e7e05dd6149deb1.text:
## Graph Querying, Semantics, and Scalable RDF Systems

This community centers on efficient querying and management of RDF and graph data. A major theme is SPARQL foundations and optimization: OPTIONAL and left-outer joins, multiset semantics, algebraic rewriting, entailment under OWL, preferences, provenance, incomplete information, and hybrid SPARQL–keyword queries. Federated querying is prominent, including source selection, heuristic reordering, replicated fragments, SPARQL-LD, and large-scale federation experience.

A second theme is graph analytics and path processing. Work addresses regular and context-free path queries, reachability in temporal graphs, shortest-path and distance indexing, graph traversal systems, and information diffusion or dynamic monopolies in social networks. Temporal models increasingly support time-aware paths and centrality measures.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and semantics analysis with indexing, query rewriting, cost-based or runtime optimization, incremental evaluation, graph parsing, and empirical benchmarking. Schema and data-quality research includes relational-to-RDF/OWL mappings, RDF shapes, XML schema inference, unordered XML, and validation.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and adaptive execution (ROSIE, incremental maintenance), heterogeneous and replicated data sources, usability through example-based querying, property-graph frameworks, workload generators such as gMark, and specialized benchmarks for geospatial RDF stores.

03f47d75e6d3cc2833e32daca0a1e05d9549d457.text:
### Adaptive Data Warehousing, XML Analytics, and Benchmarking

This community centers on performance, scalability, and automation for data-intensive systems. A dominant theme is complex and XML data warehousing: reference architectures, XOLAP operators, summarizability over irregular hierarchies, XML tree patterns, fragmentation, and materialized-view selection. Related work addresses integrating heterogeneous, multimedia, medical, archaeological, and Web data for decision support, including lightweight business intelligence for small enterprises.

Typical methods are workload-aware and data-mining-based. Frequent-itemset mining, query clustering, affinity analysis, and k-means guide index, view, and fragmentation decisions, while pattern trees and query-based techniques support XML analytics. Simulation and configurable evaluation frameworks study dynamic access patterns, object clustering, and database behavior. Benchmark suites and generators—including XML warehouse, big-data, text-classification, stream-processing, and top-k benchmarks—provide scalable, application-specific evaluation.

Recent trends emphasize increasingly heterogeneous and large-scale data, distributed processing, and controllable benchmarking. Research moves beyond static workloads toward evolving access patterns, dynamic administration, and adaptive physical design. It also increasingly couples optimization choices—such as indexes and materialized views—and targets complex hierarchies, high-dimensional text, streaming systems, and the 4V requirements of big data.

a0ac8f87b719f9f88a8a6f4af09003ab9e3853bc.text:
## Durable, Semantic, and Temporal Web Archives

This community studies how to preserve, model, discover, and reuse evolving digital knowledge. A central theme is durable archiving: digital repositories such as Fedora and aDORe represent heterogeneous, compound objects, metadata, rights, and OAIS packages, while VXA preserves executable decoders to protect compressed content from technological obsolescence. Related work addresses scholarly “orphans,” scientific research lifecycles, provenance, authoring, versioning, and nanopublications.

Web preservation is another major focus. Studies measure resource disappearance and archival coverage, estimate creation dates, analyze archived collections and domains longitudinally, and investigate acquisition, timestamping, and replay challenges. Methods include large-scale crawl and access-log analysis, longitudinal sampling, link-neighborhood analysis, social-bookmark evidence, and focused crawling augmented with social media.

The community also develops semantic infrastructures: RDF/LOD publication, SPARQL querying, temporal and multi-version data models, semantic layers for archived documents, and ontologies for mechanisms, cultural objects, and contextualized educational resources. Open Annotation and SharedCanvas support interoperable scholarly and cultural interpretation, while entity linking and data-quality principles improve discoverability and trust.

Recent trends emphasize freshness and evolution rather than static preservation: integrating social signals into crawling and temporal search, tracking changing linked datasets and biological entities, detecting breaking news from Wikipedia edit spikes, quantifying annotation loss, and building scalable, machine-readable corpora such as TweetsKB.

577fc84bff3b3ea1fb5343e6c995e07f55755edb.text:
### Principles and Systems for Scalable Data Management

This community studies efficient, reliable, and intelligent data management across relational, graph, distributed, and cloud settings. A central theme is query processing and optimization: join ordering via mixed-integer linear programming, worst-case-optimal and multiway joins, cardinality estimation with deep learning, sampling-based aggregates, inequality-aware conjunctive queries, and theoretical bounds on plans and communication. Parallel correctness, coordination-free computation, MapReduce optimization, and SQL-on-Hadoop comparisons address distributed execution.

Another major theme is high-performance systems. Papers explore column stores for graph analytics, relational graph engines, adaptive indexing, high-level query engines, multicore OLTP, parallel recovery, transaction-conflict repair, and predictive execution for distributed transactions. Practical data platforms support dataset versioning, stale-view cleaning, replicated index tuning, fast-stream analytics, and visual-insight recommendation.

Methods range from combinatorial and complexity analysis to MILP, worst-case communication bounds, sketches and sampling, learned models, declarative languages, and system benchmarking. Reliability and governance appear through bounded staleness, cloud privacy, MapReduce security, and collaborative lifecycle management for machine learning.

Recent directions emphasize integrating machine learning into databases and analytics, automating optimization and resource allocation, exploiting multicore and cloud infrastructure, and unifying declarative usability with competitive performance.

e175091ed836bfd57905165393b698a0ccc437f2.text:
## Data Integration, Uncertainty, and Explainable Database Intelligence

This community centers on making heterogeneous, noisy, and inconsistent data usable. Major themes include data fusion and truth discovery across conflicting sources, entity resolution and record linkage, probabilistic and uncertain databases, integrity repair, and provenance-based explanation. Related work addresses causality for query answers and non-answers, peer-to-peer data exchange, XML access-control consistency, workflow reproducibility, and crowdsourced data quality.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with practical database algorithms. They include probabilistic graphical and relational representations, knowledge compilation, decomposition trees, safe query plans, approximate lifted inference, indexing and sorting for uncertain joins, probabilistic blocking and locality-sensitive hashing, and optimization of human–machine workflows. Provenance graphs, Datalog rewritings, answer-set programs, database repairs, chase procedures, and axiomatic discovery of dependencies support explanation, diagnosis, and consistency management. Mining tree-shaped graph patterns and spatial or urban data relationships extends integration beyond conventional relations.

Recent trends emphasize scalable automation and practical quality guarantees: deep-learning-based entity resolution, probabilistic blocking for large-scale linkage, hybrid models supporting multiple truths, and cooperative human–machine ER. Research also increasingly targets correlated uncertainty, probabilistic top-k and aggregate queries, crowdsourcing reliability, spatial task assignment, and performance explanations for MapReduce. Overall, the community is moving toward integrated systems that combine uncertainty reasoning, provenance, automation, and explicit quality control.

e3507c5a6852796291f338d24f5879010755a112.text:
### Network Dynamics, Influence, and Social Information Flow

This community studies how structure, interaction, and information shape complex networks, especially social and online systems. A major theme is opinion dynamics: DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, biased-assimilation, and signed-network models examine consensus, polarization, disagreement, antagonism, susceptibility, and social power. Extensions address multiple interdependent topics, dynamic interaction matrices, heterogeneous thresholds, Bayesian decision makers, and feedback between opinions and personalized recommendations.

A second theme concerns identifying influential structure. Papers develop and compare centrality measures, axioms for evaluating them, navigability and discoverability scores, robustness indices, PageRank manipulation, and methods for modifying edges to improve communicability, coverage, delay, or influence. Link prediction, spectral embeddings, Markov-chain optimization, and backbone discovery provide scalable computational tools.

Methods commonly combine graph theory, Laplacian and matrix analysis, dynamical-systems and consensus theory, random walks, spectral methods, optimization, information theory, motifs, and empirical analysis of Twitter, traffic, and interaction data. Web crawling provides historical context for collecting and indexing online information.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic, topic-specific, and personalized behavior; controversy detection and stance-aware explanation; scalable algorithms for large networks; and network design that actively shapes information flow, resilience, and polarization.

7b2b407198117cdb9706990a4acc5145ff769d75.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Retrieval, and Bibliometric Intelligence

This community studies scholarly information spaces as interconnected networks, emphasizing author identity, research impact, retrieval, and knowledge organization. A major theme is author-name disambiguation in digital libraries and collaboration networks, ranging from initials-based and topological heuristics to hybrid, semi-supervised, and seed-and-expand methods; evaluation uses multiple labeled datasets, simulated identities, and manually curated claims.

PageRank and related Google-matrix techniques recur throughout the community. They are applied to author-citation networks, papers, patents, Wikipedia, and multilingual cultural or geopolitical networks to distinguish popularity from prestige, identify communities, trace technological emergence, and analyze information flow. Work also examines centrality stability, eigenvectors, damping factors, and structural patterns such as striations.

Typical methods combine social-network analysis, bibliometrics, statistical modeling, visual mapping, and iterative ranking. Information retrieval research explores discipline-specific query expansion, Bradfordizing, knowledge maps, visualization, and bibliometric-enhanced search, alongside studies of relevance-assessment reliability.

Recent directions include scalable network modeling with graphons and MapReduce, Linked Data for metadata enrichment, publication recommendation under limited ground truth, semi-supervised disambiguation, multilingual mining, and interactive visual frameworks. The community also increasingly addresses reproducibility and infrastructure through Jupyter notebooks and studies of durable scientific data practices.

7a25b0d18481ed1a55edf4e8e5d7aac6ba0b138b.text:
### Collaborative Web Knowledge and Social Search

This community studies how user-generated platforms become knowledge infrastructures for search, organization, and collaboration. Major themes include Wikipedia and Wiktionary mining; folksonomy and collaborative-tagging dynamics; semantic enrichment and ontology/thesaurus construction; social and professional search; and influence, expertise, and attention in online networks.

Typical methods combine large-scale crawling and log analysis with graph-based modeling. Researchers extract links, categories, tags, edits, clickstreams, and user profiles; analyze power laws, vocabulary growth, heterogeneity, homophily, reciprocity, and network centrality; and apply clustering, matrix factorization, PageRank/HITS, ontology matching, NLP, entity linking, and learning-to-rank. Prototype systems demonstrate news detection, semantic navigation, synonym and related-term search, entity ranking, expertise discovery, and product design from tags. Evaluation uses test collections, human judgments, click data, and interactive experiments, including methods to correct presentation bias.

Recent work trends toward scalable, multilingual, and densely annotated resources such as DAWT; high-throughput, language-agnostic entity linking; and personalized search in professional networks. Social search is increasingly modeled as collaborative and context-dependent rather than solitary, while tagging and attention are analyzed as evolving collective processes. Wikipedia and Wiktionary increasingly serve as bridges between informal social data and structured Semantic Web representations.

1ad14aff3f5a9a5dfda4d316858a842f07e59c2d.text:
### Scalable Search, Data Management, and Scholarly Discovery

This community focuses on making large, heterogeneous data collections searchable, analyzable, and useful. Core themes include database indexing and compression (bitmap indexes, Roaring bitmaps, multidimensional indexes, adaptive sorting, and lightweight alternatives to B-trees), efficient query processing (RDF, graph, fuzzy, skyline, workflow, and relational keyword queries), and scalable data acquisition from hidden web databases.

Typical methods combine algorithmic analysis with empirical systems evaluation. They exploit SIMD instructions, GPUs, multicore CPUs, distributed in-memory dataflows, batching and data sharing, and machine-word parallelism. Scientific applications are prominent, including astronomy, pathology imaging, finite-element analysis, and mining scholarly publications. Semantic publishing uses extraction, linked open data, and citation-network queries to assess research quality.

Information retrieval and recommendation form another strand: query and tag reranking, academic-paper recommendation services, learning-to-rank with counterfactual correction for biased clicks, and fairness-aware diversification. Recent work increasingly applies machine learning to system decisions, including learned graph query planning and deep reinforcement learning for sponsored search. Overall, the trajectory is toward petabyte-scale scientific data platforms, GPU/distributed acceleration, service-oriented scholarly tools, and more personalized, fair, and user-controllable search.

0f8eead1c7c180087009fc66bbe007a53e6efb69.text:
### Scholarly Metrics, Search, and Open Science

This community studies how scholarly information is indexed, ranked, evaluated, and disseminated online. A major theme is comparative bibliometrics: Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and Microsoft Academic Search are assessed for citation coverage, highly cited-document identification, journal metrics, institutional benchmarking, and research-program evaluation. Google Scholar generally offers broader coverage, but raises concerns about data quality, profile maintenance, platform decline, and manipulation of h-index values through article merging or splitting.

A second theme concerns information retrieval and library discovery. Studies examine ranking factors for library materials, search-engine technology in catalogs, credibility signals, query expansion, representative query sampling, and learning-based topic selection to reduce the cost of constructing IR test collections.

Typical methods include large-scale citation and web-data extraction, longitudinal and cross-sectional comparisons, correlation analysis, benchmarking, network/link analysis, visualization, automated querying, and computational-complexity analysis.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes open access measurement, combining sources to distinguish legal and sustainable availability, and testing the effects of repository mandates. Other emerging concerns include the growing citation of older literature, alternative online attention indicators, academic search-engine coverage, and the reliability and governance of metrics used in research assessment.

9eccb258d5467e528504b76ba0bdaf418fa887ee.text:
## Spatial Community Detection, Modularity, and Network Intelligence

This community centers on detecting and analyzing structure in networks while accounting for geography, distance, and computational constraints. Several papers extend modularity-based community detection: distance-aware null models and spatially-near modularity incorporate physical separation, while distance modularity is used to identify geographically dispersed organizational groups. A latent-parameter, node-centric model addresses the challenge of inferring spatial connection costs.

A second major theme is the theory of modularity optimization. Studies establish that maximizing bipartite modularity is NP-hard and develop additive-approximation algorithms and theoretical limits for modularity maximization and clustering.

Applications emphasize security and social-network intelligence. Research models the spatial and temporal diffusion of political violence, identifies violent gang members using modified centrality and arrest metadata, and introduces ORCA for estimating gang membership, finding influential individuals, and decomposing criminal ecosystems. Viral-marketing work develops scalable methods for selecting small tipping-model seed sets, evaluated across many real-world networks.

Overall, the research trends from topology-only community detection toward geographically informed objectives, scalable algorithms, provable approximation guarantees, and operational analysis of violence, gangs, and influence.

200a78929af1181699098a9a1b649b7ea94a7ab1.text:
### Social, Cognitive, and Temporal Recommendation

This community centers on recommender systems enriched by social, temporal, geographical, and cognitive information. A major theme is social tagging and hashtag recommendation: studies model human memory and tag reuse through ACT-R activation, especially frequency, recency, semantic context, forgetting, and individual versus social reuse. These cognitive-inspired methods address sparse folksonomies and often outperform popularity-based baselines.

A second theme is social and marketplace recommendation. Research combines transactions with friendships, trust, location, comments, and product categories, examining social influence, consumer choice, cold start, and the differing effects of friends versus crowds. Spatial recommenders model geographical sparsity, regional interest drift, sentiment, and travel behavior.

Typical methods include collaborative filtering, hybrid and content-based recommendation, matrix factorization comparisons, neural item embeddings, deep learning for cold start, graph and link-analysis ranking, trust models, and cognitive activation equations. Evaluation increasingly considers diversity, novelty, and practical scalability alongside accuracy.

Another thread develops scalable similarity search for streaming and unbounded data, using sliding windows, time-dependent similarity, locality-sensitive hashing, freshness and quality-aware retention, and top-*k* joins. The community also includes theoretical models of PageRank without teleportation, rumor convergence, and social commerce networks.

Recent trends emphasize integrating heterogeneous data, temporal dynamics, bounded-memory streaming, explainable cognitive models, and deployment-oriented architectures rather than optimizing prediction accuracy alone.

3ab0911e113f6cdd0a10c2d89d70da34cb6c0eec.text:
## Social Media Mining, Search, and Community Intelligence

This community studies how social platforms can reveal users, behaviors, attitudes, and information structures. Major themes include identifying gang affiliates on Twitter, measuring public attitudes toward China, characterizing communities through social identity and cohesion, and detecting illicit drug dealing or abuse. Public-health work extends analysis from text to geo-tagged Instagram imagery, using user tags and automatically generated image annotations.

Typical methods combine supervised and multilabel classification, profile-description word embeddings, behavioral and network analysis, and multimodal text–image modeling. Cross-platform discovery is another focus: hashtags link Twitter, Flickr, and YouTube for clustered immersive search, while Pinterest recommendations map Twitter interests to pinboard topics and diversify visual results. Digital-archive research uses character n-gram language models and suffix-tree indexing for approximate search and document comparison. Ranking-comparison measures support longitudinal evaluation of search engines, while user taglines offer alternative summaries of expertise and interest.

Recent trends emphasize richer representations—embeddings, images, and platform-spanning signals—alongside fine-grained, large-scale measurement and practical systems for law enforcement, public health, recommendation, and digital scholarship.

63137939c6b363a402020c36a8d2f207ce8d6b0c.text:
### Geometric Models, Routing, and Constrained Network Generation

This community centers on geometry-based models of complex networks and algorithms that exploit or reproduce their structure. HyperMap infers latent hyperbolic coordinates by replaying network growth, providing a fast mapping method for real networks. Geometric inhomogeneous random graphs (GIRGs) offer a theoretical framework for networks combining geometry, clustering, and heterogeneous connectivity, while also supporting decentralized greedy routing and a theoretical account of the algorithmic small-world phenomenon.

A complementary theme is how structure shapes network dynamics: cascade studies show that even simple information-diffusion rules produce markedly different outcomes across network models, motivating analysis beyond the simplistic “superspreader” view.

Several papers address controlled random-graph generation. Metropolis–Hastings sampling generates graphs conditioned on properties such as connectivity, including spatially embedded Waxman networks. Generalized higher-order \(k\)-edge switching extends edge-swap methods to improve access to graph spaces under constraints such as fixed degree distributions.

Overall, the work trends from abstract network geometry toward practical inference, decentralized algorithms, dynamic-process analysis, and more flexible, reliable sampling of structurally constrained graphs.

68b06b875f604c9c5f32b7895de85fba1086c5ae.text:
## Network Science of Knowledge, Software, and Online Communities

This community applies complex-network analysis to human and computational systems. Major themes include online collaboration and governance (especially Wikipedia), scientific collaboration and interdisciplinarity, bibliographic-data quality, software architecture, and organizational or healthcare networks. Researchers examine community structure, centrality, degree mixing, preferential attachment, small-world and scale-free properties, influence, and network evolution.

Typical methods combine web crawling and bibliographic extraction with graph statistics, longitudinal and multilayer analysis, centrality measures, community/group detection, clustering, and network sampling or simplification. Temporal behavior is modeled using Markov and hidden Markov models, finite-state comparisons, null models, sequence analysis, and measures of dynamicity. Citation and entity-entity networks are used to assess knowledge structures and impact, while software is represented through class dependencies.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes dynamic, negative, and normative interaction: revert-driven conflict, “war/peace” states, conservative norm evolution, multilingual editing, and Wikipedia’s role in social movements and collective memory. Other emerging directions include sequence-based analysis of distributed work, robust cross-language growth clustering, entitymetrics, web-search-derived interdisciplinarity, and stronger scrutiny of database inconsistencies and sampling-induced structural bias.

6e7307df8143773b0d6073d9a812df63c3132635.text:
## Energy-Efficient and Autonomic Distributed Databases

This community investigates how database architecture and query execution can reduce energy consumption without sacrificing performance. A central theme is energy proportionality: comparing relational, in-memory, and key-value systems; evaluating query optimization under varied workloads; and treating energy as a first-class objective alongside response time and throughput.

Several studies explore scale-out designs, including dynamically sized clusters of lightweight (“wimpy”) nodes as alternatives to over-provisioned servers. They address the friction costs of parallelism, workload adaptation, data migration, and dynamic partitioning in shared-nothing systems. Other work targets cluster-level architectural choices for energy-efficient parallel DBMSs.
