Data placement is another major theme. Graph partitioning, replica selection, and co-location are used to reduce network communication, congestion, and energy costs for relational and large-scale analytical workloads.

The community also emphasizes autonomic, resource-aware systems operating on opportunistically available workstation resources. Systems such as H2O automate replication, load balancing, backup, and adaptation to changing machine availability.

Recent trends move toward integrated management of energy, performance, resources, and placement: adaptive cluster sizing, physiological partitioning, workload-aware query controls, and self-managing distributed databases designed for both operational efficiency and reduced environmental impact.

4f0513f0dabac00ad9fbe3a2b33ea39cebad8e09.text:
### Diffusion, Influence, and Epidemic Processes on Networks

This community studies how information, influence, disease, and failures propagate through complex, social, temporal, and interdependent networks. Major themes include influence maximization and marketing, epidemic modeling and containment, source localization, hidden-network recovery, and diffusion-signal comparison. Applications span malicious-information tracing, mobile crowd sensing, conservation, cyber-physical infrastructure, advertising, product adoption, and video popularity.

Typical methods combine probabilistic cascade models—including independent cascade, susceptible-infected, SIS, linear-threshold, continuous-time Markov, and complex-contagion models—with optimization and inference. Researchers use submodularity and adaptive submodularity for greedy seed selection, mixed-integer programming for network design, particle-swarm heuristics for estimating infection probabilities, and random-matrix, message-passing, and optimization techniques for epidemic costs and resilient systems. Source detection uses Jordan centers, candidate subgraphs, covering algorithms, and two-stage procedures, while cascade structure is learned from partial temporal information using directed spanning trees and contrastive training.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and partially observed settings: evolving networks, adaptive containment, evolving teleportation in PageRank, online and adaptive influence campaigns, collective diffusion, and temporal-versus-static seed selection. Work also increasingly incorporates economic outcomes—cost, revenue, pricing, adoption, and resource constraints—rather than measuring spread alone.

32209690aafd1a4eac72e3b1065a68854a686ea4.text:
## Dynamic Topic and Social-Media Intelligence

This community centers on extracting structured knowledge from large, evolving text and social-media collections. Major themes include latent topic discovery and evolution; event detection, retrieval, summarization, and timeline construction; information retrieval and query expansion; recommendation and popularity modeling; and applications in public health, disasters, tourism, science, and environmental monitoring.

Typical methods include probabilistic topic models such as LDA, hierarchical and nonparametric Dirichlet processes, dynamic models, citation-network topic models, and multi-grain models. Researchers combine these with graph representations, clustering, term-distribution and ontology-based expansion, fuzzy logic, named-entity and relation extraction, and thematic visualization. Social-media studies use statistical propagation and popularity models, neural networks and character-based embeddings, sentiment and interest inference, geotemporal features, and active learning. Evaluation often compares against baselines, expert or journalist summaries, historical discoveries, and operational datasets.

Recent trends emphasize scalability and real-time analysis through data decomposition, document summarization, and streaming systems; richer temporal, spatial, and relational modeling; neural recommendation and multilingual processing; and integrating Twitter, news, Wikipedia, and domain data. Increasing attention is also given to validation, misinformation, actionable decision support, and rare-event forecasting.

cd34fd8afcd06401a95c94c87513e9a7d13f9c26.text:
## Community Detection in Complex and Dynamic Networks

The community focuses on defining, detecting, evaluating, and exploiting community structure in complex networks. Core themes include the ambiguity of what constitutes a “good” community, comparison of partitions using multi-criteria or Pareto-based evaluation, and quality metrics for overlapping and fuzzy communities. Methods range from modularity optimization, adaptive edge weighting, label propagation, density-based clustering, manifold learning, clique percolation, and local spectral or diffusion-based approaches, to probabilistic models with variational Bayes inference. Theoretical work examines spectral detectability limits, metastability in distributed dynamics, neighborhood communities, cores, and global bridges.

A major trend is moving beyond simple, static, single-layer graphs. Research addresses multilayer and multiplex networks, jointly modeling shared and layer-specific communities, overlapping membership, node and edge attributes, and two-mode structures. Scalability motivates local algorithms, PageRank localization, real-time dense-cluster discovery, and algorithm-selection strategies tailored to network characteristics. Dynamic-network studies preserve visual mental maps, track influential core nodes, and analyze evolving bibliometric or social structure.

Applications include web-service networks, Twitter and microblog event detection, social activity organization, smartphone adoption, churn, risky behavior, and peer influence, often combining topology with behavioral or attribute information.

2f76c70b53e6079be5e9b2c1875fe2bddfae0756.text:
## Social Networks, Diffusion, and Influence

This community studies how online and real-world social networks form, evolve, and transmit information, behavior, risk, and cultural artifacts. Major themes include information cascades and rumor diffusion; influence, virality, engagement, and popularity; community structure, homophily, diversity, and strong/weak ties; anomaly, crime, malicious-URL, fake-news, and systemic-risk detection; and privacy, demographic inference, and sensitive behavior such as suicide ideation. Scientific collaboration and citation networks extend these questions beyond social media.

Typical methods combine large-scale network analysis with centrality, modularity, pair-dependency, fractal vulnerability measures, cascade-structure analysis, and randomized baselines. Researchers use machine learning, embeddings, topic and visual-meme models, crowd signals, and content-aware signed-network inference. Temporal behavior is modeled with Hawkes processes, point processes, dynamic programming, and early prediction systems. Experiments include longitudinal platform datasets, real-time event detection, in-vivo rating interventions, and visual analytics.

Recent directions emphasize multimodal and multifaceted data, including transactions, video, text, user profiles, and relational tables; measuring engagement rather than simple views; modeling exogenous forces such as mass media and incentives; and moving from prediction toward intervention—controlling campaigns, limiting misinformation, and managing cascading financial or social risks.

01d8ecb088788d81ba100a08c44baee1db8c7f39.text:
## Scientometrics, Research Evaluation, and Science Mapping

This community centers on measuring, mapping, and interpreting scientific knowledge and research performance. Major themes include citation-based evaluation of authors, journals, institutions, countries, and R&D programs; field normalization and cross-disciplinary comparability; and critiques of impact factors, h-indices, percentiles, rankings, and statistical inference. Other work studies intellectual structure and evolution through citation networks, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, journal relations, technology relatedness, and research fronts.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, and PubMed data with network analysis, centrality measures, clustering, community detection, similarity and distance metrics, fractional counting, and visualization. Proposed indicators include K-index, weighted h-indices, percentile-based measures, normalized impact metrics, contribution-sensitive authorship indices, and institutional publication-profile measures. Text analytics and MeSH terms complement citation data for field taxonomies and paper-level mapping.

Recent trends emphasize open or alternative databases and their data quality, interactive tools such as RPYS i/o and CRExplorer, historiographic reconstruction through Reference Publication Year Spectroscopy, and increasingly fine-grained analyses of co-citation and textual similarity. The literature also stresses fairness, conservation in aggregation, unintended effects of assessment exercises, and the weakening link between journal impact factors and individual paper citations.

d030a52adce1f8a20ebf1fadfe226bfd70c15231.text:
### Learning, Retrieval, and Scalable Data Systems

This community combines intelligent text and mathematical information retrieval with high-performance data management. Research on text mining addresses clustering, classification, authorship analysis, topical diversity, and user-directed grouping. Typical methods include probabilistic mixture models, k-nearest-neighbor and k-medoids classifiers, association-rule feature pruning, hyperonymization, genetic keyword selection, relevance feedback, and active learning. Quality estimation and graph-based propagation extend classification to noisy or linked data.

A second major theme is mathematical search and digital libraries. Systems combine textual keywords with formula queries, using formula canonicalization, semantic enrichment, Lucene-based indexing, merging strategies, and faceted web interfaces. Related work extracts identifier definitions and namespaces from mathematical language and notation.

Database research emphasizes expressive foundations and efficient execution: relational lattices, conjunctive queries over trees, visual query languages, memory-aware and least-expected-cost optimization, and randomized external-memory lower bounds. Systems work targets heterogeneous and graph-intensive workloads through polystores, associative arrays, Accumulo/D4M, Graphulo, and external graph analytics.

Recent trends favor scalable infrastructure and adaptive automation: billion-scale ingestion, provenance storage, cloud cost/performance management, dynamic resource scaling, and learning-based workload advisors. High-recall review and sentence-level feedback likewise push toward autonomous, efficient human-in-the-loop analysis.

3b2e6601ebf264840c1a412d5fa0bd165e8f56e2.text:
## Reliable Data Integration and Probabilistic Analytics

This community focuses on making data management reliable when data are uncertain, inconsistent, correlated, incomplete, or sourced from multiple parties. Major themes include probabilistic databases and approximate query answering; data fusion and truth discovery; entity resolution and record linkage; provenance, causality, and explanations; and integrity constraints, repairs, and secure updates.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with practical algorithms. These include probabilistic query plans, structural decompositions, knowledge compilation, semiring/semimodule representations, indexing and sorting for uncertain joins, and database-native approximation for otherwise #P-hard inference. Data fusion models infer source reliability, account for copying and correlations, and support multiple truths. Entity-resolution systems use embeddings, locality-sensitive hashing, blocking, redundancy, and human–machine cooperation, often optimizing quality guarantees against labeling cost. Provenance and causality are addressed through lineage, Datalog rewritings, abductive diagnosis, and answer-set repair programs. Pattern-mining work develops tree queries, episodes, utility-oriented patterns, and dependency discovery.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and accessible systems: deep-learning-based ER with reduced feature engineering, probabilistic blocking and massive linkage, crowd quality control, spatial task assignment, correlated probabilistic models, and approximate inference executed within standard relational engines. There is also growing attention to explanations, belief annotations, multiple conflicting truths, and principled repair of inconsistent or insecure data.

8d200cae871056691d516065c24b3ddf2f00bdef.text:
### Social Media Networks, Political Behavior, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online social platforms shape political behavior, public discourse, and information ecosystems. Major themes include community structure and polarization, voter and topic preference inference, misinformation and conspiracy diffusion, extremist and state-sponsored campaigns, demographic inequality, and platform security. Applications range from predicting elections and sports outcomes to targeted public-health interventions and analyzing food culture.

Typical methods combine large-scale data collection from Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Instagram, and Gab with graph analysis and machine learning. Researchers use nonnegative matrix factorization, latent Dirichlet allocation, sparse learning, regression, supervised and semi-supervised classification, propagation and temporal features, random-walk sampling, social embeddings, and image-based demographic inference. Studies also employ surveys, browser/search logs, controlled bot interventions, and simulations to evaluate credibility, bias, manipulation, and vulnerability.

Recent work increasingly focuses on misinformation and coordinated influence: echo chambers, fact-checking, narrative competition, autogenerated content, extremist adoption, Russia-sponsored campaigns, crowdturfing, and election disinformation. Cross-platform analyses examine how the same content produces polarization across services, while operational systems pursue real-time spam and bot detection, curated information lists, personalized interventions, and decentralized search. Security research highlights Sybil attacks, social engineering, malicious applications, and the risks of automated agents, alongside efforts to improve privacy, resilience, and trustworthy information access.

61a62efd3270f6105569db9540c58df2b29df57b.text:
### Geospatial Social Media Analytics and Urban Behavior

This community studies how social-media and location-based data reveal human behavior, places, and urban dynamics. Major themes include geolocating tweets and Reddit users without explicit tags; mapping mobility, commuting, visited locations, urban boundaries, and functional neighborhoods; and modeling group colocation, event scheduling, social influence, and commercial activity. Other work applies these data to disaster response, emergency-aid retrieval, collective action, urban parks, emotional routes, soundscapes, smellscapes, and business-site selection.

Typical methods combine natural-language processing, geospatial statistics, network analysis, and machine learning. Convolutional and other deep models integrate tweet text with profile metadata, while heuristic labeling, hyper-local n-grams, Gaussian mixture models, and probabilistic representations infer uncertain locations. Low-rank approximation, density-based spatial-textual clustering, burst detection, mobility networks, sentiment analysis, and multimodal image-text processing are also prominent. Studies increasingly address bias and validation through population synthesis, independent travel surveys, calibration metrics, and out-of-sample testing.

Recent trends emphasize multimodal and large-scale streaming data, continuous detection of spatial events, uncertainty-aware geolocation, and richer semantic interpretation of urban environments. Social media is increasingly treated not merely as content, but as a proxy for mobility, perception, collective action, and city structure.

0db309f03a1c31a3079689053bcbc326403487b1.text:
## Recommender Systems: Personalization, Robustness, and Richer Signals

This community centers on personalized recommendation from explicit ratings, implicit feedback, sequential behavior, and heterogeneous relationships. Core themes include collaborative filtering, personalized ranking, session and playlist continuation, news and educational recommendation, and content-based or hybrid systems. Persistent challenges are sparse interactions, cold-start users/items, long-tail content, diverse user interests, and changing behavior.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, slope-one predictors, nearest-neighbor models, Bayesian Personalized Ranking, co-clustering, and graph/network algorithms to Markov chains, context trees, factorization machines, and collective matrix factorization. Neural approaches increasingly use autoencoders, variational and autoregressive models, recurrent networks, nonlinear latent-factor models, and deep feature-interaction architectures such as DeepFM. Side information is incorporated through text, tags, subtitles, audio, visual features, social ties, and multimodal embeddings.

Recent work emphasizes combining long- and short-term preferences, modeling mixtures of user tastes, exploiting multiple item relationships, and improving recommendations when modalities or feedback are missing. There is also growing attention to interpretable and scalable recommendation, including overlapping co-clusters and real-time cold-start prediction. Trustworthiness is a major concern: studies analyze fraudulent reviews, reputation, rating reliability, filter bubbles, popularity effects, and learned adversarial fake-user attacks.

a7a5dd55f8b237fd115f844ec98b54c2c9686dff.text:
## Network Structure, Dynamics, and Representation Learning

This community studies how to model, sample, analyze, and learn from complex networks, especially social, heterogeneous, temporal, and multi-relational graphs. Major themes include community detection and clustering, link and relationship prediction, anomaly and fraud detection, centrality, dense-subgraph discovery, graph categorization, and structural inference under uncertainty. Several works address applications in knowledge-graph fact checking, entity normalization, insider trading, criminal networks, privacy, online-game teams, and signed social interactions.

Typical methods combine statistical network models—stochastic blockmodels, probabilistic graph grammars, maximum-likelihood inference, and absorbing Markov chains—with machine learning, including random forests, deep neural networks, dynamic and structural embeddings, ensemble scoring, and path-based link prediction. Algorithmic work emphasizes scalable indexing, MapReduce triangle counting, distributed graph generation, local-information optimization, and bipartite peeling.

A strong methodological concern is sampling: surveys and new methods examine traversal strategies, bias, quality guarantees, uncertain networks, and hybrid affiliation graphs. Recent trends emphasize temporal and continuous-time modeling, lossless event representations, temporally robust embeddings, dynamic clustering, indirect co-location links, and richer structural representations that preserve triangles and relational patterns. Overall, the field is moving from static topology toward scalable, dynamic, heterogeneous, and application-aware network intelligence.

79afa66b9a216c3b9ecc385dee7a1690c52e16d2.text:
## Information Retrieval, Ranking, and Search Infrastructure

This community focuses on improving search quality, scalability, and interpretability across web, personal, mobile, bibliographic, multimedia, and time-series settings. Core themes include learning to rank, query understanding and expansion, answer-passage retrieval, expert and entity search, clustering, spam and content-quality detection, and similarity search.

Typical methods combine neural architectures, word and query embeddings, convolutional models, kernel-based interaction modeling, semantic hashing, and supervised or multi-task learning. Ranking research addresses pairwise, listwise, bipartite, and online optimization, including methods that correct click and position bias, learn from list-level feedback, and directly optimize retrieval metrics. Graph and heterogeneous-network representations support expert finding and authority ranking. Entity salience, linking, decomposition, temporal aspects, and news-to-Wikipedia information flow enrich search context.

A parallel emphasis is efficient infrastructure: compressed vector indexes, source-code reranking, topology-preserving signatures, partition-based similarity joins, moving-object indexes, and scalable clustering. Benchmarks such as LETOR 4.0 and WikiPassageQA enable standardized evaluation.

Recent directions emphasize neural and representation-learning approaches, real-time and conversational/mobile search, dynamic and temporal retrieval, explainable and model-agnostic ranking, theoretically reliable online evaluation, and practical systems capable of processing massive or continuously arriving data.

f23501e392eecb3e149eb796f2cb21a65525c353.text:
## Graph Querying, Semantics, and Scalable Graph Analytics

This community centers on efficient, expressive querying and management of RDF, property graphs, XML, and temporal graphs. A major theme is SPARQL: algebraic foundations, multiset semantics, OPTIONAL/left-outer-join optimization, runtime and heuristic query reordering, OWL entailment, preferences, provenance, keyword integration, and federated execution. Work on federations addresses source selection, replicated fragments, large-scale deployments, and heterogeneous relational/RDF resources.

A second theme is graph representation and interoperability. Contributions define property-graph type systems and DDLs, translate SPARQL to Gremlin, map relational databases to RDF/OWL, validate RDF with ShEx, and support querying by example. Path-query research covers regular, context-free, temporal, reachability, shortest-path, and simple-path queries, often with specialized indexes or structural result representations.

Typical methods include formal semantics and complexity analysis, algebraic rewriting, constraint-based optimization, incremental evaluation and view maintenance, partition- and summary-graph indexing, graph parsing, and extensive benchmarking with schema-driven workload generators such as gMark. Provenance, differencing, segmentation, and summarization support reproducible workflows and understandable data-science histories.

Recent directions emphasize adaptive/runtime optimization, robust federated querying through replication, cross-model interoperability, usability for non-experts, temporal analysis, and richer analytical processing of semantic data cubes.

8421fa7995526ba7db3d94ebb6a71ef56647a636.text:
## Data Management, Search, and Collaborative Information Systems

This community centers on scalable data management and information retrieval over relational, multidimensional, spatial, graph, and web databases. Major themes include flexible querying of vague data through fuzzy summaries and SQLf; keyword search, object summaries, hidden-database crawling, workflow retrieval, reranking, and skyline queries; and collaborative tagging, recommendation, vocabulary growth, and group information seeking.

Typical methods combine specialized indexes and compact representations—bitmap and Roaring indexes, multidimensional and spatial indexes, compressed inverted lists, variable-byte and Huffman coding, set-intersection algorithms, hashing, and histogram-aware sorting. Query processing is optimized through top-*k*/any-*k* algorithms, pruning, ranking models, association rules, and grammar-based matching. Distributed dataflow systems support frequent subgraph mining, while GPUs, SIMD instructions, multicore CPUs, and flat combining accelerate transactions, compression, and spatial comparisons.

Recent directions emphasize hardware-conscious, high-throughput processing and reduced storage or maintenance costs, including GPU OLTP, hybrid CPU–GPU analytics, SIMD compression, and lightweight indexing. Research also increasingly addresses user-centered retrieval: concise summaries, personalized reranking, collaborative search, tag consistency, fairness-aware recommendations, and flexible fuzzy summaries. Social tagging studies further model emergent semantics, heterogeneous behavior, and power-law vocabulary and attention dynamics.

60714d117f6a74124b77914c97190870a5427d40.text:
### Social Networks: Dynamics, Influence, and Scalable Analysis

This community studies how information, opinions, products, and influence evolve over complex and changing networks. Major themes include opinion formation and consensus (DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, biased, signed, and multi-topic models), competitive product diffusion, social power, recommender feedback, controversy, and political affinity. A second focus is network structure: centrality, communicability, navigability, robustness, node discovery, PageRank, link prediction, missing edges, communities, and network backbones.

Typical methods combine graph theory, dynamical-systems and control analysis, stochastic processes, game theory, optimization, spectral embeddings, and computational mining of social-media, voting, traffic, and interaction data. Researchers derive convergence, stability, equilibrium, and complexity results; characterize graph conditions; design edge or node interventions; and develop scalable algorithms with accuracy or convergence guarantees.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic, signed, multilayer, and incomplete networks; topic- and time-aware user behavior; and feedback between users and platforms. Work increasingly connects formal models with large-scale data, including temporal event discovery, motif-based controversy detection, political inference, and fast updating of random-walk and centrality measures. Another emerging direction is network design for improving influence, communicability, coverage, navigability, and delay while accounting for robustness and privacy.

4164edfd39fb937d103c8ad89d1eb075ee246993.text:
## Semantic Preservation and Temporal Web Knowledge

This community studies how to preserve, model, discover, and reuse evolving digital information. Major themes include web archiving and missing-page recovery; durable repositories for heterogeneous digital objects; linked open data and multi-version datasets; provenance, annotation, and formal representation of scientific claims; and preservation of scholarly artifacts, social media, manuscripts, and cultural heritage.

Typical methods combine standards-based architectures (OAIS, RDF/S, MPEG-21, PROV-O, Open Annotation, PAV), persistent identifiers, semantic layers, and modular repositories such as Fedora and aDORe. Researchers build temporal query languages, SPARQL services, entity-centric search tools, and virtual machines that archive decoders with compressed data. Empirical studies analyze Internet Archive logs and collections, longitudinal web graphs, social-bookmarking and Twitter data, page titles, links, annotations, and entity co-occurrences. Crawlers integrate topical and temporal signals to collect fresh content, while entity linking and extraction support retrieval and visualization.

Recent work emphasizes evolving and versioned information, quality and repeatable timestamping, interoperable annotations, nanopublications, and provenance. It also addresses “orphaned” web-native scholarship, social-media content, and annotations, alongside improved temporal search, graph access, and preservation workflows for large, heterogeneous archives.

3bd17ede605bd58b83d2c69ac327544d464e8444.text:
## Web Knowledge, Search, and Scholarly Impact

This community studies how web-based resources can be structured, searched, evaluated, and used to measure scientific activity. A major theme is Wikipedia and Wiktionary as collaborative knowledge infrastructures: papers analyze category and link graphs, semantic coverage, entity annotations, synonym discovery, ontology matching, news detection, and entity ranking. Related work applies search-engine technology to library catalogs, query expansion, ranking, and low-cost information-retrieval evaluation.

A second strong theme is bibliometrics and research assessment. Studies compare Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and Microsoft Academic Search; examine citation coverage, highly cited documents, journal metrics, cited half-life, open-access availability, and correlations between citation indicators and peer assessment. Institutional and national research units are benchmarked using publication and citation measures.

Typical methods include large-scale automated querying, citation and hyperlink analysis, social-network and webometric techniques, graph centrality and HITS algorithms, learning-to-rank, statistical correlation, longitudinal comparisons, and visualization. Structured extraction from collaborative text and SPARQL-accessible lexical data supports database and semantic-web applications.

Recent trends emphasize Google Scholar’s broad coverage, open and repository-based dissemination, multilingual and densely annotated datasets, user-centered ranking, and intelligent topic selection to reduce the cost of IR evaluation.

3f58d4d345f48924f35c137d590d2582ca608208.text:
## Principles and Systems for Scalable Data Management

This community spans database theory and practical systems for large-scale analytics. Core themes include query optimization and evaluation—join ordering via MILP, cardinality estimation with deep neural networks, worst-case-optimal and single-round parallel joins, inequalities, provisioning, sampling, and dynamic query answering. Distributed data management is also prominent, covering coordination-free computation, communication complexity, MapReduce optimization, replicated-database index tuning, and cloud security and privacy.

A second major theme is high-performance execution: multicore OLTP under contention, predictive transaction placement, parallel recovery, MVCC conflict repair, batching data-intensive queries, and high-level relational engines for graphs and analytics. Reliability and freshness appear through quorum staleness bounds, stale materialized-view cleaning, and dataset version control.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and correctness analyses with specialized data structures, sketches, sparse tensors, column-oriented execution, parallel algorithms, and optimization solvers. Several systems integrate machine learning directly into data management, including learned cardinalities, relational model training, gradient descent over joins, automated model selection, resource allocation, and revenue-aware recommendation.

Recent directions emphasize declarative, integrated, and adaptive tooling: learned and predictive optimization, interactive insight discovery, collaborative data science, semi-automated data-structure design, approximate analytics, and exploiting application semantics for scalable execution and recovery.

237018f840aa57b999e2a5e1ff219ee1d9ff9196.text:
## Bibliometrics, Scholarly Networks, and Enhanced Information Retrieval

This community studies how scholarly information can be identified, organized, ranked, visualized, and retrieved. A major theme is author-name disambiguation, addressing homonyms and incomplete identities through collaboration patterns, network topology, initials-based baselines, semi-supervised learning, and validated “seed+expand” workflows. Evaluation of digital-library data and assessor reliability is also prominent.

A second theme is network-based measurement of scientific influence. Studies apply PageRank and weighted variants to co-citation, author-citation, patent, and author–paper networks, distinguishing popularity from prestige and examining damping factors, brokerage, closure, and emergent technology clusters. Community detection, stochastic block models, and temporal prediction extend these analyses toward technology growth and researcher development.

Information retrieval research incorporates bibliometric signals, discipline-specific query expansion, Bradfordizing, citation-based recommendation, metadata enrichment through Linked Data, and knowledge maps. Visualization and social collaboration are presented as ways to navigate expanding digital collections and interdisciplinary domains.

Methods typically combine bibliometric analysis, social-network statistics, graph algorithms, machine learning, empirical evaluation, and qualitative studies of infrastructure and data practices. Recent directions emphasize dynamic prediction, interactive and visual scholarly systems, semantic-web vocabularies, reproducible computational workflows using Jupyter, and stewardship of open and “grey” data while protecting privacy and academic freedom.

692f066607c6adca552ef5296b921c95d3c63dc9.text:
### Scholarly Knowledge Extraction and Recommendation

This community focuses on making scientific literature machine-readable, searchable, and easier to navigate. A major theme is semantic publishing: extracting metadata, document structure, citations, author contributions, and quality indicators, then publishing and interlinking these data as Linked Open Data or knowledge graphs. Citation matching and reference parsing are examined at scale, including comparisons of rules, regular expressions, and machine-learning tools.

A second strong theme is research-paper recommendation. Studies address recommender-system design, user modeling, repository integration, and deployment through Mr. DLib’s Recommendations-as-a-Service API and the CORE Recommender. Large operational resources such as the 94-million-record RARD II dataset support evaluation and reuse. Research also investigates practical concerns including choice overload, position bias, reproducibility, noisy data, and the need to evaluate effectiveness over time rather than through single aggregate metrics.

Typical methods combine hybrid information extraction, supervised learning, bibliographic and network features, Hadoop/MapReduce processing, automated crawling, and knowledge-graph construction. Empirical work uses large scholarly corpora, real-world recommendation logs, parser comparisons, and ranking correlations.

Recent directions emphasize production-scale infrastructure, continuously updated scholarly knowledge graphs, richer semantic datasets, deployable recommendation services, and more nuanced evaluation of ranking behavior and user interaction.

569b1daced39f62596221ab27d8738d316893856.text:
### Social Graphs, Recommendations, and Streaming Intelligence

This community studies how social, behavioral, spatial, and temporal data can support recommendation, discovery, and analysis. A central theme is social recommendation: systems combine ratings, tags, friendships, marketplace interactions, location, and cross-platform behavior to improve product, resource, job, venue, and pinboard recommendations. Several works address the long tail, novelty, diversity, coverage, and the effects of social influence on consumer choice.

A second theme concerns social-media mining for public-interest intelligence, including identifying gang members, tracking drug dealing and reactions, measuring attitudes toward China, and studying public-health behaviors. Community and rumor dynamics are examined through network structure, identity, cohesion, trust, and agent-based models.

Typical methods include collaborative filtering and re-ranking, topic modeling and multilabel classification, semantic and word embeddings, multimodal image-text analysis, kernel density estimation, network/link analysis, graph closures, and cognitive models of frequency, recency, forgetting, and semantic context. Streaming work develops sliding-window similarity joins, time-sensitive search, and bounded-memory locality-sensitive hashing.

Recent trends emphasize neural embeddings, multimodal and spatio-temporal representations, cross-platform data integration, scalable services, and recommendation objectives beyond accuracy—especially novelty, diversity, coverage, and semantic user acceptance.

c2b0007d10966ece90ecb6124693d9d52e82ac9f.text:
## Network Science for Ranking, Information, and Social Systems

This community studies large, directed and evolving networks, with particular emphasis on information flow, centrality, and structure. A major theme is Google-matrix analysis: PageRank, CheiRank, two-dimensional ranking, spectra, eigenvectors, reduced Google matrices, and localization are applied to Wikipedia, Twitter, web sites, integers, dynamical systems, and geopolitical relations. Researchers also examine the mathematical reliability of centrality measures, including stability, continuity, discriminating power, and personalized or seeded PageRank.

Wikipedia is a central empirical platform for studying cultural exchange, historical worldviews, geopolitics, social norms, collaboration, conflict, gender inequalities, and breaking-news dynamics. Related work analyzes Twitter diffusion, political communication, and crowd behavior. Other strands address graphons and generative network models, sampling biases, community structure, software and urban street networks, and knowledge structures in multidisciplinary research.

Typical methods combine network construction from hyperlinks, edits, citations, retweets, or geospatial data with spectral decomposition, random walks, centrality measures, temporal analysis, null models, statistical comparisons, and visualization. Text-focused studies use extractive summarization, lexical or semantic graphs, sentiment features, WordNet, and Wikipedia knowledge.

Recent directions emphasize scalable estimation and localization, longitudinal and real-time analysis, multilingual and cross-cultural comparison, social sensing, and applying network methods to policy, urban form, gender, and emerging research fields.

f4e74f84c99912423d0a3d2ce592b7f1f1bbe53d.text:
## Complex Event Processing for Real-Time Streams

This community centers on **complex event processing (CEP)**: detecting meaningful patterns by correlating heterogeneous, high-volume event streams from sources such as RFID, sensors, and IoT devices. Key themes include scalable stream querying, real-time monitoring, event-to-information transformation, and integration with asynchronous messaging and data-stream systems.

Typical methods represent pattern detection with **non-deterministic finite automata (NFAs)**, including more efficient lazy chain automata. CEP systems also use evaluation-structure adaptation to respond to changing stream statistics, and apply join-query optimization because pattern detection resembles multi-join execution. Other work addresses graceful degradation through CEP-specific load shedding, as well as distributed inference and query processing for reconstructing containment and location information missing from raw RFID data.

A parallel foundational trend seeks a principled theory and common processing model for CEP, streaming, event processing, and publish/subscribe technologies, including explicit consideration of consistency over time. Applications increasingly motivate distributed architectures capable of processing massive physical-world data streams, while recent research emphasizes adaptability, efficiency under resource constraints, scalable inference, and stronger conceptual foundations.

bfa7f879d4a43301aeaa7420130f2e4382fc11b5.text:
## Structural Balance in Signed Networks

This community studies structural balance in signed networks, where positive and negative relations encode friendship/enmity, agreement/disagreement, or similar ties. Core themes include measuring partial balance, evaluating balance through simple cycles, and quantifying a network’s distance from complete balance using the frustration index or line index of balance. Applications span social networks, political science, physics, chemistry, biology, and European Parliament voting data.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic analysis with optimization. Researchers formulate exact frustration- and line-index computations as quadratic or linear binary/integer programming problems, often solved with Gurobi, while addressing their relationship to NP-hard problems such as MAXCUT. Cycle-based definitions provide an alternative perspective. Empirical work constructs weighted signed voting networks, compares community-detection algorithms, and uses Parallel Iterative Local Search; other studies develop balance-based measures, models, and link-prediction algorithms.

A recent trend is the movement from classical theory—focused on complete balance and balanced cycles—toward practical measures of partial balance and scalable, exact computation. Studies also increasingly test whether negative links provide meaningful information for graph partitioning and apply balance concepts to real-world networks rather than treating them solely as abstract graph properties.

dd6a9b7efe05413b6aa9c4cbbc9a6d4b91a6d88a.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Contagion

This community studies how information, products, diseases, failures, and tasks propagate through social, technological, biological, and cyber-physical networks. Major themes include influence maximization and advertising, epidemic modeling and containment, diffusion-source localization, hidden-network and parameter recovery, and diffusion-aware signal or trajectory analysis.

Typical models include independent-cascade, SI/SIS, threshold, complex-contagion, continuous-time Markov, temporal, adaptive, and competing-product processes. Methods range from Jordan-center and covering algorithms for locating one or multiple sources, to message passing and factor graphs for cascading failures and self-healing. Network design and intervention are addressed through greedy and adaptive-submodular policies, community-based heuristics, random walks, mixed-integer programming, and stochastic optimization. Random matrix theory quantifies epidemic costs, while particle-swarm optimization estimates edge-infection probabilities. Diffusion and superposition distances compare network-supported signals.

Recent directions emphasize partial observations, limited probing, and aggregate cascade data; recovery of hidden structures with sample-complexity guarantees; and nonstationary settings with temporal or adaptive networks. Influence optimization is becoming more realistic through myopic feedback, continuous time, online activity, adoption and revenue objectives, and resource-constrained worker recruitment. Learning-based approaches also appear, including contrastive training of cascade models and latent social modeling for popularity prediction.

76509e9d2be5c76a3199bf11cba01f18443ab272.text:
### Topic Models, Social Media Analytics, and Intelligent Retrieval

This community centers on extracting structure, meaning, and actionable knowledge from large, evolving collections of text and social-media data. A major theme is topic modeling: latent Dirichlet allocation and extensions address hypertext links, temporal topic evolution, multi-grain review aspects, scientific-article bundling, event visualization, and creative cross-domain discovery. Dynamic and scalable variants model changing topic birth, death, popularity, and distribution, while clustering, summarization, and data decomposition improve large-scale learning.

Another strong theme is social-media intelligence. Studies detect and summarize real-world events from Twitter, geo-tagged streams, and scheduled-event streams; infer interests, sentiment, trust, misinformation, revisits, and popularity; and apply analytics to tourism, libraries, public health, and environmental early warning. Typical methods include statistical time-series and power-law analysis, neural networks and character embeddings, ontology similarity with fuzzy logic, information extraction, ranking, and visualization.

The community also develops recommendation and scholarly-information services, including next-song and video recommendation, content-based microblog ranking, recommender-as-a-service, algorithm selection, hypothesis generation, citation analysis, author-contribution extraction, and semantic publishing. Recent trends emphasize real-time processing, scalable and dynamic models, neural representations, automated validation, and integrating extracted knowledge into decision-support systems.

f2a757fd07f000353abf21031f3136d3ebafc074.text:
### Scientometrics, Research Evaluation, and Knowledge Mapping

This community focuses on measuring and visualizing scientific and technological activity. Major themes include field-normalized impact assessment; evaluation of authors, journals, universities, countries, and R&D programs; and critiques of indicators such as the h-index, impact factor, SNIP, percentiles, and I3. Researchers also study citation-network structure, institutional and journal relationships, cognitive distance, research fronts, collaboration, and the historical roots of fields.

Typical methods involve large-scale Web of Science and Scopus data, comparisons with Microsoft Academic and Dimensions, citation and co-citation networks, bibliographic coupling, centrality measures (including PageRank and K-index), percentile classes, fractional counting, diversity indices, and statistical or benchmark-based comparisons. Network maps, overlays, clustering, MeSH-linked representations, and Reference Publication Year Spectroscopy (RPYS) support visualization and historiography.

Recent directions emphasize validating databases and metrics, correcting normalization and counting procedures, and assessing fairness in multi-authored or large-collaboration research. Studies increasingly examine disciplinary, national, ethnic, gender, and affiliation diversity, while questioning simplistic rankings and the use of statistical inference. Digital dissemination is also linked to a weakening relationship between journal impact factors and individual paper citations.

c2646bcb96efe141026bc026d2ed33f1ed6053c1.text:
## Community Structure in Complex and Social Networks

This community centers on detecting, evaluating, and interpreting cohesive structure in complex networks. Major themes include disjoint, overlapping, fuzzy, attributed, uncertain, multilayer/multiplex, and dynamic communities, alongside related core–periphery structure, bridges, cores, and influential nodes. Applications span social and wireless networks, web services, bibliometric science mapping, online dating, smartphone adoption, risky behavior, and geo-social groups.

Typical methods include modularity optimization (including multislice and adaptive signed-weight variants), label propagation, density-based clustering with manifold learning, clique percolation, local spectral clustering, personalized PageRank diffusion, and locally biased dynamical processes. Probabilistic approaches use generative models, maximum likelihood, variational Bayes, and conditional latent trees. Evaluation increasingly treats quality as multidimensional, using multiple criteria, Pareto optimality, conductance, spectral analysis, and algorithm-selection models rather than relying solely on modularity. Theoretical work studies detectability thresholds, metastability, localization, and neighborhood communities.

Recent trends emphasize scalable local methods for very large graphs, stable and online analysis of evolving networks, joint modeling of multiple edge types and node attributes, explicit treatment of uncertainty and shared/private communities, and richer structural interpretations involving peer influence, global bridges, and core–periphery organization.

506c7b4d75860f61dad11f0a380f400ba61c6054.text:
## Online Social Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Risk

This community studies how online social networks form, evolve, and shape the diffusion of information, opinions, products, and harmful content. Major themes include cascade structure and virality; meme and video popularity; influence, campaigning, and intervention; community structure and weak/strong ties; anomaly, malicious-URL, and systemic-risk detection; privacy exposure; and prediction of user attributes, engagement, and behavior. Applications span Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Yelp, scholarly citation networks, financial guarantees, online games, and criminal networks.

Typical methods combine graph analysis—centrality, pair-dependency, modularity, community detection, structural balance, vulnerability indices, and diffusion models—with large-scale empirical datasets. Machine-learning approaches include embeddings, multitask prediction, unsupervised signed-network induction, trend prediction, latent-topic and visual-meme extraction, and sociologically informed predictive analytics. Temporal behavior is modeled using rumor and cascade processes, popularity-growth models, multivariate Hawkes processes, and dynamic network analysis. Visual analytics supports financial-risk monitoring, while privacy studies use measurement and controlled interface evaluation.

Recent directions emphasize multimodal and semantic signals, latent or indirect interactions, exogenous forces such as mass media and incentives, early prediction of engagement and popularity, real-time event sensing, and optimization of influence or campaigning. Research also increasingly examines network heterogeneity, turnover, content-agnostic effects, and the societal risks of platform-mediated diffusion.

8cc51cde396b43d5c0b3b3f8790afb05da10f319.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Metrics, and Research Discovery

This community studies how scholarly impact can be measured, predicted, and operationalized across articles, books, journals, publishers, researchers, and institutions. Major themes include validation of altmetrics and their relationship to peer-assessed quality; comparisons of Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and specialized databases; and the use of downloads, readership, social-media activity, web links, library loans, and online reviews as complements to citations. Open access, arXiv dissemination, and early visibility are examined as potential influences on citation impact.

Typical methods combine large-scale bibliographic and platform data with correlation, regression, factor analysis, longitudinal analysis, and statistical modeling. Network and webometric analysis map science parks, social-platform links, and scholarly structures, while visualization and co-readership reveal research domains. Machine learning, affinity modeling, and integer programming support venue recommendation, conference classification, and paper–reviewer assignment. Ranking and benchmarking studies develop indicators for journals, books, publishers, and research units.

Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous data quality and source dependencies, broader assessment of societal impact, and richer book and publisher metrics. The literature also reflects growing reliance on academic social networks, digital-library usage logs, online reviews, and automated bibliographic processing, alongside continuing scrutiny of metric validity, bias, and interpretation.

ff03138ebb3778ac701870c0e5a22a6c0bf3ccf1.text:
### Semantic Text Mining and Mathematical Information Retrieval

This community centers on organizing, classifying, and searching textual and mathematical content. Text-mining themes include unsupervised clustering, automated categorization, authorship and opinion-spam detection, topical diversity, thematic analysis, imbalanced corpora, and quality-aware subject indexing. Mathematical information retrieval (MIR) focuses on formula representation, identifier semantics, semantic enrichment, and combined text–formula search, supported by digital repositories and web interfaces.

Typical methods include multinomial mixture and topic models; k-nearest-neighbor, k-medoids, association-rule, and term-class relevance classifiers; feature selection using genetic optimization; syntactic dependency pruning, hyperonymization, WordNet and ontological expansion; and semantic or vector-space representations. Graph propagation supports image classification, while hypergraphs and tree-edit distance support structural similarity. For mathematics, systems use LaTeX, MathML, canonicalization, presentation- and content-based representations, Lucene indexing, query-result merging, and pattern-based or probabilistic identifier-definition extraction.

Recent trends emphasize semantic rather than purely lexical retrieval: enriching formulas with meaning, exploiting ontologies and related concepts, and integrating keywords with mathematical expressions. Work also moves toward scalable, open digital infrastructures—including DRMF, MIaS, WebMIaS, MathSearch, and Mathoid—alongside adaptive interfaces, web-scale scientific crawling, robust evaluation, and document-level confidence or quality estimation.

aedefde9b809a097cbd358e4609ff017aa4702b8.text:
## Multiplex Social Networks and Dynamic Community Analysis

This community centers on modeling and analyzing complex social and information networks, especially multiplex or multilayer systems where users share several kinds of ties across online and offline platforms. Major themes include multilayer centrality, community detection and evolution, identity linkage, homophily, missing data, sampling, and layer entanglement. Applications span recommendations, human resources, marketing, misinformation, sentiment and topic analysis, disease containment, and information cascades.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic measures—degree, reciprocity, clustering coefficients, modularity, PageRank, and similarity indices—with community algorithms such as GED, SGCI, Louvain, Infomap, and stochastic block models. Dynamic settings are addressed through incremental clustering, evolving teleportation, historical group-evolution chains, and epidemic or branching-process models. Other work uses association-rule mining, topic modeling, distant supervision, feature engineering, negative sampling, and language models. Experiments commonly rely on Twitter, Facebook, blogs, email, Wikipedia, browse logs, mobile-phone data, and synthetic networks.

Recent trends emphasize unified multilayer models, cross-platform identity and privacy risks, scalable synthetic-data generation, robust sampling under missing observations, and prediction or control of diffusion, epidemics, and community evolution.

77da584abd9e40eb553cb2f3d9ecb435f48bf163.text:
### Social Media Networks, Misinformation, and Online Influence

This community studies how social-media networks shape political opinions, public discourse, and information diffusion. Major themes include political community detection and polarization; voter-preference and election prediction; misinformation, conspiracy narratives, fake news, and disinformation campaigns; extremist and bot activity; and security threats such as Sybil devices, malicious applications, and organizational profiling. Several works also examine demographic inequalities, online conflict, health interventions, and social-media applications in disaster and environmental monitoring.

Typical methods combine network analysis with machine learning and statistical modeling. Nonnegative matrix factorization, community detection, homophily and segregation models, and propagation analysis identify groups and information flows. Researchers use sparse learning, supervised and semi-supervised classifiers, latent Dirichlet allocation, negative-binomial regression, and metadata, linguistic, temporal, and interaction features to infer preferences or detect spam, bots, autogenerated content, and extremist users. Surveys, credibility studies, and manually annotated datasets complement computational approaches.

Recent directions emphasize cross-platform analysis, election-related disinformation, echo chambers, narrative and emotional dynamics, real-time detection, and intervention. Rather than merely classifying content, newer work evaluates ranking bias, fact-checking and crowd signals, targeted health messaging, spreading strategies, and the practical security consequences of coordinated or automated activity.

0d0e4b8572a922ac88513895288194369ec20c98.text:
### Reliable Data Management Under Uncertainty

This community studies how to make data integration, querying, and analytics reliable despite uncertainty, inconsistency, conflicting sources, and incomplete information. Major themes include probabilistic databases and uncertain relations; data fusion and entity resolution; integrity constraints, repairs, and access-control consistency; and explanations through causality, provenance, and debugging. Query answering under peer-to-peer exchange constraints, conceptual dependencies, and inconsistent databases is another recurring concern.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with practical database algorithms. Probabilistic work uses safe query plans, knowledge compilation, decomposition trees, correlation-aware models, and approximate lifted inference. Integration systems employ blocking, locality-sensitive hashing, similarity ranking, record linkage, and learned representations, increasingly combining automated processing with human judgments. Constraint-oriented research uses chase procedures, answer-set programs, active repairs, and dependency discovery. Provenance and causality are captured through lineage, Datalog rewriting, and responsibility measures.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and quality-aware automation: deep-learning-based entity resolution, human–machine and crowd-based quality control, fault-tolerant fusion, and billion-scale vector indexing. Research also increasingly models richer dependencies and beliefs, supports aggregates and top-\(k\) queries over probabilistic data, and provides approximate answers or explanations when exact computation is intractable.

890372e2d18125baf357737f0ccb43db7ec56bc5.text:
## Geospatial Social Media and Urban Intelligence

This community studies how location-aware and user-generated data can reveal human behavior, urban structure, and place perception. Major themes include geolocation inference from tweets and Reddit without reliable geotags; mobility, commuting, visited locations, colocation, and urban-boundary detection; and reconstruction of spatial, tourist, and contact networks. Other work applies social data to disaster response, emergency-aid retrieval, collective action detection, business-site selection, special offers, and review-based reputation.

Urban experience is treated broadly: studies map smell and sound, identify beautiful, quiet, or happy routes, and measure improved affect near parks. Food imagery, profile changes, event scheduling, and gender or influence inference examine online behavior and identity.

Typical methods combine large-scale geo-tagged social media, check-ins, photos, reviews, and mobile records with convolutional and other deep neural models, Gaussian mixtures, heuristic labeling, sentiment and semantic analysis, low-rank approximation, graph features, clustering, and spatial-textual retrieval. Several works emphasize scalable stream processing, probabilistic confidence, and network-aware modeling.

Recent directions favor multimodal disaster datasets, content-based geolocation with calibrated uncertainty, bias correction and independent validation, continuous detection of spatial bursts, and richer representations of qualitative urban environments and collective behavior.

62ed4da6d0aab1fe1098690ac2544fe335c53172.text:
## Recommender Systems: Personalization, Robustness, and Diversity

This community centers on modeling user–item preferences across collaborative, content-based, social, and contextual recommendation settings. Core themes include long- and short-term sequential behavior, session and playlist continuation, news and travel recommendation, education, advertising, and local events. Persistent challenges are sparsity, cold start, popularity and filter bias, long-tail discovery, noisy or fraudulent feedback, interpretability, and changing user interests.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, neighborhood models, Slope One predictors, co-clustering, signed bipartite graphs, ontologies, and hybrid content–collaborative systems to latent semantic analysis and multimodal representations using text, audio, images, and visual features. Neural approaches increasingly model nonlinear interactions with autoencoders, recurrent networks, factorization machines, DeepFM, joint collaborative filtering, and mixture-of-tastes models. Context trees and inter-session models extend personalization beyond a single session.

Recent work emphasizes robust and flexible systems: learning with missing modalities and cold-start users or items, integrating heterogeneous item relationships, and improving long-tail exposure through personalized reranking and diversity-aware determinantal point processes. Reinforcement learning is applied to online advertising while accounting for user experience. Evaluation increasingly includes real-world experiments, behavioral analysis, attack impact, and scalable, interpretable deployment.

710bc54288fada0911fbc9fefc9f37b20d556f88.text:
### Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Semantic Search, and Interactive Systems

This community centers on improving search relevance, efficiency, and user interaction across web, enterprise, mobile, bibliographic, e-commerce, dataset, and question-answering settings. Major themes include learning-to-rank and multi-stage retrieval; query understanding through expansion, clustering, intent-term selection, entity decomposition, and app targeting; and specialized retrieval such as expert finding, non-factoid passage QA, personal-memory QA, and dataset search.

Typical methods combine supervised ranking, pairwise or pointwise classification, relevance feedback, ensemble and bipartite ranking, support vector machines, kernels, and graph-based models. Neural approaches increasingly use word and query embeddings, convolutional networks, semantic hashing, entity-aware representations, and pretrained BERT architectures for reranking and entailment. Distributed or binary signatures, hashing, and sketching address large-scale similarity and time-series search.

The papers also emphasize operational concerns: spam and content-quality detection, high-recall technology-assisted review, dynamic multi-stage utility, online evaluation with theoretical guarantees, and post-hoc or local-model interpretability. Entity salience, temporal aspects, news processing, and web-assisted data imputation extend retrieval toward knowledge-rich applications. Recent work trends toward pretrained deep models, end-to-end or multi-task learning, conversational and assistant-mediated search, richer answer retrieval, and more transparent, interactive, and latency-aware systems.

4185a093b9ccc3910c7482db8fc6823d38922e82.text:
### Network Intelligence in Dynamic and Heterogeneous Graphs

This community studies methods for representing, modeling, searching, and mining complex networks, especially social, temporal, heterogeneous, and knowledge graphs. Major themes include network representation learning and embedding evaluation; link and relationship prediction; community detection, clustering, and dense-subgraph discovery; graph similarity search; and structural analysis of networks and motifs.

Temporal structure is increasingly central, with temporal event graphs, dynamic stochastic blockmodels, latent-space generative models, continuous-time prediction, and temporally robust embeddings addressing evolving nodes and edges. Heterogeneous and multi-relational methods incorporate types, metapaths, content, predicate paths, and higher-order structures such as triangles and parallelograms. Knowledge-oriented work applies embeddings and ensemble scoring to entity normalization, triple ranking, and fact checking.

Typical methods combine random walks and Markov chains, probabilistic and generative models, stochastic blockmodels, neural networks, deep embeddings, random forests, min-cut algorithms, MapReduce, and external-memory distributed computation. Sampling quality, bias, scalability, and approximation are recurring concerns.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic and continuous-time modeling, cross-modal urban and text mining, privacy and fraud attribution, anomaly detection, covert-network analysis, and principled benchmarking. Theory remains active through analyses of clustering thresholds, locality, convexity, centrality hardness, and link-formation mechanisms.

31fa06d23f0824b993a3d84f04d04690cf5424d6.text:
### Data-Centric Search, Analytics, and Responsible Recommendation

This community spans database systems, information retrieval, large-scale analytics, and social recommendation. Core research addresses flexible querying of uncertain or incomplete data, including fuzzy relational models, linguistic summaries, skyline queries, aggregate joins, multidimensional “diamond dice,” and concise object summaries. Search-oriented work studies hidden-database crawling, third-party query reranking, collaborative and group search, graph-pattern retrieval, and efficient set intersection.

Typical methods combine specialized indexes and encodings—bitmap and spatial indexes, compressed inverted lists, variable-byte and Huffman coding, hashing, locality-sensitive hashing, and low-overhead structures such as Hippo—with algorithmic optimization for top-k, threshold, skyline, and anytime queries. Systems research emphasizes data-intensive scientific workloads, distributed data management, query batching, relational backends, and CPU/GPU acceleration.

A substantial social-computing strand analyzes collaborative tagging, vocabulary growth, heterogeneity, product design, and tag recommendation using power-law models, association rules, and behavioral analysis. More recent work increasingly foregrounds responsible ranking and recommendation: fairness-aware reranking, demographic representations, bias measurement, polarization reduction through antidote data, and semantic bias in high-stakes classification. Overall, the trajectory moves from principled query and storage efficiency toward scalable, heterogeneous, interactive, and socially accountable data systems.

3a44692bb92eaddcd77af15c91fbe0a99fbe3505.text:
### Data Management for Optimized, Learned, and Distributed Analytics

This community centers on efficient query processing and data management at scale. A major theme is join and query optimization: MILP formulations, memory-aware cost models, cardinality estimation, learned optimizers, index tuning, and provisioning techniques target better plans and reduced execution cost. Approximate and interactive analytics use sampling algebras, maximum-entropy summaries, deep generative models, speculative execution, and attention-oriented systems such as MacroBase.

Parallel and distributed computation is another strong focus, including worst-case-optimal multiway joins, communication-free conjunctive-query evaluation, coordination-free computation, MapReduce security, replication consistency, and distributed OLTP. Transactional research addresses multicore contention, predictive execution, recovery, MVCC conflict repair, and blockchain/database design.

Many papers bridge relational systems with graphs and machine learning. Graph algorithms are expressed through SQL, Datalog, and relational joins, with specialized hardware and column stores supporting graph processing. Other work integrates model training directly over relational data and manages shared ML resources.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and communication analyses with cost models, sketches, sampling, deep learning, declarative languages, and prototype evaluation. Recent directions emphasize learned and high-level query engines, approximate answers, hardware-conscious execution, collaborative data management, and scalable analytics over dynamic, replicated, or heterogeneous data.

2bb75bf0adee98fad12ffcd40e7e95fc508741f1.text:
## Network Influence, Community Detection, and Spatial Social Analysis

This community centers on methods for understanding influence and structure in complex and social networks. One strand develops the PWP framework for indirect influence: studying its stability, ranking nodes and links, and applying it to international trade. Related work uses link rankings and Girvan–Newman-style deconstruction to identify clusters and core–periphery organization.

A major theme is extending modularity to spatial and specialized networks. Distance-aware null models and “spatially-near” modularity incorporate geographic costs, while distance modularity targets geographically dispersed communities. Latent node-centric models address the unknown cost functions governing connections in spatial networks. Bipartite modularity is examined from a computational-complexity perspective.

Another strand focuses on scalable and theoretically grounded optimization. Papers establish NP-hardness for bipartite modularity and study additive approximation algorithms and fundamental approximation limits for modularity maximization.

Applications include modeling the spatial and temporal diffusion of political violence, identifying violent gang members using enriched centrality features and classifiers, and supporting law-enforcement intelligence through ORCA. Viral-marketing work develops fast seed-selection methods with guaranteed network-wide adoption under tipping models.

Recent trends emphasize integrating geography and domain metadata, pairing practical large-network tools with provable guarantees, and translating network structure into operational predictions and interventions.

d9022c29e7991381a118bb2c9e79547cc7ca3a0b.text:
## Network Analysis of Web, Social, and Information Systems

This community studies large-scale networks as models of the Web, Wikipedia, universities, countries, social media, transportation, and collaboration. Major themes include ranking and centrality, information flow, influence, navigability, robustness, and network design. PageRank, CheiRank, two-dimensional ranking, Google matrices, random walks, and eigenvalue analysis are recurring tools for identifying important nodes and characterizing information organization. Researchers also examine centrality stability, discriminating power, localization, and the effects of noise or node removal.

Typical methods combine theoretical analysis, optimization, spectral computation, and experiments on real network snapshots. Wikipedia is a particularly prominent data source for studying geopolitical ties, cultural perspectives, universities, mathematicians, historical leaders, collective behavior, disagreement, and breaking-news detection. Social-media studies model topic-specific behavior, diffusion power, temporal relevance, and political communication. Other work addresses scalable crawling, graphons for massive networks, dynamic random walks, traffic backbones, and delay minimization.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic and temporal networks, multilingual and cross-cultural analysis, influence-aware centrality, robustness and controllable network structure, and algorithms with scalability or approximation guarantees. Text summarization and event detection extend network methods toward information retrieval and real-time web intelligence.

5549516d90469be1c8ba413ec92f28a68d1e9291.text:
## Graph Querying, Semantics, and Scalable Data Integration

This community primarily studies graph-data management, with a strong emphasis on RDF and SPARQL. Major themes include query optimization—especially joins, OPTIONAL/left-outer joins, entailment, preferences, provenance, federated execution, and hybrid keyword–SPARQL search. Work on RDF semantics addresses incomplete information, multiset semantics, relational-to-RDF mappings, and OWL entailment. A parallel stream investigates property-graph systems, Gremlin, graph schemas, interoperability, and incremental view maintenance.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and semantic analysis with algebraic rewrites, Datalog, categorical and equational formalisms, indexing, partition and summary graphs, source selection, query reordering, and runtime or incremental evaluation. Experimental studies use large federations, generated workloads, and graph-specific benchmarks. Path-query research covers reachability, temporal paths, regular and context-free paths, and simple-path complexity.

The community also addresses practical usability and trust: querying by example, provenance and reproducibility, graph visualization/summarization, domain-specific validation, and schema inference for XML and semantic annotations. Recent directions emphasize adaptive optimization under poor cardinality estimates, federated querying across heterogeneous Web and relational sources, replication for availability, translation between RDF and property graphs, and scalable processing of evolving, richly attributed graphs.

fccecd6302c772ceb1598bc579c7bf3ab9715b48.text:
### From Collaborative Knowledge to Personalized Search

This community centers on exploiting collaboratively created knowledge—especially Wikipedia, Wiktionary, categories, and linked-data resources—for information retrieval, natural-language processing, and semantic organization. Major themes include extracting structured databases and thesauri from Wiktionary; multilingual ontology matching; entity linking and disambiguation; query expansion; synonym and related-term search; and using Wikipedia categories and links for ranking, navigation, and knowledge discovery.

A second strong theme is search evaluation and improvement. Studies address learning-to-rank topic selection, deep versus shallow relevance judging, representative query sampling, credibility, search metrics, clickthrough bias, and applications to library catalogs. Professional-network search extends these ideas through personalized expertise and talent retrieval, ideal-candidate search, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, homophily features, and learning-to-rank.

Typical methods combine graph analysis (centrality, HITS, category and social networks), information-content and semantic-similarity metrics, machine learning, crowdsourced judgments, large-scale crawling, and interactive visualization. Work also analyzes influence, location, job hopping, and multilingual editing in online communities.

Recent directions emphasize billion-scale, multilingual datasets; language-agnostic entity linking; cross-platform expert discovery; behavior-aware personalization; unbiased implicit-feedback collection; and integrating social, textual, and knowledge-graph signals into search systems.

a8165eda26f8d88c9f456d71daae847e44d8b6b9.text:
### Scalable Data Management, Event Processing, and Complex Analytics

This community focuses on managing, organizing, and analyzing large-scale, heterogeneous, and continuously changing data. Major themes include XML and complex data warehousing, OLAP, fragmentation, query optimization, and automatic selection of indexes and materialized views. A related stream-processing line addresses complex event processing, real-time event detection, and social-media or IoT data analysis.

Typical methods combine workload-aware data mining with systems design: frequent-itemset mining and query clustering guide index, view, and fragmentation selection; affinity analysis and k-means control XML partitioning; tree-pattern matching supports XML querying; and simulation frameworks evaluate clustering, dynamic access patterns, and database performance. Stream systems use clustering, statistical anomaly detection, finite automata, lazy evaluation, adaptation, and load shedding. Benchmarks and scalable synthetic-data generators support evaluation, while classification research includes large-scale hierarchical learning and deep reinforcement learning.

Recent trends emphasize scalability, real-time processing, and adaptation to evolving workloads and data characteristics. Research increasingly targets complex, multimodal, distributed, and heterogeneous sources, including healthcare, archaeology, Web data, RFID, and social networks. There is also a movement toward lightweight architectures for smaller enterprises, unified event-processing models, and more autonomous database administration.

9eda29ab888684c24cdb4016ce88f772de366340.text:
### Unified High-Performance Data Management

This community investigates scalable systems and formal foundations for integrating heterogeneous data models. A major theme is polystore computing: BigDAWG connects PostgreSQL, Accumulo, SciDB, and other engines, while tensor, associative-array, and LARA formalisms provide shared semantics across relational, key-value, array, matrix, and graph processing. Apache Calcite and SQL++ similarly address query processing and language unification over heterogeneous and semi-structured sources.

A second theme is high-throughput big-data infrastructure. D4M and Accumulo support extreme ingest rates, provenance collection, graph storage, and scientific workloads; SciDB targets massively parallel array and imaging data; Loginson addresses large-scale log collection. Graphulo brings GraphBLAS-style sparse matrix and graph kernels into Accumulo, while BigSparse uses SSD-based external-memory processing for graphs.

Theoretical work establishes expressive power, semantics, and complexity boundaries for relational lattices, MongoDB, visual query languages, web wrappers, XPath, conjunctive queries, and streaming/external-memory computation. Typical methods combine algebraic modeling, formal proofs, complexity dichotomies, system architecture, and cluster benchmarking. Recent trends emphasize server-side graph analytics, Julia-based tooling, optimized federated query planning, formalization of NoSQL and semi-structured languages, and reducing data movement across specialized engines.

c085fce99b419568fa4e817498793a2a3695310f.text:
### Scholarly Information, Networks, and Research Analytics

This community centers on improving the discovery, evaluation, and organization of scholarly information. Major themes include author-name disambiguation, metadata cleaning and record linkage, citation and coauthorship analysis, bibliometric ranking, scientific recommendation, and knowledge mapping. It also addresses digital-library design, research-data access, open science, and the stewardship and durability of scholarly infrastructures.

Typical methods are graph-based: coauthor, citation, author–paper, patent, and collaboration networks are analyzed with PageRank and weighted or recursive variants, community detection, stochastic block models, and network-structure measures such as brokerage and closure. Information-retrieval studies use query expansion, Bradfordizing, relevance-assessment reliability measures, user interaction signals, and discipline-specific search resources. Entity resolution combines string similarity, blocking, collaboration patterns, topological features, Linked Data links, and semi-automatic “seed+expand” workflows. Surveys and visual analytics are used to map research domains and knowledge-organization systems.
