Recent trends emphasize scalable and predictive analytics, including MapReduce implementations, LSTM-based growth prediction, emerging-technology detection, and neural title simplification. The literature also increasingly values reproducibility and richer scholarly ecosystems through Jupyter notebooks, integrated research-data libraries, Semantic Web vocabularies, open-data stewardship, and visualization-supported collaboration.

d47ad3455f9eb2a8acffde6d1c5c309b53f1df8a.text:
### Utility-Aware and Concise Sequential Pattern Mining

This community centers on extending pattern mining beyond frequency toward **utility, economic value, recency, and significance**. Major themes include high-utility itemsets, episodes, and sequential patterns; individualized or item-specific utility thresholds; trend- and recency-aware mining; and utility analytics over uncertain, multi-sequence, and privacy-sensitive data. Applications span retail, recommendation and revenue maximization, IoT, clickstreams, social content, and NLP.

A second strong theme is controlling pattern explosion and redundancy. Work mines closed episodes, non-derivable itemsets, generic association-rule bases, compressed serial episodes, and statistically significant or non-free-rider patterns. Subsequence constraints—including length, gap, span, regular-expression, and hierarchy constraints—are unified to improve expressiveness and usability.

Typical methods include projection-based utility mining, upper-bound pruning, episode closure and partition models, equivalence classes with closed itemsets and minimal generators, Minimum Description Length coding, statistical testing, and constraint-based search. Distributed scalability is addressed through MapReduce algorithms for sequential mining, social matching, and n-gram statistics.

Recent trends emphasize realistic objectives beyond uniform thresholds and raw support: individualized utility, temporal change, uncertainty, privacy preservation, and business revenue. The field increasingly combines richer semantics with concise representations and parallel processing to produce actionable rather than merely frequent patterns.

40ab729c9f715cf087949081ffecc7c3a812d651.text:
## Opinion, Belief, and Influence Dynamics in Social Networks

This community studies how opinions, beliefs, social power, and information evolve in networked populations. Major themes include consensus and disagreement; polarization, structural balance, and signed trust–mistrust relations; biased assimilation, homophily, bounded confidence, and heterogeneous thresholds; and influence over directed, weakly connected, stochastic, or dynamically changing networks. Several works model logically interdependent topics and individual belief systems, while others examine recommender feedback, social learning, data incest, and community identity.

Typical methods combine DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, DeGroot–Friedkin, Bayesian, Markov, and bounded-confidence models with graph-theoretic analysis. Papers derive convergence, stability, harmonic-limit, influence, and polarization conditions using Laplacians, structural balance, stochastic processes, Fokker–Planck analysis, and asymptotic arguments. Network sensing and control are addressed through active estimation, stubborn-agent excitation, selective adjustment of interpersonal weights, and belief-control formulations. Empirical studies mine voting and YouTube data using feature selection, sensitivity analysis, prediction models, and vine copulas.

Recent directions emphasize signed and evolving random networks, nonlinear social biases, multi-topic logic, platform-mediated filtering and recommendation loops, and stochastic effects. The community also increasingly connects rigorous network dynamics with large-scale observational data and practical influence or control problems.

60d5fe9a8cb8f738d9448bc973a34fe59afc2be3.text:
## Privacy-Preserving Data Analysis and Secure Data Sharing

This community centers on releasing and analyzing sensitive data while balancing formal privacy, utility, and practical query performance. Differential privacy is the dominant theme, applied to histograms, sparse and hierarchical data, range and high-dimensional statistical queries, clustering, decision trees, frequent-itemset mining, search logs, recommendations, mobility data, and data cleaning. Typical methods include calibrated noise, wavelet and hierarchical decompositions, matrix mechanisms, workload-specific strategy queries, convex optimization, adaptive/data-aware partitioning, and local differential privacy.

A second theme concerns privacy risks beyond formal noise guarantees: reconstruction, background knowledge, algorithm-aware adversaries, group-based anonymization, membership disclosure, and the utility–privacy tradeoff. Techniques include slicing, set-valued k-anonymity, transparent risk models, surrogate graph elements, provenance views, and randomized release.

Systems research addresses secure querying and data federation through query binning, secure multiparty computation, trusted hardware, encrypted databases, and k-anonymous query processing. Applications increasingly involve graphs, social links, location trajectories, and fair decision-making.

Emerging directions emphasize stronger utility guarantees and automation—near-optimal query strategies, accuracy-aware exploration, private cleaning interfaces, bias-adjusted synthetic mobility data, and privacy-aware recommendation—alongside scrutiny of local DP, sparse-vector variants, and trusted execution environments.

abcf4746de14392fda4d0e1384ac93fda5424179.text:
## Social Media Mining, Networks, and Recommender Systems

This community develops computational methods for extracting knowledge from large, heterogeneous social and document networks. Major themes include public-safety and health surveillance: identifying gang members on Twitter, detecting illicit drug dealing and abuse on Instagram, monitoring drug interactions and adverse reactions, and analyzing health-related images and prescribing biases. Other work measures public attitudes, social identity and cohesion, music sentiment, urban places, and user expertise.

Typical methods combine text mining, sentiment and profile analysis, network analysis, classification, clustering, and statistical comparison. Word and spatio-temporal embeddings support gang-profile identification, user and location modeling, and point-of-interest recommendation. Multimodal analysis integrates Instagram images, tags, and text, while hashtag-based systems connect Twitter, Flickr, and YouTube. Graph-based research examines fuzzy and semi-metric closures, document proximity, protein-interaction networks, and recommendation quality. Retrieval systems use character n-gram language models, suffix trees, and ranking-comparison measures; other approaches include agent-based self-organization and biologically inspired distributed knowledge management.

Recent directions emphasize dense embeddings, contextual and sequential modeling, multimodal social-media evidence, cross-platform integration, and large-scale geotemporal analysis. Applications increasingly target actionable public-health, law-enforcement, urban, and personalized recommendation tasks.

774070f821dd632a8d2b55b0fc17869b7b9f6acb.text:
### Network Diffusion, Influence, and Social Dynamics

This community studies how information, opinions, epidemics, and failures propagate through social, temporal, signed, and interdependent networks. Major themes include influence maximization and worker recruitment; epidemic modeling, containment, economic cost, and external spreading agents; source localization and cascade-based recovery of hidden network structure; and opinion formation under biases, multiple topics, recommendations, and political affiliations. Competing products, complex contagion, and network design extend diffusion beyond standard models.

Typical methods combine probabilistic diffusion models (independent cascade, SIS/SI, threshold, Markovian, and adaptive processes) with graph theory, optimization, and dynamical-systems analysis. Researchers use submodularity and adaptive-greedy guarantees, mixed-integer programming, particle-swarm heuristics, Jordan-center/cover algorithms, message passing, random-matrix theory, spectral and stability analysis, and statistical estimation from partial or aggregate observations. Simulations on synthetic and real-world networks are common.

Recent directions emphasize adaptivity and limited feedback, continuous-time and time-varying networks, arbitrary inter-switching behavior, partial observability, multiple sources, and hidden-structure inference. The community also increasingly addresses resilience and intervention—self-healing cyber-physical systems, epidemic containment, resource-constrained sampling, and manipulating network topology or interpersonal weights—while linking diffusion models to applications such as conservation, education, marketing, and mobile crowdsensing.

3f7ae56072626186296aaf766c4bd2d2f96f66db.text:
## Cognitive and Social Recommender Systems

This community centers on recommender systems that model human cognition and social influence rather than relying solely on behavioral data. A major theme is tag and hashtag recommendation: studies model memory activation, frequency, recency, semantic context, forgetting, and lexical–semantic distinctions using ACT-R and Base-Level Learning. These cognitively inspired methods address sparse folksonomies, improve tag reuse prediction, and examine user acceptance.

A second theme is social recommendation. Research combines marketplace behavior with social-network, trust, and location data; exploits weak ties and regular equivalence; and models heterogeneous influence through characterized social regularization. Applications include products, categories, jobs, resources, e-books, and social commerce. Empirical work investigates how friends, ratings, and seller relationships affect consumer choice, including negative social influence and strong-tie commerce.

Typical methods include collaborative filtering, hybrid and content-based recommenders, matrix-factorization comparisons, graph and triadic analyses, semantic similarity, online user studies, and computational models with convergence analysis for rumor dissemination. TagRec provides an evaluation and development toolkit.

Recent directions emphasize temporal and context-aware recommendation, multi-source social data, scalable service architectures, diversity, novelty, and user acceptance—not accuracy alone. Neural item embeddings and cognitive-inspired hashtag models extend these ideas to job portals and Twitter.

e591a36442399ef16a317d35faa59bd8ab69e9a7.text:
## Scientometrics, Research Evaluation, and Scholarly Networks

This community focuses on measuring, mapping, and evaluating scientific activity at the levels of papers, authors, journals, institutions, countries, and fields. Major themes include citation-based impact assessment; field normalization and percentile indicators; author-level indices; institutional and national rankings; technology and journal network mapping; research-front evolution; and the delineation of emerging or interdisciplinary fields.

Typical methods combine Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, and patent data with citation, co-authorship, bibliographic-coupling, and journal–journal networks. Researchers use centrality measures, PageRank, h-index variants, fractional and positionally weighted counting, similarity-adapted vectors, stochastic and multivariate models, percentile classes, Gini and diversity indices, regression, Granger causality, expert validation, and randomized baselines. Comparative studies assess database coverage, normalization schemes, relatedness measures, and the statistical or conceptual validity of indicators.

Recent work emphasizes more nuanced and responsible evaluation: field- and source-normalized metrics, uncertainty in institutional comparisons, limitations and distortions of national assessment exercises, and the weakening link between journal Impact Factor and article citations in the digital era. Emerging directions include alternative scholarly databases, fine-grained citation contexts, diversity in collaboration, internationality, conference-publication effects, and network-based measures of reputation and social recognition.

31a67fda4158cbb2903971b319a3fd65ffc98d72.text:
## Online Social Networks: Structure, Diffusion, and Risk

This community studies online social networks as dynamic systems of interaction, information exchange, and collective behavior. Major themes include identifying influential brokers and global bridges; detecting anomalies, malicious users, and harmful content; explaining community structure, homophily, weak and strong ties, and network paradoxes; and modeling network growth, decay, vulnerability, and systemic risk.

Information diffusion is central: papers analyze rumors, memes, video remixes, reviews, malicious URLs, and political discourse through cascade structures, affect, attention, virality, and external media influence. Related work predicts popularity, engagement, and trends in user-generated content, while other studies infer demographics, gender, interests, and social influence from relational and transaction data.

Typical methods combine graph centrality and dependency measures, modularity-based and Louvain-style community detection, clustering, embeddings, topic and sentiment models, statistical learning, large-scale measurement, and visual analytics. Dynamic processes are modeled with contagion systems (including probabilistic and delay-based SIR variants), Hawkes processes, diffusion models, and adaptive-network simulations.

Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous and temporal data, beyond-view engagement metrics, early prediction, latent interactions such as remixing and indirect co-location, real-time event sensing, explainable structural indicators, and intervention—shaping activity, controlling viral marketing, and managing financial or online security risks.

1341af0bc1f4349eb7b8a471adbb1ba59fc52019.text:
### Multilayer Social Networks and Online Social Intelligence

This community centers on modeling and analyzing complex social systems in which people, platforms, relationships, and interactions form multiple interconnected layers. Major themes include multiplex centrality and structural measures, layer entanglement, missing-data effects, sampling, and unified representations of online and offline identities. Community detection and evolution are prominent, including group extraction, stable-change identification (SGCI), GED, prediction of future group states, and dynamic clustering.

A second major theme is diffusion: information, opinions, misinformation, diseases, and viral campaigns are studied across social, physical, and multilayer networks. Work uses epidemic and independent-cascade models, branching processes, theoretical threshold and outbreak analysis, mobile-phone proximity and mobility data, and seed-selection strategies. Other applications include recommendations, influential-user discovery, human resources, sentiment and topic analysis, and fact-check retrieval.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic measures, community algorithms such as Louvain and Infomap, association-rule mining, topic modeling, sentiment classification, language models, feature engineering, embeddings, and synthetic-network generation. Datasets include Twitter, Facebook, blogs, email, Web 2.0, cellular records, and cross-platform profiles.

Recent trends emphasize multilayer rather than single-layer analysis, cross-platform identity linkage, dynamic and predictive modeling, scalable sampling and generation, privacy-aware synthetic data, and computational responses to misinformation and epidemics.

efa67df43eddb3f3cbdad1864d65080964e8df1a.text:
## Community Detection and Network Structure

This community centers on defining, detecting, evaluating, and exploiting communities in complex networks. Major themes include the ambiguity of “good” communities, comparison of algorithms, overlapping and fuzzy membership, multilayer and multiplex structure, attributed and uncertain graphs, and temporal network evolution. Core–periphery organization, dense subgraphs, centrality, and influence processes form complementary meso-scale perspectives.

Typical methods include modularity optimization (including multislice and adaptive signed-weight variants), stochastic block and geometric block models, spectral and local clustering, density-based manifold learning, label propagation, clique percolation, and core/k-truss methods. Probabilistic approaches use maximum likelihood and variational Bayes; evaluation increasingly uses multiple criteria, Pareto frontiers, stability, and algorithm-selection models. Personalized PageRank and related diffusion methods support localized community discovery, link prediction, and dynamic importance estimation.

Applications span social, communication, bibliometric, web-service, recommendation, dating, and mobile-phone networks, as well as image segmentation. Recent directions emphasize scalable local algorithms for massive graphs, stable and interpretable detection, simultaneous shared/private communities across layers, incorporation of node and edge attributes or uncertainty, active learning, and methods that track evolving layouts, centrality, influence, and community structure over time.

5f98675b5ab44106292bd961a4ac3b125c080cf3.text:
## Recommender Systems: Sequential, Neural, and Responsible Personalization

This community centers on modeling user preferences and item relationships for personalized recommendation across products, media, news, travel, education, and advertising. Major themes include collaborative filtering and matrix factorization; sequential and session-based recommendation; playlist and news continuation; multimodal and content-based recommendation; and graph-, social-, trust-, and ontology-aware ranking.

Typical methods combine long-term preferences with short-term dynamics using Markov chains, latent-variable models, recurrent networks, and graph neural networks. Neural collaborative filtering, variational autoencoders, factorization machines, metric learning, attention, and nonlinear interaction models address sparse and complex user–item relationships. Content is represented through text, audio, images, subtitles, tags, and ontologies, while hybrid models mitigate cold-start and missing-modality problems. Ranking and re-ranking methods target diversity, long-tail exposure, and top-N quality, including determinantal point processes and personalized diversification.

Recent trends emphasize deep learning for session and sequential recommendation, richer multimodal and cross-domain modeling, mixture-of-tastes representations, and recommendation under shared accounts. The community also increasingly considers robustness and societal or business objectives: shilling attacks, reputation, popularity bias, user experience in advertising, revenue maximization, and the effects of social influence. Real-world evaluations and large-scale challenges complement offline algorithm comparisons.

9fddc72421f86e05dd8191160a8055110ba3d275.text:
## Geospatial Social Media Analytics and Urban Behavior

This community studies how social-media and mobile data reveal human behavior, places, and social processes. Major themes include geolocation inference from Twitter and Reddit, mobility modeling, visited-location semantics, urban boundaries, functional regions, and spatial interactions. Researchers also examine urban perceptions through “smellscapes,” soundscapes, beauty, quietness, happiness, parks, food imagery, and emotional sentiment.

Typical methods combine large-scale data collection from Twitter, Instagram, Flickr, Facebook, Yelp, check-ins, telecommunications, and mobile applications with spatial statistics, network analysis, clustering, low-rank approximation, probabilistic geospatial reasoning, and density-based retrieval. Machine-learning approaches include convolutional and deep neural networks, supervised classification, graph-based recommendation, influence modeling, and interactive learning. Streaming algorithms support burst detection and real-time situational awareness, while multimodal frameworks incorporate text, images, metadata, and geolocation.

Applications span disaster response, emergency-aid retrieval, collective action, sexual-violence tracking, tourism, business-site selection, route recommendation, event scheduling, sports prediction, and review summarization. Recent work trends toward scalable analysis of massive and continuous data, multimodal crisis intelligence, automated inference where geotags are absent, personalized and emotionally aware urban services, and models that capture temporal network dynamics, social influence, and group behavior.

5598f33580a0d258d0fc9332bcb01688bd561b6f.text:
## Social Media Networks, Politics, and Misinformation

This community studies how social-media networks shape political opinion, polarization, misinformation, and collective behavior. Major themes include community detection and ideological segregation; voter-preference and demographic inference; fake-news, spam, bot, and extremist-content detection; computational propaganda and disinformation campaigns; and security threats such as Sybil devices, malicious applications, and socialbots. Several papers examine information verification, fact-checking, conflict, and the curation of online discussions and user lists.

Typical methods combine network analysis with machine learning and statistical modeling. Researchers use nonnegative matrix factorization, PCA, assortativity, graph and propagation features, and community-detection techniques, alongside sparse learning, classifiers, LDA, regression, semi-supervised and real-time detection systems. Studies also use surveys, manually labeled datasets, crowdsourced signals, and cross-platform behavioral traces.

Recent work increasingly focuses on election-related manipulation, polarized political conversations, extremist adoption, and Russia-sponsored or anti-Latinx computational propaganda. It also emphasizes methodological caution: quantifying search and classification bias, including low-connectivity users, evaluating stance metrics, and testing whether propagation features reliably identify misinformation. Alongside diagnosis, the community develops interventions—fact-checking, targeted public-health bots, malicious-node removal, and privacy/security defenses—and explores decentralized search and large-scale comparative studies across platforms.

aa0af788d4ac0a95c89ffd25735b2b51c0e13ace.text:
### Information Retrieval Ranking and Semantic Search

This community centers on improving search and ranking across web, email, e-commerce, mobile apps, datasets, entities, and question answering. Core themes include relevance estimation, query understanding and expansion, semantic similarity, expert and entity retrieval, web quality and spam detection, and efficient similarity search.

Typical methods combine learning-to-rank with deep representation learning. Models use word and query embeddings, concept hierarchies, knowledge-enriched entity representations, kernel interactions, and semantic hashing. Neural rankers include DeepRank, permutation-invariant and groupwise scoring models, multi-task architectures, and BERT-based pointwise or pairwise rerankers. Multi-stage retrieval pipelines are common, balancing ranking quality and latency. Other work applies graph models to bibliographic networks, dependencies, and nearest-neighbor structures; ensemble and bipartite-ranking methods address web quality. Benchmark collections and datasets support evaluation for learning-to-rank, passage retrieval, and dataset search.

Recent trends emphasize pretrained language models, multilingual and zero-shot relevance transfer, non-factoid and personal question answering, and direct optimization of retrieval metrics. Research also increasingly models context: document interactions, query intent, temporal entity aspects, user neighborhoods, and dynamic multi-stage search. Interpretability, axiomatic regularization, large-scale indexing, and web-assisted knowledge integration address reliability, transparency, and efficiency.

e1dbcdbd0a8081f49438326fc03a196b5f05dec5.text:
## Dynamic Networks, Graph Learning, and Reliable Network Mining

This community centers on learning from complex, heterogeneous, and evolving graphs. Major themes include temporal network representation and forecasting, community detection, link prediction, graph similarity, network sampling, and scalable graph processing. Several works model dynamics explicitly through temporal event graphs, continuous-time relationship prediction, dynamic embeddings, dynamic stochastic blockmodels, and latent-space generative models.

Typical methods combine structural signals—motifs, triangles, clustering coefficients, degree correlations, paths, and community structure—with attributes, text, and knowledge-base information. Neural and representation-learning approaches are prominent, including graph embeddings, metapath-guided cross-modal models, deep clustering, and neural inference. Other studies use probabilistic models, Markov chains, random forests, MapReduce, distributed external-memory algorithms, and ensemble scoring. Sampling quality, embedding benchmarks, and bias quantification emphasize reliable evaluation rather than accuracy alone.

Applications span social-network fusion and privacy, fraud and insider-trading detection, criminal and covert networks, fact checking, entity normalization, urban dynamics, and team recommendation. Recent trends favor temporally robust and continuous-time modeling, scalable analysis of massive graphs, integration of multimodal information, and adversarial perspectives—such as hiding from community detection or de-anonymizing fraudsters.

2dfe058bfb84626580a7855528a25912d56b976d.text:
## Graph Data Management, Querying, and Semantics

This community centers on graph data systems, especially RDF, SPARQL, and property graphs. A major theme is efficient query processing: optimization of joins and OPTIONAL patterns, runtime and incremental evaluation, federated querying, replicated-fragment selection, summary- and partition-based indexing, and analytical queries over RDF data cubes. Work also addresses richer query interfaces, including preferences, keyword–SPARQL hybrids, example-based knowledge-graph querying, and translations between SPARQL and Gremlin.

A second theme is formal semantics and interoperability. Papers study incomplete RDF information, OWL entailment, provenance, query containment and subsumption, relational-to-RDF mappings, RDF–property-graph direct mappings, data integration, view updates, and typed property-graph schemas. Formal tools include Datalog, algebraic and categorical formalisms, relational and nested relational algebra, and complexity classification for regular and context-free path queries.

Typical methods combine soundness and completeness proofs, undecidability and complexity analyses, indexing and labeling schemes, query rewriting, source selection, graph summarization, and empirical evaluation on large federations or generated workloads. Complementary work covers temporal reachability, graph databases, provenance visualization, and reproducibility.

Recent directions emphasize interoperability across graph models, scalable and adaptive optimization, trustworthy/provenance-aware querying, schema and type support for flexible graphs, and more accessible interfaces for non-expert users.

48e419dd264a8b0f44c1bae0229d63e29810e43f.text:
## Semantic Preservation and the Temporal Web

This community studies how digital objects, scholarly artifacts, linked data, and Web resources can be represented, preserved, queried, and reused over time. A central theme is semantic and provenance-aware modeling: scientific life cycles, mechanisms, manuscripts, annotations, claims, nanopublications, and heterogeneous digital objects are described through RDF, ontologies, persistent identifiers, versioning, and provenance vocabularies. Repository architectures such as Fedora and aDORe support aggregation, dissemination, rights management, and standards-based archival storage.

A second major focus is Web archiving. Work addresses acquisition and text extraction from mementos, collection curation, temporal search, resource dating, missing and orphaned content, annotation persistence, and longitudinal studies of Web popularity. Typical methods include large-scale log and archive analysis, longitudinal sampling, social-bookmark and social-media signals, focused crawling, caching, machine-learning prediction, and semantic layers queried with SPARQL. Systems such as Memento, ArcLink, Tempas, and Carbon Date operationalize these approaches.

Recent trends emphasize evolving and linked open data, including historical queries and change tracking; scalable RDF corpora such as TweetsKB; richer open annotation and entity-linking infrastructure; and preservation of web-native scholarly objects. The community increasingly integrates social signals, machine learning, formal semantic models, and interoperable standards to improve discoverability, freshness, trust, and long-term accessibility.

abbaf254f8dfeb95c6862066ed39fb448e786bfd.text:
## Search, Ranking, and Structured Web Information

This community centers on improving information access across search engines, recommender systems, libraries, social platforms, and Web databases. Major themes include flexible retrieval over imperfect or hidden data—fuzzy summaries and SQL, incomplete data streams, hidden-database crawling, concise relational object summaries, and workflow search—as well as multi-criteria decision support through skyline, aggregate skyline-join, and influence-set queries.

Ranking is addressed both algorithmically and institutionally. Work examines ranking factors for library materials, third-party query reranking, experiential search, and collaborative search. Increasing attention is given to fairness, polarization, and representation: proposed methods include fairness-aware reranking, diversity-based MMR using demographic representations, and “antidote” data for improving recommender outcomes. Bias is also measured in high-stakes occupation classification.

Typical methods include learning-to-rank, query and result reranking, approximate nearest-neighbor locality-sensitive hashing, graph/link analysis, association rules, fuzzy linguistic summaries, power-law and scaling analysis, and polynomial-time algorithms for structured retrieval. Evaluation research emphasizes efficient topic selection and the deep-versus-shallow judging tradeoff.

The community also mines collaborative tagging and Wikipedia for vocabulary growth, semantic similarity, entity annotations, ontology matching, news discovery, and product insight. Recent directions combine large multilingual resources, behavioral and geospatial streams, practical search services, and socially responsible ranking.

0ab173df38c2cd5e7c4a243558faaffdd25a8233.text:
## Network Analysis of Wikipedia, Social Systems, and Narratives

This community studies large-scale networks as representations of information, people, institutions, and fictional worlds. Wikipedia is a central testbed: papers construct longitudinal, multilingual hyperlink datasets and apply PageRank, CheiRank, reduced Google matrices, spectral analysis, and centrality measures to study cultural differences, geopolitics, universities, mathematicians, information flow, and article-coverage gaps. Related work examines web crawling, Twitter, scientific migration, traffic networks, and open-source collaboration.

A second theme is network structure and optimization. Researchers analyze navigability, communicability, node discovery, backbone extraction, edge modification, centrality discrimination, PageRank maximization, and strategic network formation. Game-theoretic, spectral, random-walk, thermodynamic, and statistical approaches are common.

Narrative analysis represents characters and interactions as static, temporal, signed, or multilayer graphs. These models support genre classification, summarization, role analysis, plot smoothing, and prediction of events such as character deaths. Text-based methods also induce signed relations, lexical chains, and extractive summaries.

Recent directions emphasize temporal and cross-cultural analysis: real-time Wikipedia edit spikes and social-media behavior support breaking-news detection and time-aware ranking; multilingual mining exposes cultural entanglement; and dynamic conversational and collective-state models capture evolving social and narrative processes.

28a4500979c250ca57ab40b8abdd5247dbfdec3c.text:
## Scholarly Information Retrieval and Bibliometric Knowledge Systems

This community studies how scholarly information is organized, searched, linked, evaluated, and visualized. Major themes include interactive and domain-specific information retrieval; knowledge maps and knowledge-organization systems for the Semantic Web; digital libraries integrating publications, datasets, surveys, and related resources; and metadata enrichment through record linking and Linked Data.

A prominent focus is bibliometric analysis of authors, publications, and research communities. Work addresses author-name disambiguation, publication-oeuvre construction, coauthorship and citation structures, prestige versus popularity, and the effects of citation practices. PageRank and weighted variants are repeatedly applied to author, paper, patent, and citation networks, alongside centrality measures, community detection, stochastic block models, and network visualization.

Typical methods combine log and behavioral analysis, relevance-assessment statistics, string similarity and blocking, graph algorithms, recursive ranking, machine learning, PCA, interviews, ethnography, and large-scale bibliographic datasets. Evaluation emphasizes labeled datasets, inter-assessor agreement, simulated identities, and empirical retrieval performance.

Recent trends move toward dynamic and predictive analyses of emerging technologies and scholar development; richer visual and interactive interfaces; semi-automatic metadata and identity resolution; reproducible computational research using Jupyter; and integrated, open research-data infrastructures. These developments also foreground long-term maintenance, privacy, stewardship, and the reliability of scholarly data.

7aca766a097f3e1d948414b8c3f0fe5199e30508.text:
## Learning, Parallelism, and Declarative Data Management

This community studies scalable, principled data management across query processing, analytics, distributed systems, and emerging platforms. Core themes include query optimization and cost estimation (MILP join ordering, memory-aware hashing models, learned cardinalities, neural optimizers, and replica-aware index tuning), as well as parallel query evaluation, communication complexity, coordination, and dynamic query maintenance. Graph processing is repeatedly expressed through relational joins, SQL, or Datalog, with specialized engines and hardware explored for graph pattern matching.

Typical methods combine formal complexity and correctness analyses with systems prototypes and empirical evaluation. Techniques include worst-case-optimal multiway joins, sampling and deep learning, probabilistic summaries and maximum-entropy models for approximate queries, sketches and reservoir sampling for streams, model-based compression, and declarative compilation in high-level languages. The community also addresses recovery, transaction conflicts, consistency, dataset versioning, and blockchain/database relationships.

Recent trends emphasize learned and probabilistic data systems, end-to-end integration of data engineering with machine learning, high-level abstractions without performance loss, and exploiting multicore, parallel, specialized, or relational infrastructure for graph and analytical workloads. Blockchain emulation, cross-chain atomicity, and practical consistency broaden the scope toward decentralized data platforms.

11c6da64f8be5834d42ca7a4ec70bd49bc41a1de.text:
**Scalable Data Management for Scientific and Analytical Workloads**

This community studies efficient management, indexing, querying, and analysis of large multidimensional and scientific datasets. Major themes include OLAP pruning and scalability, spatial indexing and cross-matching, bitmap and inverted-index operations, and database support for astronomy, pathology, finite-element analysis, and language models. Several works address user-facing access through natural-language interfaces, SQL generation, and semantic mapping of keywords and join paths.

Typical methods emphasize compact representations and hardware-conscious execution: bitmap, B-tree, multidimensional, zones, and novel indexing schemes; differential, Huffman, variable-byte, and SIMD-based compression; fast set intersection and hashing; and row or attribute reordering to improve compressed bitmap performance. Systems exploit GPUs, multicore CPUs, SIMD instructions, in-memory execution, and relational backends. Distributed dataflow frameworks support frequent subgraph mining and batch scheduling that maximizes shared data access.

Recent trends move toward petabyte- and exascale scientific infrastructures, full-lifecycle and streaming astronomy services, metadata and provenance management, and high-throughput transactional processing on GPUs. There is also increasing emphasis on reducing index storage and update costs, accelerating compressed data directly, and integrating large-scale databases with accessible natural-language and web-based analytical tools.

65a30a23cb79937ed8c02069d7d4abb3488cda50.text:
**Cognitive and Social Recommendation in Networked Platforms**

This community centers on recommender systems that incorporate human cognition, social relationships, and temporal behavior. A major theme is social tagging: models of memory activation, frequency, recency, semantic context, forgetting, and lexical–semantic processing are used to recommend tags, hashtags, and items. These cognitive-inspired approaches address sparse folksonomies and often outperform popularity-based or conventional collaborative-filtering methods.

A second theme is social recommendation across marketplaces and commerce platforms. Studies exploit friendship, trust, location, messaging, weak ties, triadic closure, and social influence to recommend products, categories, and sellers, while also examining how friends, crowds, and negative opinions affect consumer choices. Trust-based collaborative filtering and characterized social regularization target sparsity and cold-start problems.

Typical methods include user- and item-based collaborative filtering, hybrid models combining metadata and behavioral signals, graph and regular-equivalence techniques, ACT-R/BLL memory equations, semantic similarity, embeddings, deep learning, and pre-filtering for scalability. Evaluations use multi-platform datasets, Mechanical Turk and small user studies, online A/B-style experiments, and metrics beyond accuracy such as click-through rate, diversity, novelty, and acceptance.

Recent work trends toward real-time embedding-based job recommendation, fairer music recommendation, scalable service architectures, and cognitively grounded, context-aware systems validated in operational settings.

c3343d383437c9c93cfb79bf49f0328d64c578bf.text:
## Networked Information Mining and Social Media Analytics

This community explores computational methods for extracting knowledge from interconnected textual, visual, and social data. A major theme is social-media analysis: Twitter is used to measure attitudes toward China, while Instagram images and timelines support public-health monitoring, including drug abuse, drug interactions, adverse reactions, and lifestyle risks. Cross-platform discovery is addressed through hashtag-based search and Pinterest recommendations for Twitter users.

Network science provides a second core theme. Papers study fuzzy-graph and distance closures, semi-metric behavior in co-occurrence and document networks, and the use of non-metric edges for improved recommendation. These ideas are evaluated on benchmarks such as MovieLens and applied to web, bibliographic, and semantic networks.

Typical methods include multimodal learning, automatic image annotation, multilabel classification, clustering, network analysis, agent-based modeling, linear text classifiers, word-proximity networks, and character n-gram indexing with suffix trees. Ranking-comparison measures are also used to assess search-engine stability and similarity.

Recent work trends toward large-scale, heterogeneous, and cross-platform data integration, especially combining social signals with images and health records. The community increasingly emphasizes adaptive, distributed, and biologically inspired systems, while applying network-based inference to public-health surveillance and recommendation.

d60ff982eb265346f0695769baeb68561709019e.text:
**Topic-Centric Mining of Dynamic Web and Scholarly Data**

This community focuses on discovering, organizing, and exploiting latent structure in large, evolving collections of text and social-media data. A major theme is topic modeling: extensions of LDA/PLSA model hyperlinks, temporal topic birth and evolution, multi-grain review aspects, scientific-article bundles, and cross-domain “bisociative” connections. Scalable and parallel dynamic topic models address large data streams, while summarization reduces the cost of topic learning.

A second theme is social-media intelligence, including event detection and retrieval, real-time event summarization, geo-temporal analysis, sentiment and misinformation monitoring, popularity and revisitation dynamics, and inference of user interests. Applications include tourism, public health, libraries, online video, and rare environmental-event prediction. Typical methods combine statistical or neural models, clustering, machine learning, query expansion, network analysis, and visualization.

Scholarly information systems receive sustained attention through semantic publishing, citation and contribution extraction, bibliometrics, hypothesis-generation validation, paper recommendation, and entity/timeline summarization. Linked data, ontologies, fuzzy similarity, and candidate ranking support these tasks.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic, real-time, and geographically sensitive analysis; neural representations such as CNNs and character-based embeddings; scalable processing; and human-centered systems offering explanation-based tuning and recommendation services.

0c8bd598e08f234efabc9985565376a62a01942d.text:
### Multilayer Social Networks, Identity, and Dynamic Diffusion

This community centers on analyzing social systems as multilayer or multiplex networks, where online, offline, semantic, professional, and physical ties interact. Major themes include layer-aware centrality and structural measures; homophily and tie strength; community discovery, evolution, and prediction; cross-platform and cross-device identity linkage; and information, epidemic, and influence diffusion.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic measures (degree, reciprocity, cycles, triplets, clustering, entanglement), community algorithms such as GED, SGCI, Louvain, and Infomap, and probabilistic diffusion models including independent-cascade, branching-process, and epidemic models. Researchers also use topic modeling, sentiment analysis, association-rule mining, language models, feature engineering, negative sampling, and embedding-based matching. Empirical studies rely on Twitter, Facebook, blogs, email, student networks, browse logs, cellular data, and synthetic networks; sampling, missing-data analysis, and privacy-aware data generation address practical limitations.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes dynamic and interconnected settings rather than isolated graphs: predicting group evolution, updating communities efficiently, modeling interacting or multilayer spreading processes, and combining online with offline or physical networks. Identity research is moving toward unsupervised factoid embeddings and cross-platform datasets, while applications expand to misinformation fact-checking, personalized recommendation, disease containment, viral campaigns, human resources, and targeted information diffusion.

cf68f8d3dfb99c2933672dd01f55ba35a1b64618.text:
**Online Social Networks: Structure, Diffusion, and Influence**

This community studies online social networks as dynamic systems for communication, influence, information diffusion, and risk. Major themes include community structure and tie strength; identifying influential nodes, global bridges, intermediaries, and malicious accounts; anomaly, fraud, and harmful-content detection; and the spread and popularity of rumors, memes, videos, reviews, and URLs. Other work examines user attributes, gender, attention, engagement, collective intelligence, social isolation, and network growth or decay.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic analysis—centrality, pair-dependency, modularity, community detection, clustering, vulnerability indices, and structural paradox analysis—with large-scale mining of Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Yelp, and transaction data. Researchers use diffusion and contagion models (SIR variants, delay differential equations, Hawkes processes, viral-marketing models, and indirect co-location graphs), machine learning and embeddings for prediction, topic and sentiment analysis, visual-meme detection, and visual analytics. Surveys distinguish static/dynamic and labelled/unlabelled anomalies.

Recent directions emphasize more realistic, heterogeneous, and dynamic models: incorporating mass media, absent nodes, node-specific contagion and immunity, exogenous incentives, content-agnostic popularity factors, engagement rather than views, and latent interactions such as remixing. Large datasets increasingly support early prediction, real-time event sensing, and applications spanning political discourse, finance, cybersecurity, health, and marketing.

3b7b1c15f1f81711cecded1b5fede67cfed55441.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Metrics, and Digital Research Infrastructure

This community studies how scientific visibility, use, quality, and societal impact can be measured across traditional and emerging platforms. Major themes include the validity and interpretation of altmetrics; comparisons among Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar; citation and readership analysis; open access, arXiv, and web usage effects; and evaluation of books, publishers, journals, institutions, and researchers. Related work examines scholarly communication systems, venue recommendation, conference classification, reviewer matching, editorial-board networks, and science-park link structures.

Typical methods combine large-scale bibliographic, download, loan, social-media, review, and web-link datasets with citation analysis, correlations, regression, longitudinal comparisons, principal-component and factor analysis, and indicator benchmarking. Network analysis is used to map institutional, editorial, and scholarly relationships, while text mining, machine learning, integer programming, and automated record matching support recommendation, peer-review allocation, and bibliographic disambiguation.

Recent trends emphasize expanding evaluation beyond citations toward online attention, readership, downloads, reviews, and societal reach, while testing their reliability, quality, heterogeneity, and dependencies. Google Scholar and publisher/book metrics receive increasing scrutiny; open-access and preprint repositories are analyzed as drivers of early visibility and citation advantage. Research is also moving toward automated, user-adaptive tools for discovery, assessment, and scholarly workflow management.

402130315859c0f78bfd5fb39c5618e8342f21d5.text:
### Reliable Data Integration and Reasoning

This community studies how to make heterogeneous, uncertain, and crowdsourced data trustworthy and useful. Major themes include entity resolution and consolidation, data fusion and conflict resolution, probabilistic databases, integrity constraints and repairs, provenance, causality, and explanation. Applications span Web and enterprise integration, geo-information, spatial crowdsourcing, data markets, and large-scale vector search.

Typical methods combine formal database theory with scalable systems techniques. Researchers develop probabilistic models for correlated or uncertain sources; blocking, hashing, embeddings, and progressive comparison for entity resolution; and human–machine workflows to control precision, recall, worker reliability, and cost. Other work uses answer-set programs, abductive diagnosis, active integrity constraints, and complexity analysis for repairs and causality. Query evaluation relies on knowledge compilation, semirings, decomposition trees, query rewriting, database-native approximation, and specialized indexing or join algorithms. Provenance and performance logs support auditing, debugging, and explanations.

Recent directions emphasize democratizing and scaling data quality: deep-learning-based and schema-agnostic entity resolution, fault-tolerant crowd integration, billion-scale similarity search, and efficient address linkage. Probabilistic inference is moving toward approximate lifted evaluation inside standard database engines, while richer correlation models and probabilistic ranking address realistic uncertainty. Data-market platforms increasingly connect sharing incentives with discoverability and integration.

2bb8c8bffa0f853b3bde88e17c2349759092d747.text:
## Graph Data Management, Querying, and Integration

This community centers on scalable management and analysis of RDF, knowledge graphs, and property graphs. A major theme is SPARQL optimization: join reordering, OPTIONAL/left-outer-join processing, runtime and summary-graph optimization, preference and keyword integration, OWL entailment, OLAP over RDF cubes, and federated querying across heterogeneous or replicated endpoints. Related work addresses RDF incompleteness, relational-to-RDF mappings, RDF–property-graph translation, and interoperability with Gremlin.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with indexes, labels, partition and summary graphs, adaptive storage structures, source selection, query rewriting, and empirical benchmarking. Graph algorithms cover temporal reachability, distance queries on scale-free networks, regular simple paths, opinion spreading, and entity resolution. Systems research includes graph database taxonomies, type systems, schema-driven workload generation, cloud databases, and high-throughput batch processing.

Another strand focuses on trustworthy and usable data infrastructure: provenance visualization and differencing for reproducibility, schema and semantic validation, functorial/algebraic data migration, view updates, and query-by-example interfaces.

Recent trends emphasize large-scale and distributed knowledge graphs, federation reliability through replication, runtime/adaptive optimization, cross-model querying, richer semantics, and making complex graph data accessible to non-expert users.

19fcb891e16f4609530284e996a73c7b7d90eb19.text:
## Flexible, Efficient, and Responsible Data Search

This community spans database systems, information retrieval, and recommender systems. Major themes include flexible querying over fuzzy, incomplete, multidimensional, and streaming data; skyline, aggregate, keyword, workflow, and hidden-database search; and collaborative, experiential, and expert recommendation. Fairness is an emerging concern, addressing demographic bias in ranking, biographies, image representations, polarization, and recommendation diversity.

Typical methods combine formal query models (GEFRED, SQLf, linguistic summaries), skyline and pruning algorithms, re-ranking, association rules, tensor/matrix factorization, and context-free workflow grammars. Systems research emphasizes compact and fast data structures, including bitmap and Roaring indexes, set-intersection algorithms, spatial indexes, locality-sensitive hashing, and low-overhead indexing. Compression methods such as Variable-Byte, difference-Huffman, and SIMD-based encoders target inverted lists and multidimensional data.

A strong systems trend is exploiting modern hardware and distributed infrastructures: GPU/CPU hybrids for pathology analysis, GPU transaction processing, SIMD acceleration, in-memory dataflow systems such as Spark and Flink, and storage-conscious indexing for SSD/NVM environments. Recent work increasingly treats search quality as multidimensional—balancing relevance, diversity, fairness, and user preferences—while also extending analytics to large-scale, heterogeneous, and socially consequential data.

ae02f5466f2e84cf8a3664eabfd3893ec22eb280.text:
## Collaborative Knowledge, Search, and Semantic Networks

This community studies how user-generated and linked data can support information access, knowledge representation, and social computing. A major theme is extracting structured resources from Wikipedia and Wiktionary: parsers transform entries into relational or machine-readable dictionaries, while categories, links, annotations, and multilingual content support ontology matching, entity ranking, synonym discovery, and entity linking. Semantic Web standards such as SKOS and SPARQL provide interoperability mechanisms.

A second theme concerns search and evaluation. Work addresses library ranking and catalog improvement, query expansion, topic selection for inexpensive IR test collections, clickthrough bias correction, and meta-evaluation of search metrics. Typical methods include learning-to-rank, graph centrality and HITS/PageRank-style algorithms, category and hyperlink analysis, matrix factorization, and interactive or large-scale empirical evaluation.

The community also analyzes collective behavior in tagging and online networks. Power-law and allometric models characterize vocabulary growth and heterogeneity; co-occurrence, cosine similarity, clustering, and network centrality reveal emergent semantics and influential nodes. Applied studies forecast locations, map attention flows, identify expertise, and model talent mobility through professional-network data.

Recent directions emphasize multilingual, high-throughput processing of user-generated text, personalized expertise and job search, scalable behavioral analytics, and awareness of presentation, societal, and recommender-system bias.

526b5f0737b094a0540e0efdc389f8d9902a245d.text:
## Community Detection in Complex and Dynamic Networks

This community focuses on defining, detecting, evaluating, and exploiting community structure in complex networks. A major theme is that no single community definition or quality measure is universally adequate: studies examine multi-criteria and Pareto-based evaluation, overlapping and fuzzy modularity, algorithm-selection strategies, and taxonomies of detection methods.

Typical approaches include modularity and multislice modularity optimization, stochastic and geometric block models, spectral and local spectral methods, density-based clustering with manifold learning, label propagation, clique percolation, and variational Bayesian inference. Work also addresses attributed, weighted, signed, uncertain, multiplex, multilayer, and two-mode networks, as well as core–periphery structure.

Dynamic-network research emphasizes visualization with mental-map preservation, evolving PageRank, temporal centrality stability, and prediction of influential nodes. Applications include social influence on churn and smartphone adoption, online dating, recommendations, bibliometric mapping, Web services, and polarization analysis. Theoretical contributions study detectability thresholds, metastable dynamics, graphons, and axiomatic centrality or core–periphery models.

Emerging directions favor scalable, interpretable, and localized analysis for massive graphs; joint treatment of shared and layer-specific communities; principled handling of uncertainty and attributes; active learning; and adversarial community deception for privacy.

333b22d53766770ca16ab544672f9c941a658a85.text:
### Semantic Retrieval, Text Mining, and Mathematical Information Systems

This community centers on organizing and searching heterogeneous digital collections. A major theme is text clustering and categorization, including probabilistic mixture models, topic models, k-nearest-neighbor and k-medoids methods, association rules, term-class relevance, genetic feature selection, and machine-learning approaches for multilingual, authorship, sentiment, spam, and micro-text classification. Feature selection, weighting, pruning, and semantic enrichment are recurring concerns.

A second theme is semantic retrieval. Studies augment keyword and vector-space models with named entities, identifiers, WordNet relations, ontological classes, spreading activation, and wikitology. Evaluation emphasizes precision/recall-oriented measures and query-result merging.

Mathematical information retrieval forms a distinctive subarea. Systems combine textual and formula queries, compare presentation- and content-based representations, canonicalize LaTeX/MathML, analyze mathematical notation and identifier namespaces, and develop repositories, interfaces, and rendering infrastructure. Emerging methods include formula embeddings and TopicEq, which jointly models equations and surrounding text.

A parallel systems strand addresses XML and web-scale data management through path summaries, XPath-aware structural descriptions, indexing, distributed materialized views, and adaptive P2P content redistribution. Recent trends move toward neural representations, deep quality estimation, integrated semantic/formula search, large scientific corpora, and practical open digital-library platforms.

aec533ed5faa4d4e3de23d41de4cc3255697a801.text:
## Network Analysis, Representation, and Prediction

This community studies methods for extracting structure, semantics, and dynamics from complex, social, temporal, and knowledge networks. Major themes include link and relationship prediction, graph similarity, community detection, anomaly and fraud detection, sampling bias, privacy, and analysis of covert or criminal networks. Knowledge-graph applications cover triple scoring, entity normalization, and path-based fact checking.

Typical methods combine local structural signals—common neighbors, triangles, clustering coefficients, reliable routes, and predicate paths—with probabilistic models, random walks, Markov chains, graph grammars, and scalable MapReduce algorithms. Machine learning is prominent: random forests, neural networks, latent-space models, deep and dynamic graph embeddings, and ensemble systems integrate topology with node attributes, text, and external knowledge bases. Diffusion-based distances and structural graph classifiers provide additional ways to compare signals and identify network domains.

Recent trends emphasize temporal and continuous-time modeling, including temporal event graphs, dynamic embeddings, and generative models with evolving communities. Research increasingly targets heterogeneous and multimodal networks, urban dynamics, cross-network fusion, and unseen entities. There is also growing attention to evaluation quality, statistical guarantees for sampling, robustness to temporal change, business-oriented fraud metrics, privacy prediction, and adversarial behavior in hidden networks.

0e6553f04ed2f8621d43b93414f02d907448b132.text:
### Social Media Networks, Polarization, and Misinformation

This community studies how social platforms shape political opinion, information diffusion, and online safety. Major themes include community structure and polarization; misinformation, fake news, rumors, and disinformation; political persuasion and computational propaganda; and detection of malicious users, bots, spam, extremist content, and Sybil devices. Several works examine political events including U.S. elections, Charlottesville, ISIS support, Italian European elections, and Russia-sponsored campaigns, while others address health interventions, disasters, and crowdsourced mapping.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Facebook, Gab, and search-log datasets with network analysis, retweet and followership graphs, temporal analysis, and diffusion or propagation modeling. Machine-learning approaches include nonnegative and structured matrix factorization, sparse learning, latent Dirichlet allocation, regression, semi-supervised and deep neural models, PCA-based ideological scoring, and metadata/network feature classification. Surveys, user studies, and simulation models complement computational analysis.

Recent trends emphasize early, message-level rumor detection; distinguishing data from ranking sources of search bias; identifying overlapping beliefs rather than strictly separate camps; measuring continuous intra-community conflict; incorporating low-connectivity users; and developing interventions such as crowd-based fact checking, targeted health bots, and methods to remove or contain malicious nodes.

852657daf02f6bf684534534375b0a899c65c47c.text:
### Graph Data Management, Querying, and Interoperability

This community focuses on scalable management and analysis of RDF, knowledge graphs, and property graphs. A major theme is SPARQL optimization, including OPTIONAL/left-outer joins, federated and SPARQL-LD queries, runtime plan adaptation, summary- and partition-driven processing, OWL entailment, preferences, keywords, and example-based querying. Work on RDF also addresses incomplete information, relational-to-RDF mappings, semantic data cubes, and interoperability with property-graph systems through translation and graph-mapping languages.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with practical indexing and systems techniques. Examples include hop-doubling and temporal reachability indexes, structural and summary graphs, source selection and replicated fragments for federations, adaptive storage architectures, incremental evaluation, and Gremlin-based traversal translation. Graph algorithms study opinion spreading, regular and context-free path queries, author disambiguation, and large-scale distance computation.

A parallel strand examines graph-system design, including property-graph type systems, graph database taxonomies, workload generation, and Gremlin’s traversal model. Provenance and reproducibility research uses graph segmentation, summarization, differencing, and workflow analysis, while algebraic and Datalog-based approaches support data integration and view updates.

Recent directions emphasize very large and evolving datasets, cloud and federated execution, adaptive physical organization, cross-model interoperability, and making complex graph querying more accessible.

ee1b12c201077529dc1d510ee1e6da348047ba49.text:
**Network Mining Across Web, Social, and Narrative Systems**

This community studies how network structure and digital traces reveal influence, communities, behavior, and information flow. A dominant theme is Wikipedia and related knowledge graphs: multilingual hyperlink networks support PageRank, CheiRank, 2DRank, reduced Google-matrix analysis, geopolitical and university comparisons, cultural bias studies, article recommendations, vandalism detection, and real-time breaking-news detection. Twitter and Facebook data similarly support political-intention prediction, trend-aware ranking, and information-flow analysis.

A second theme is network theory and algorithms. Papers investigate centrality, PageRank optimization, network formation games, learning and belief dynamics, communicability-enhancing edge modifications, node discovery, backbone extraction, link prediction, navigation, and scalable spectral embeddings. Mathematical analyses are frequently paired with simulations and empirical network comparisons.

Narrative networks form another substantial strand. Character-interaction graphs and multilayer or temporal models are used for genre classification, summarization, plot analysis, role detection, and predicting events such as character deaths. NLP methods include sentiment-enhanced extractive summarization, vector-context filtering for word-sense disambiguation, and unsupervised signed-network induction from dialogue.

Recent work trends toward longitudinal and multilingual datasets, dynamic and multilayer representations, real-time monitoring, scalable computation, and combining structural network measures with machine learning and semantic content.

53f5f931e22ba82fcb026b7c85a37e151667266f.text:
### Learning, Scaling, and Formalizing Data Management

This community centers on high-performance database systems and query processing. Major themes include join ordering and optimization (MILP, memory-aware cost models, learned cardinalities, neural optimizers, and index tuning), worst-case-optimal and parallel conjunctive-query evaluation, and formal complexity results for inequalities, projections, dynamic updates, XQuery, and distribution policies.

Graph analytics is frequently recast as relational processing: SQL, Datalog, joins, matrix multiplication, and specialized hardware support graph pattern matching and vertex-centric workloads. Several systems target large-scale and streaming data, including Accumulo/D4M associative arrays, column stores, in-memory databases, and lightweight blockchain or replicated-database infrastructure. Reliability and distributed consistency appear through parallel recovery, quorum staleness, cross-chain atomic commitment, and comparisons between blockchains and databases.

Typical methods combine theoretical bounds and combinatorial techniques with practical systems evaluation, parallel execution, sketches, sampling, compression, and hardware-conscious data structures. Machine learning increasingly supports data management: deep models estimate cardinalities, optimize plans, answer approximate aggregates, filter video queries, and integrate relational data with model training. Declarative, end-to-end analytics platforms seek both usability and performance.

Recent directions emphasize learned and probabilistic query processing, approximate interactive analytics, high-level languages without performance loss, collaborative/versioned datasets, and unified systems spanning data engineering, machine learning, graphs, and streaming workloads.

004d71a7632a0f979a77959f935d8aa2eef31781.text:
### Collaborative Web Knowledge, Search, and Social Networks

This community studies how user-generated Web data can support information retrieval, knowledge representation, and network analysis. Major themes include Wikipedia and Wiktionary as structured knowledge sources; collaborative tagging and folksonomies; search and ranking for Web, library, entity, and talent-search applications; and analysis of social, attention, and professional networks.

Typical methods combine graph-based algorithms (PageRank, HITS, centrality, link analysis, and network clustering), learning-to-rank and topic selection, query expansion, semantic similarity, entity linking, ontology matching, and statistical modeling of vocabulary and tagging growth. Several works transform semi-structured Wiktionary or Wikipedia content into relational, thesaurus, ontology, or machine-readable resources. Others use categories, hyperlinks, co-occurrence, clickstreams, or social labels to rank entities, identify expertise, recommend tags, and locate influential users.

Recent directions emphasize multilingual and language-agnostic processing, including cross-language ontology matching, densely annotated Wikipedia data, and scalable entity disambiguation on user-generated text. The community also increasingly applies these techniques to practical systems: low-cost IR evaluation, improved library catalogs, collaborative search, product design, talent discovery, and analytics of job mobility and talent-flow networks.

2b9e5cc6ed81f67687cf74a05baca19270de8a3f.text:
**From XML Warehousing to Real-Time Event Intelligence**

This community centers on managing and analyzing complex, heterogeneous, and rapidly changing data. A major theme is XML data management: tree-pattern querying, structural preferences, XML warehouse modeling, fragmentation, benchmarks, summarizability, and workload-aware materialized-view selection. Data-warehouse optimization more broadly includes dynamic index selection, frequent-itemset mining, query clustering, and database auto-administration.

A second theme is event and stream processing. Work addresses complex-event detection with NFAs, lazy chain automata, adaptive evaluation structures, load shedding, consistency, and RFID stream transformation. Social-media research applies statistical mention anomalies, entity clustering, and temporal-community modeling to detect and visualize real-time events.

Typical methods include workload-driven data mining, clustering, simulation and configurable evaluation frameworks, benchmark and synthetic-data generation, query-based optimization, and architecture design. Applications span business intelligence for small enterprises, healthcare, archaeology, IoT, and multimedia or multimodal repositories.

Recent trends emphasize scalability and immediacy: processing high-volume social and sensor streams, supporting complex data and changing access patterns, exploiting hybrid high-bandwidth memory, and automatically adapting indexes, views, event plans, and storage layouts. There is also growing attention to realistic benchmarking through scalable generators and feature-controlled synthetic datasets.

15fd83d1da1ee0c6a529804138e3f4b27e328b25.text:
## Semantic Web Preservation and Temporal Knowledge

This community studies how to represent, preserve, retrieve, and enrich evolving digital information. Major themes include web archiving and digital preservation; semantic modeling of scientific artifacts, mechanisms, manuscripts, and scholarly claims; modular repositories for heterogeneous digital objects; and linked open data with provenance, versioning, and quality control.

Typical methods combine persistent identifiers, RDF/OWL and SPARQL, semantic layers, ontologies, OAIS-based packages, MPEG-21 representations, and modular repository architectures such as Fedora and aDORe. Researchers build practical systems and libraries—including VXA, ArcLink, Carbon Date, TweetsKB, nanopub-java, and the Open Annotation model—and evaluate them on large web archives, social-media corpora, scholarly objects, and cultural collections. Empirical studies use access logs, longitudinal snapshots, link neighborhoods, social bookmarks, and annotation datasets to assess disappearance, popularity, freshness, and discoverability.

Recent work increasingly treats information as temporal and evolving: it addresses multi-version data, historical linked datasets, changing entities, web-page loss, orphaned annotations, and scholarly “orphans.” Search and collection increasingly exploit social signals, semantic metadata, and temporal ranking, while focused crawling incorporates freshness. Another trend is toward machine-actionable scientific communication through nanopublications, formal claims, provenance, and interoperable annotations, alongside stronger attention to data quality, rights, and durable access.

c99e759e8a99a1ae3c9b5727cdd48ef8672838bc.text:
### Keyphrase-Centered Document Understanding

This community focuses primarily on extracting keyphrases, keywords, concepts, and important passages to support indexing, retrieval, classification, summarization, recommendation, and news aggregation. Applications span scientific, biomedical, medical, broadcast, online news, social tagging, and disaster-response data.

Typical methods combine lexical statistics (TF–IDF, frequency, position), supervised machine learning, neural networks, and graph-based ranking. Text is modeled as graphs, complex networks, multipartite graphs, dependency trees, or folksonomies; PageRank variants incorporate semantic relatedness, semantic roles, connectivity, and topical information. Text denoising is used to retain information-rich sentences before indexing or relation extraction. Extracted terms also support title construction, conceptual representations, popularity prediction, and hierarchical multi-document summarization.

Privacy is a distinct theme: secure binary embeddings enable approximate summarization and passage retrieval without exposing document content. Evaluation and resources are receiving increased attention through large-scale cross-domain comparisons and KPTimes, an editor-curated news keyphrase-generation dataset. Recent directions emphasize neural keyphrase generation, semantic and contextual graph features, domain-aware ranking, actionable hashtag identification, real-time processing, and more rigorous benchmarking.

c7ec171f425cff22aa911b5a7e291c5711a84efe.text:
### Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing and Analysis

This community centers on protecting sensitive relational, graph, transactional, mobility, and behavioral data while retaining analytical utility. Differential privacy is the dominant framework, complemented by k-anonymity, l-diversity, t-closeness, randomization, provenance privacy, and secure computation.

A major theme is accurate private query answering: histograms, range and marginal queries, high-dimensional workloads, and batch workloads. Typical methods include hierarchical decompositions, wavelet transforms, matrix mechanisms, optimized strategy queries, adaptive workload selection, data-aware partitioning, and noisy linear counting interfaces. Other work applies privacy to clustering, decision trees, frequent-itemset mining, search-log sanitization, data cleaning, recommendation, and hierarchical demographic estimation.

A parallel theme addresses privacy-preserving publication and inference risks, including sparse data, unstructured records, background knowledge, reconstruction, algorithm-aware adversaries, and membership disclosure. Graph-oriented studies protect provenance, paths, and social links using views, surrogates, and link anonymization. Systems research explores partitioned outsourcing, federated databases, and trusted hardware.

Recent directions emphasize local differential privacy, scalable and utility-aware mechanisms, workload- and data-adaptive error optimization, privacy-preserving exploration, fair decision-making, and synthetic mobility data that accounts for demographic bias.

18de0c172009d124c602269172b1d4acd463e726.text:
## Recommender Systems: Sequential, Neural, and Responsible Personalization

This community centers on personalized recommendation across e-commerce, media, news, travel, education, and advertising. Major themes include collaborative filtering and matrix factorization; session- and sequence-based prediction; playlist and event continuation; multimodal and content-aware recommendation; and modeling diverse user interests. Researchers also address long-tail exposure, popularity bias, diversity, cold starts, missing modalities, shared accounts, cross-domain behavior, and anonymous users.

Typical methods range from slope-one predictors, neighborhood and signed-bipartite ranking, ontologies, latent semantic analysis, and hybrid content–collaborative models to neural collaborative filtering, variational autoencoders, nonlinear interaction networks, recurrent models, graph neural networks, mixture-of-tastes models, factorization machines, and multimodal attention. Ranking and selection increasingly use re-ranking, determinantal point processes, context trees, metric learning, and reinforcement learning.

Recent trends emphasize dynamic behavioral modeling through sessions, inter-session history, and complex item transitions; richer use of text, audio, images, temporal signals, trust, and social ties; and practical constraints such as scalability, online updates, and real-world evaluation. Work also increasingly considers robustness and system impact, including fraudulent reviews, reputation, offline-evaluation bias, popularity and long-tail inequalities, user experience, and revenue optimization.

28d29c4ad9fe7a80e87b76dafc64642c74f0444f.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Source Inference

This community studies how information, infection, failures, wildlife, and products spread through social, technological, biological, and cyber-physical networks. A major theme is **influence maximization**: selecting seeds to increase adoption, recruitment, advertising revenue, or cascade size under budget, pricing, quantity, or resource constraints. Work increasingly considers temporal, continuous-time, adaptive, and activity-aware networks, as well as non-submodular and complex contagion.

A second theme is **inverse diffusion**. Papers infer hidden sources, initiation times, edge infection probabilities, network structures, and propagation dynamics from incomplete, aggregate, or partially ordered cascades. Methods include Jordan centers and covers, candidate-subgraph extraction, optimization, soft thresholding, directed spanning-tree models, contrastive training, and network infusion.

Other studies address epidemic containment and economic or social costs, cascading failures and self-healing interdependent systems, diffusion-based signal distances, and stability in time-varying networks. Typical tools include epidemic and cascade models, continuous-time Markov chains, random matrix theory, message passing, stochastic optimization, mixed-integer programming, submodularity-based greedy guarantees, heuristics, particle swarm optimization, random walks, and simulation.

Overall, the research trends toward realistic partial feedback, evolving or adaptive topology, limited observations and probing resources, multiple objectives beyond spread, and data-driven inference integrated with principled approximation or recovery guarantees.

a4313f3f7f0e9964f92781c1b636f34005de6660.text:
## Learning-Based Search, Ranking, and Semantic Retrieval

This community centers on improving information retrieval through learned representations, ranking models, and search infrastructure. Major themes include document and passage ranking, query understanding and expansion, entity and expert retrieval, dataset search, semantic similarity, and specialized applications such as email, mobile-app, e-commerce, healthcare, and personal-memory search. It also addresses web quality, spam detection, and dynamic or temporal information needs.

Typical methods combine traditional retrieval principles with machine learning: learning-to-rank using pointwise, pairwise, listwise, groupwise, or bipartite objectives; neural architectures that model local relevance, cross-document interactions, entities, fields, or query context; embeddings, semantic hashing, kernel models, and approximate nearest-neighbor graphs; and heterogeneous-network authority and content analysis. Query clustering, pseudo-relevance feedback, schema-label generation, and concept-guided expansion support query interpretation. Benchmark collections and theoretical or axiomatic frameworks guide evaluation and model design.
