Recent work is strongly shaped by pretrained language models, especially BERT and multilingual BERT, used for multi-stage reranking, passage retrieval, entailment, and cross-lingual transfer. Multi-task learning, direct metric optimization, permutation-invariant ranking, interpretability, and latency–quality tradeoffs are emerging concerns. Dataset search, non-factoid question answering, temporal entity aspects, and dynamic retrieval reflect expanding search scenarios.

00b6723f6cbfa9f6164b53015054c0eb401828aa.text:
## Community Detection in Complex and Evolving Networks

This community centers on defining, discovering, and evaluating communities in complex networks. Major themes include the ambiguity of “good” communities and the comparison of quality functions, with multi-criteria evaluation, modularity variants, conductance, NMI, Omega, and node-level F-scores used for assessment. Work also addresses overlapping, attributed, weighted, two-mode, multiplex, and dynamic networks, reflecting increasingly rich representations of social, biological, bibliometric, and information systems.

Typical methods include modularity optimization (including multislice and adaptive signed-weight formulations), label propagation, density-based clustering with manifold learning, clique percolation, core methods, latent Bayesian relational models, and bio-inspired optimization. Spectral techniques are prominent: local spectral clustering, Krylov subspaces, graph spectra, personalized PageRank, and diffusion-based approaches support scalable or seed-based detection. Theoretical studies examine detectability limits, localization, neighborhoods, and graph equivalence.

Recent directions emphasize moving from global to local detection for massive graphs; handling overlapping membership, node attributes, multiple edge types, and temporal evolution; stabilizing and regularizing algorithms; and selecting algorithms or quality functions according to network context. Related studies apply communities to peer influence, churn, adoption, risk prediction, social activity organization, visualization, and science mapping.

e0d83f5c1042530148ff1a1884dcdd6ada73434f.text:
## Dynamic Social and Text Analytics

This community centers on extracting knowledge from large, heterogeneous, and continuously changing data. A major theme is topic modeling: latent topics for hypertext, scientific articles, reviews, bibliographic networks, and creative discovery, including multi-grain, nonparametric, and dynamic models that capture topic birth, death, popularity, and temporal evolution. Scalability is a recurring concern, addressed through clustered/decomposed inference, summarization, and compact query-provisioning sketches.

A second major theme is social-media intelligence. Twitter and other platforms are treated as real-time sensors for sports, protests, disasters, disease outbreaks, misinformation, sentiments, tourism, and social action. Typical methods combine stream mining, event and sub-event detection, burst-region discovery, retrieval, summarization, spatial-temporal analysis, and visualization. Wikipedia and linked web content provide complementary sources for disease monitoring and forecasting.

The community also studies personalization and behavior, including neural next-song recommendation, video longevity, revisits, retweets, and heterogeneous representations of individuals. Methods increasingly use convolutional or character-based neural networks, multimodal evidence, ontologies, fuzzy logic, and graph-based representations. Recent work trends toward real-time operation, large-scale deployment, multilingual and multimodal analysis, dynamic modeling, and decision support for public-health, emergency, and environmental applications.

e59057fd5e8c26b3cf61b53a03952153483e2969.text:
### Scholarly Impact and Digital Research Communication

This community studies how scholarly work is discovered, disseminated, evaluated, and used across journals, books, repositories, libraries, and social platforms. Major themes include the validity and interpretation of altmetrics; relationships among citations, readership, downloads, tweets, and online reviews; open-access and preprint effects; scholarly search and recommendation; peer-reviewer assignment and conference classification; and bibliometric assessment of books and publishers. Several studies examine web links, digital-library usage, citation behavior, and positional or author-related biases.

Typical methods combine large-scale bibliographic, usage-log, social-media, and peer-assessment datasets with statistical analysis, including correlations, regression, principal-component and factor analysis, distribution modeling, and validation against expert judgments. Other work uses text and review mining, machine learning for hyperlink classification and bibliographic-reference matching, visualization and interviews, integer programming for reviewer assignment, and network or behavioral analysis.

Recent trends emphasize moving beyond citations toward heterogeneous digital traces of scholarly and societal impact, while critically addressing data quality, platform dependencies, and disciplinary differences. Preprint repositories, open access, and rapid online responses are increasingly central to communication studies. Research also trends toward automated discovery and recommendation systems, dynamic researcher interests, improved repository search, and data-driven indicators for books, publishers, and venues.

b6acdab37343a8f9abbe1073974f0d522a1caa4b.text:
## Online Social Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Risk

This community centers on how online social networks form, evolve, and shape information and behavior. Major themes include information cascades, rumor and product diffusion, virality, social influence, popularity, and engagement across Twitter, YouTube, Facebook, Yelp, games, and scholarly citation networks. Other recurring concerns are anomaly and malicious-URL detection, fake news, privacy exposure, financial contagion, criminal intermediaries, suicide risk, and network vulnerability.

Typical methods combine large-scale observational datasets with graph analysis: centrality and pair-dependency measures, community detection, homophily and tie-strength analysis, cascade-structure characterization, and temporal network modeling. Researchers also use threshold and strategic adoption games, point processes and multivariate Hawkes models, stochastic diffusion models, recommender-system theory, machine learning, crowd signals, visual analytics, and multimodal content analysis. Several studies provide algorithmic or complexity results, while others validate models on massive real-world platforms.

Recent directions emphasize richer and more realistic diffusion models incorporating mass media, absent nodes, exogenous activity, competing products, and active campaigning. Work increasingly predicts popularity and engagement early, distinguishes content effects from structural factors, analyzes visual memes and disaster imagery, and targets interventions against misinformation and malicious influence. Privacy-aware controls, systemic-risk monitoring, and cross-domain “universal” diffusion dynamics are also growing concerns.

ba414ff261ae4dbc7ba73e1fa4a5a2789c9771f1.text:
**Multilayer Social Networks: Dynamics, Diffusion, and Identity**

This community studies social networks as multiplex or multilayer systems, where users may be connected through friendship, communication, shared objects, professional ties, or activity across platforms. Major themes include defining and measuring multilayer structure (degree centrality, reciprocity, motifs, clustering, multiplexity, missing data, and link prediction), modeling online/offline and cross-platform identities, and analyzing group formation and evolution.

A substantial line of work detects, compares, and predicts community changes using GED, SGCI, Louvain, Infomap, temporal features, and classifiers. Other studies examine influence and information diffusion through seed selection, branching processes, epidemic models, and coupled social–physical networks. Applications include recommendations, human resources, disease containment, viral campaigns, misinformation, sentiment, and influential-blogger discovery.

Typical methods combine graph-theoretic metrics, spectral and probabilistic models, community detection, language modeling, topic and sentiment analysis, machine learning, feature engineering, and experiments on Web 2.0, email, blog, Twitter, Facebook, Foursquare, cellular, and browse-log data. Synthetic-network generation and sampling address scale and privacy constraints.

Recent directions emphasize unified theories and dynamical models for multiplex networks, scalable algorithms for changing graphs, cross-platform user matching, privacy and deanonymization risks, and more realistic diffusion, epidemic, and recommendation models that exploit interactions among layers.

7fb98d3a72df7aceed5823014e7a80f69071007b.text:
## Bibliometric Evaluation, Equity, and Research Performance

This community studies how scientific performance is measured and how institutional, geographic, demographic, and collaborative factors shape evaluation outcomes. A major focus is the Italian higher-education and research system, including north–south disparities, regional specialization, university rankings, national assessment exercises (VQR), nepotism, recruitment, academic age and seniority, and the persistence of highly productive scientists.

Typical methods are large-scale bibliometric analyses of Web of Science and Google Scholar data, using field-standardized productivity and citation indicators such as FSS, MNCS, h-index, impact factor, and SSI. Researchers apply multivariate and quantile regression, time-series and Granger-causality tests, network analysis, clustering for author disambiguation, Gini and Pareto analyses, funnel plots for uncertainty, and stochastic models. Comparative studies examine gender, academic rank, co-authorship, international collaboration, interdisciplinarity, author order, and counting methods.

Recent trends emphasize methodological critique and fairness: questioning journal impact factor and per-publication indicators, correcting rankings for gender and field differences, accounting for uncertainty and contribution, and evaluating optimal observation periods. The community also extends bibliometrics toward knowledge-flow analysis, publication recommendation, scientific specialization, and the effects of editorial-board membership and collaboration on research impact.

16de7738a93660b413b01fe20db78ac5b5f13e30.text:
### Social Media Integrity, Polarization, and Manipulation

This community studies how online social networks shape political discourse, information quality, and collective behavior. Major themes include misinformation, rumors, conspiracy narratives, fake news, extremism, and echo chambers; algorithmic and data-driven bias in search and news feeds; demographic inequality and user profiling; and security threats from socialbots, Sybil devices, crowdturfing, and malicious applications. Several studies examine fringe communities such as Gab and 4chan, politically motivated networks, ISIS support, Russia-sponsored campaigns, and Gamergate.

Typical methods combine large-scale data collection from Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, and web services with network analysis, temporal and propagation modeling, surveys, controlled bot experiments, and cross-platform measurement. Machine-learning approaches include nonnegative matrix factorization, supervised and semi-supervised classification, stance and rumor detection, domain adaptation, embeddings, demographic inference, and feature-based prediction using content, metadata, network, and temporal signals. Formal metrics and analytical models are used to quantify bias, visibility, segregation, and inequality.

Recent work trends toward studying information ecosystems rather than isolated platforms: linking search, social, and advertising data; evaluating fact-checking and verification; tracking cascades with platforms such as Hoaxy; and deploying bots for health, activism, or manipulation. Attention is also shifting toward reproducibility, evaluation bias, intervention design, and the societal consequences of algorithmic amplification.

6ea5849b8952bdfe31ae11d52a5b6c8f90bc0943.text:
## Recommender Systems: From Collaborative Signals to Context-Aware Personalization

This community centers on personalized recommendation across products, movies, news, education, images, and tags. Core themes include collaborative filtering from ratings or implicit feedback, sequential and session-based prediction, and integration of content, social, geographic, and item-relationship signals. Several works address practical challenges such as sparse data, cold-start users and items, long-tail discovery, anonymous sessions, missing modalities, noisy ratings, fraudulent reviews, and filter bubbles.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, slope-one predictors, nearest-neighbor and Markov-chain models to Bayesian Personalized Ranking, graph and network algorithms, co-clustering, and collective factorization. Neural approaches increasingly model nonlinear user–item interactions, autoregressive feedback, session representations, semi-autoencoders, and educational or multimodal recommendation. Content signals include text, subtitles, audio, visual features, CNN embeddings, tags, and heterogeneous relationships such as substitutes and complements.

Emerging directions emphasize richer user representations—mixtures of tastes and inter-session behavior—alongside robustness and interpretability through reputation modeling, signed networks, overlapping co-clusters, and rating centrality. Multimodal learning is expanding toward missing or corrupted inputs and cold-start settings. Recent work also combines marketplace, social-network, and location data, while studying novelty, behavioral change, and diversity in news and long-tail recommendation.

d3d24cdf995c0c6a93fd86469cc83c135f46d35c.text:
**Social Media Analytics for Human Behavior and Urban Space**

This community studies how social and location-aware digital traces reveal human preferences, mobility, social interaction, and urban environments. Major themes include political opinion and election forecasting, voter and follower behavior, business reputation and promotion, group event coordination, and social diffusion. A substantial urban-computing strand examines mobility patterns, home and visited locations, functional regions, neighborhood signatures, city boundaries, tourism networks, and emotionally perceived routes. Other work maps urban smell and sound, measures park-related affect, and extracts qualitative geospatial knowledge.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, Flickr, check-in, mobile-network, telecommunications, and review data with natural-language processing, sentiment analysis, topic models, sparse learning, regression, and supervised classifiers. Network analysis supports mobility modeling, community detection, spatial interaction, and location recommendation. Spatial-temporal models, low-rank approximation, probabilistic geospatial inference, Gaussian mixtures, and trajectory reconstruction address geographic structure and incomplete observations. Evaluation increasingly considers accuracy, calibration, precision, coverage, and sampling bias.

Recent directions emphasize fine-grained geolocation and semantic labeling, uncertainty-aware inference, selective digital traces, multimodal urban sensing, and systems that translate social-media signals into practical tools for planning, routing, business-site selection, and interactive news or map exploration.

9d5ff0a78c83e814e889689a4cd2473f0889c3d6.text:
## Information Retrieval: Neural Matching, Interactive Ranking, and Entity-Aware Search

This community centers on improving search quality, scalability, and understanding of user intent. Major themes include learning to rank and relevance modeling; query expansion, reformulation, clustering, and entity decomposition; document and query representation; web-quality and spam detection; and retrieval over entities, tables, knowledge bases, news, and images.

Typical methods combine classical retrieval signals such as BM25, probabilistic language models, term distributions, and phrase dependence with machine learning. Neural approaches use word embeddings, convolutional and recurrent networks, interaction matrices, kernel pooling, and end-to-end pairwise ranking losses to model local and semantic relevance. Entity salience, entity linking, knowledge bases, and relationship-aware test collections support richer semantic search. For scale, researchers develop compact binary signatures, semantic hashing, K-tree clustering, and sketch-based indexing.

A strong trend is toward interactive and online retrieval: dynamic utility frameworks, session-aware query analysis, implicit feedback, list-level feedback, multileaved ranker evaluation, and dueling-bandit methods. Other emerging concerns include explainable ranking, credibility alongside relevance, real-time news processing, and behavior modeling for image search. Benchmark datasets such as LETOR and specialized collections enable systematic evaluation, while methods increasingly seek both semantic understanding and efficient deployment at large scale.

882e1d159ef40274cf24b4438e83a61b6a0a93a3.text:
### Semantic Web and Graph Querying

This community centers on querying, optimizing, and validating RDF and graph data. A major theme is SPARQL processing: algebraic foundations, multiset semantics, OPTIONAL and left-outer-join optimization, runtime and incremental evaluation, provenance, preferences, keyword integration, and OWL entailment. Federated querying is prominent, including source selection, heuristic reordering, SPARQL-LD and LDQL over heterogeneous Web sources, replicated fragments, and large-scale Bio2RDF deployments.

A second theme concerns graph and path queries, including regular and context-free path querying, simple-path complexity, Gremlin traversals, and graph processing over relational systems. Knowledge-graph usability is addressed through querying by example and relationship explanation.

The papers frequently use formal semantics, complexity analysis, algebraic rewriting, chase-based reasoning, Datalog, nested relational algebra, graph parsing, and cost- or cardinality-aware optimization. Practical evaluation relies on prototypes, federations, synthetic workload generation, and benchmarks such as gMark and Geographica.

Recent directions emphasize distributed and Web-scale data access, adaptive or incremental query execution, replicated and heterogeneous sources, richer RDF features such as incomplete information and shapes, and more accessible interfaces combining structured queries with examples or keywords.

5e7013dff087eb66972de62c1afa39e19ceac255.text:
### Network Representation and Analysis in Complex, Dynamic Graphs

This community studies how to model, represent, sample, and infer structure in large-scale social, information, semantic, and affiliation networks. Major themes include node and document representation learning, community detection, link and relationship prediction, signed-network balance, centrality, dense subgraph discovery, and network diffusion. Several works address dynamic and heterogeneous settings, including continuous-time relationship prediction, dynamic stochastic blockmodels, coevolving multilayer link prediction, temporal representation robustness, and hierarchical change-point detection.

Typical methods combine probabilistic modeling (stochastic blockmodels, maximum likelihood, absorbing Markov chains), random walks and sampling (wedge, BFS, hybrid-affiliation, and quality-guaranteed multi-network sampling), scalable distributed computation (MapReduce, MPI, external memory), and machine learning. Deep embeddings capture content and structural identity, while path-based and ensemble models support fact checking and triple scoring. Structural analysis is applied to criminal networks, insider trading, political violence, privacy, and social relationships.

Recent trends emphasize temporal, multilayer, uncertain, and signed graphs; integration of node content with topology; scalable approximation for massive networks; and richer structural representations beyond simple proximity, including structural identity, indirect co-location links, and cross-layer dependencies.

3e230b9cb767be8bbc49c49270bafbf7be205881.text:
## Scalable Analysis of Dynamic and Temporal Networks

This community focuses on making large, evolving networks analyzable and actionable. A major theme is efficient graph querying: reachability, bounded and regular reachability, shortest distances and paths, single-source queries, and temporal path queries. Proposed solutions rely on preprocessing and indexing, including hop-doubling labels, interval and hierarchical labeling, independent-set schemes, distance sketches, hub acceleration, and distributed evaluation, with attention to construction, I/O, and query-time guarantees.

A second theme develops formalisms for temporal interaction data. Time-varying graphs, stream graphs, and link streams represent changing contacts more faithfully than static snapshots. Algebraic temporal quantities and semirings support journeys, latency, waiting times, and temporal betweenness, while temporal indicators, time centrality, dynamic graphlets, and temporal community measures characterize evolving structure.

The community also studies diffusion and influence through dynamic monopolies, opinion spreading, gossip, contagion, and media effects. Applications include hospitals, mailing lists, knowledge mobilization, scientific communities, biological network comparison, recommendation, and trust-aware systems.

Recent work trends toward fully dynamic indexes, scalable and distributed processing, temporal-aware centrality and network alignment, and richer structural descriptors that preserve interaction timing rather than aggregating it away.

37821590bd0cb6a3882688c6107f4cf60d6e54f7.text:
### Preserving and Making Sense of Evolving Web Knowledge

This community focuses on durable, semantically rich preservation of digital objects, web resources, and scientific artifacts. Major themes include lifecycle and provenance modeling; modular repositories for heterogeneous, compound objects; preservation of evolving linked data; and web archiving for historical research, journalism, and digital humanities. Scholarly “orphans,” annotations, manuscripts, and social-media collections extend preservation beyond traditional publications.

Typical methods combine RDF/Linked Data, ontologies, persistent identifiers, OAIS and MPEG-21 representations, SPARQL, semantic layers, and standards-based repository architectures such as Fedora and aDORe. Researchers also use longitudinal Internet Archive collections, HTTP and metadata evidence for dating, focused crawling, temporal retrieval, link-graph analysis, and social signals from Twitter, Delicious, and Wikipedia. Supervised learning and time-aware ranking support query classification, event detection, and archive search.

Recent work emphasizes freshness and real-time collection through social-web-guided crawling, large annotated tweet corpora, and crowd behavior. Other trends address versioned data and provenance, interoperable open annotation, decentralized nanopublications, scholarly artifacts identified through ORCID, and robust timestamping and hashing. Across the community, the central challenge is maintaining trustworthy context, discoverability, and usability as resources, formats, links, and web content change.

9202eb4bda55df984c5920fc86eaa8595f19cec5.text:
## Scalable Data Management and Intelligent Query Processing

This community focuses on making data systems scalable, adaptive, and easier to use across relational, graph, cloud, and analytical workloads. A major theme is query optimization: join ordering via mixed-integer linear programming, worst-case-optimal and parallel joins, cardinality estimation with deep learning, sampling-based aggregate estimation, and size-bound analysis. Several studies address distributed execution, including MapReduce optimization, SQL-on-Hadoop comparisons, single-round conjunctive queries, coordination-free computation, and parallel correctness.

Graph processing is another prominent theme. Relational databases such as Vertica, high-level engines such as EmptyHeaded, RDF systems, and streaming-graph indexes demonstrate efforts to combine declarative interfaces with efficient execution. Systems research also targets high-level query engines, adaptive indexing, replicated-database tuning, stale-view cleaning, dataset versioning, and multi-tenant resource allocation.

Typical methods include formal complexity and communication analyses, cost-based and adaptive optimization, sketches and sampling, parallel/distributed algorithms, declarative query compilation, and empirical benchmarking. Machine learning is increasingly integrated into database management for cardinality estimation, transaction scheduling, analytics, and model lifecycle management. Recent trends emphasize intelligent automation, interactive and streaming analytics, cloud privacy and consistency, collaborative data science, and unified support for data-intensive and deep-learning workflows.

5f161c3f9e3aee20e36fd9d78c17fbf751e0fd2b.text:
## Network Dynamics, Influence, and Social Information Flow

This community studies how network structure, information, and individual behavior shape diffusion, opinions, influence, and discoverability. A major theme is opinion dynamics: DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, biased-assimilation, signed-network, and multi-topic models examine consensus, polarization, disagreement, stability, and antagonistic interactions. Related work investigates evolving social power, susceptibility, trust, and the effects of homophily, biases, and stubborn agents.

A second theme is identifying and controlling important network components. Papers develop and compare centrality measures, axioms for evaluating them, robustness indices, navigability and communicability scores, PageRank and coverage optimization, link prediction, node discovery, and strategies for modifying edges or networks to improve influence, delay, or information spread.

Typical methods combine graph theory, Markov chains, spectral embeddings, matrix and Laplacian analysis, dynamical-systems convergence proofs, optimization, motif and subgraph mining, and scalable algorithms evaluated on large real or synthetic networks. Network backbones are extracted using traffic data, clustering, and information-theoretic criteria.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic, topic-aware, and content-rich settings: personalized recommendation creates feedback loops with opinion formation; social-media genotypes model topic-specific behavior; temporal event and controversy detection incorporate interaction, time, and stance; and active sensing estimates interpersonal trust from observed opinions.

0714ee165dc101aa82625c89f93e8443f3a401a0.text:
## Scholarly Retrieval, Recommendation, and Evaluation

This community focuses on making scholarly information more discoverable, interpretable, and useful. Major themes include semantic publishing and Linked Open Data, extraction of metadata and quality indicators from papers, citation matching, and ranking academic entities or documents. A second strong theme is research-paper recommendation, especially for digital libraries, repositories, and reference managers.

Typical methods combine information extraction, citation and network analysis, machine learning, rules, and large-scale distributed processing with Apache Hadoop and MapReduce. Recommender research spans user modeling, related-article recommendation, recommender-as-a-service architectures, and large-scale operational systems such as Mr. DLib and CORE. Meta-learning is applied to select bibliographic parsers, while deep reinforcement learning is explored for sponsored-search ranking.

Evaluation is a central concern. Studies examine online versus offline metrics, choice overload, position bias, temporal variation in effectiveness, and correlations between expert, search-engine, and social-media rankings. Active and probabilistic sampling aim to reduce the cost and bias of relevance judgments; counterfactual methods address biased implicit feedback.

Recent directions emphasize production-ready services, reusable datasets such as the 94-million-record RARD II collection, scalable scholarly mining, richer Linked Data, and statistically principled, unbiased evaluation of ranking and recommendation systems.

68f3f8da0bef68cd3b8ac6a3e244a0250d035349.text:
## Scholarly Networks, Retrieval, and Bibliometric Intelligence

This community studies scholarly information as interconnected networks, with major emphasis on author identity, research impact, and information discovery. Author-name disambiguation is addressed through collaboration patterns, network topology, initials-based baselines, semi-supervised learning, seed-and-expand workflows, and evaluation on labeled digital-library data. Bibliometric research develops and assesses PageRank and its weighted, recursive, and interactive variants for ranking authors, papers, patents, and multilingual Wikipedia entities, while distinguishing popularity from prestige and tracing emerging technologies.

Typical methods include social-network analysis, coauthorship and citation modeling, eigenvector and spectral analysis of Google matrices, graph visualization, statistical reliability measures, and comparative empirical evaluation. Graphons provide nonparametric models for massive networks, while MapReduce supports scalable frequent-itemset mining.

A parallel theme concerns information retrieval and scholarly interfaces: discipline-specific query expansion, Bradfordizing, knowledge maps, visual search, metadata enrichment through Linked Data, and bibliometric-enhanced retrieval aim to improve navigation of growing collections. Studies also examine infrastructure durability, reproducible computational practice through Jupyter notebooks, and evaluation reliability.

Recent directions emphasize multilingual and geopolitical network mining, reduced Google Matrix analysis, emerging-trend detection, semi-automated and ethnicity-sensitive disambiguation, and more interpretable visual and network-based scholarly services.

3fb11dcd9264c0d58d1d77678647e29e86a3c231.text:
## Data Integration, Entity Resolution, and Human-Guided Data Quality

This community focuses on producing reliable, integrated data from heterogeneous, noisy, and conflicting sources. Major themes include entity resolution and consolidation, truth discovery and data fusion, source dependence and copying, schema/constraint discovery, and Web or Linked Data integration. Several studies address crowdsourcing, including worker assessment, unreliable labels, human–machine cooperation, low-latency labeling, and human-assisted search. Spatial crowdsourcing and urban spatiotemporal data integration form additional application areas.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and Bayesian models for truth inference, hybrid models for multiple truths, confidence estimation, and unknown-data impact analysis. Entity matching commonly uses blocking, locality-sensitive hashing, graph matching, collective message passing, deep representations, and edit-similarity joins. Rule- and constraint-based techniques discover functional, order, and ontology dependencies, while pattern learning supports schema understanding and error detection. Optimization, partitioning, indexing, and parallel processing are used to scale linkage and task assignment.

Recent directions emphasize reducing expert effort through deep learning and automation, while retaining human oversight for quality guarantees. Systems increasingly combine machine predictions with targeted crowd input, exploit source correlations and copying, and pursue scalable, adaptive processing for Web-scale and long-string data. There is also growing attention to uncertainty, multiple valid answers, latency, prediction-aware assignment, and the effects of missing or unknown data.

eff592c50f6d30c74cef6d8c4675e9e5a94cdef3.text:
## Scalable Search, Indexing, and Query Processing

This community focuses on making large-scale data retrieval faster, more compact, and more adaptable. Major themes include ranked and keyword search over relational, web, workflow, and social-content repositories; crawling hidden databases through query interfaces; and reranking results according to user preferences, consistency, diversity, or fairness. Skyline, aggregate skyline, influence-set, and fuzzy-linguistic queries extend multi-criteria and imprecise data analysis.

A second strong theme is low-level performance engineering. Papers develop compressed bitmap indexes, Roaring bitmaps, multidimensional compression, integer and key compression, SIMD decoding, fast posting-list intersection, and efficient set operations. Sorting and histogram-based layout optimization further improve compressed index performance. Hashing work examines independence and high-throughput string hashing.

Graph data receive substantial attention through RDF summary-graph query processing, subgraph-isomorphism techniques, learned query planning, heterogeneous entity-resolution blocking, and distributed frequent-subgraph mining. Specialized systems also exploit GPUs, multicore CPUs, and distributed in-memory dataflow frameworks for OLTP, pathology-image comparison, and mining.

Recent directions emphasize hardware-conscious algorithms (SIMD, GPUs, compressed execution), learned optimization and blocking, third-party query-reranking services, and responsible recommendation through fairness-aware reranking.

28bc6d11b70edca8fd13d401bcdccb41d84f0236.text:
**Scholarly Search, Metrics, and Online Knowledge Networks**

This community examines how digital scholarly infrastructures measure, organize, and disseminate knowledge. A major theme is bibliometric evaluation: comparisons among Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and Microsoft Academic Search; journal, researcher, and institutional rankings; h-index and related indicators; and relationships between citation measures and peer assessment. Several studies investigate Google Scholar’s coverage, ability to identify highly cited documents, size, metadata quality, and profile-maintenance problems, including manipulation through merging or splitting article records.

A second theme concerns information retrieval and library discovery. Work addresses ranking factors for library materials, search-engine technology in catalogs, query expansion, credibility, and learning-to-rank methods for selecting topics and reducing the cost of test-collection evaluation.

The community also studies openness and access, measuring freely available publications and assessing repositories, mandates, and alternative publishing costs through multiple data sources.

Typical methods include large-scale citation and document analysis, longitudinal comparisons, automated querying and data collection, correlation and benchmarking, webometrics, social and complex-network analysis, statistical model selection, and computational-complexity analysis.

Recent trends include broader use of Google Scholar for evaluation, systematic attention to open-access evidence and mandates, citation growth for older literature, concerns about platform obsolescence and metric manipulation, and increasingly formal analysis of Wikipedia’s collaboration, conflict, and normative networks.

e2697a32d6ae82a3c7305f283a4e53d05698421f.text:
## Scalable, Reliable Data Management for Scientific and Distributed Workloads

This community explores database systems that scale across multicore processors, clusters, data centers, and massive scientific datasets. Major themes include high-throughput OLTP, concurrency control, recovery, replication, spatial and multidimensional indexing, scientific metadata, and energy-efficient infrastructure.

Typical methods exploit hardware and workload characteristics: multiversioning, optimistic and pessimistic concurrency control, snapshot isolation, flat combining, application-aware and adaptive logging, parallel replay, log-structured storage, and physiological partitioning. Distributed systems use replication, Paxos-based protocols, multi-data-center consistency, and highly available transaction models. For scientific data, relational backends are extended with arrays, metadata and provenance support, batch scheduling, and indexes such as Hierarchical Triangular Meshes, zones, B-trees, and zone pyramids. Query generation, automatic application partitioning, reenactment-based debugging, and data-sharing-aware execution address usability and analytical performance.

Recent trends emphasize mixed OLTP/OLAP workloads, contention-resistant multicore execution, autonomous timestamping, rapid failure recovery, and cloud-scale write throughput. Energy has become a central design objective, motivating energy-aware query optimization, cluster architecture, elastic “wimpy” nodes, and dynamic repartitioning. Overall, the papers move from isolated database techniques toward integrated, modular, adaptive systems for data-intensive science and globally distributed services.

577184231efea183b21e937a1b185f26151dd0e2.text:
## Rich Semantic Modeling for Structured Knowledge

This community investigates replacing document-centered information systems with richly structured semantic representations. Core themes include modeling human activities and cultural artifacts, scientific mechanisms, historical newspapers and directories, digital repositories, and scientific research reports.

Typical methods draw on object-oriented modeling, ontologies, frame semantics, and a proposed Semantic Modeling Framework (SMF). The SMF represents mechanisms through Transitionals and hierarchies of Aggregates and Mechanisms, potentially implemented in the XFO environment. Other work extends ontologies to include state changes, instances, and scenarios. Case studies—such as Korean ceramic water droppers and mechanisms—test how detailed semantic descriptions capture production, function, variation, and causal structure.

For historical materials, text mining is coordinated with formative user-interface design to support exploratory search and richer access than keyword lookup. The proposed Norfolk directory links entities across years and connects structured summaries to newspaper mentions.

A prominent recent direction is the move toward model-oriented repositories and highly structured scientific communication. These systems organize relationships directly rather than merely storing documents, using rigorous upper ontologies and structured research designs to support assessment of scientific validity and evolving knowledgebases.

5d7e5186d6d083c7d19b698a6e27dd3553c76295.text:
## Social Networks, Influence, and Online Marketplaces

This community examines how social ties shape information diffusion, consumer decisions, recommendations, and online community platforms. One theme is rumor propagation: computational modeling links rumor spread to agents’ desires, trust networks, and societal homogeneity, with convergence analysis used to identify conditions affecting dissemination.

Several studies investigate commerce embedded in social networks. Analysis of Taobao uses transaction and social-network data, including triads and directed closure, to examine trust, information passing, and consumer choice. Recommender-system research combines online social-network and location-based data with marketplace information to improve item recommendations.

Empirical behavioral studies, including Mechanical Turk experiments, compare the effects of friends’ recommendations and aggregate ratings. They find that rating changes can influence choices more strongly than additional friend recommendations, while negative feedback from friends has particular impact.

Finally, Serefind demonstrates the implementation of a social classifieds platform, emphasizing security, privacy, usability, ranking, and communication, and evaluates deployment in a university community.

Overall, the work trends from theoretical diffusion models and network-structure analysis toward socially informed recommendation, experimentally measured influence, and practical platforms for trusted, community-based exchange.

facf7c8f4357213ed78775370c3a7035537526c2.text:
### Complex Networks for Science, Software, and Online Collaboration

This community applies complex-network methods to understand interconnected systems, especially scientific communication, software, social interaction, and online knowledge production. Major themes include the structure and evolution of coauthorship, citation, healthcare, and online social networks; interdisciplinarity and researcher–topic relatedness; and the reliability of bibliographic databases. Several studies examine software as class-dependency networks, characterizing scale-free and small-world structure, community organization, node mixing, and network-based indicators of quality, vulnerability, reuse, and controllability.

Typical methods include crawling web sites and search engines, constructing coauthorship, citation, dependency, and affiliation networks, and comparing local and global graph statistics. Researchers use centrality measures, preferential-attachment and citation-dynamics models, community and general-group detection, propagation algorithms, sequence analysis, and multi-level longitudinal analysis. Sampling and simplification techniques are systematically evaluated for their effects on communities and structural properties.

Recent trends extend network analysis beyond static topology toward evolving, multi-level, and cross-domain systems. Increasing attention is given to interdisciplinarity, influential or high-status actors, database inconsistencies, and the behavioral consequences of incomplete data. Online collaboration is also studied through collective memory, social movements, and sequential work routines, linking network structure with organizational processes and real-world outcomes.

d6cb9d609eab4872d7caba2dbd6b84594195ad71.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Epidemic Dynamics

This community studies how information, influence, disease, failures, and adoption propagate through complex, social, temporal, and interdependent networks. A major theme is **source localization and network inference** from incomplete cascades: identifying single or multiple origins, estimating initiation times, and recovering hidden structures or edge-infection probabilities. Related work develops diffusion and superposition distances, collective-diffusion models, and cascade models using partial temporal information.

A second focus is **influence maximization and intervention**. Studies select seeds, recruit workers, promote products, or allocate containment resources under static, temporal, adaptive, continuous-time, and resource-constrained settings. Objectives increasingly move beyond reach to adoption, revenue, acceptance, and quantity-limited profit. Network design, community structure, and external agents are used to improve cascade spread or epidemic control.

Typical methods include submodular and adaptive-greedy approximation, heuristic and randomized algorithms, Jordan-center/cover localization, optimization and mixed-integer programming, particle-swarm search, random walks, continuous-time Markov chains, message passing, random-matrix analysis, and simulation on real and synthetic networks.

Recent directions emphasize adaptive decisions with feedback, evolving and non-Markovian networks, complex contagion, partial observations, cyber-physical resilience, and integrating social activity, incentives, pricing, and economic or social costs into diffusion models.

6ff5efc489b0aaca8aa5701e35c8d0d0e7249961.text:
### Scientometrics, Citation Networks, and Research Evaluation

This community focuses on measuring, mapping, and interpreting science through bibliometric data. Major themes include citation-based evaluation of researchers, journals, institutions, countries, and research programs; field normalization and cross-disciplinary comparison; and the limitations and consequences of rankings and assessment exercises. A parallel strand studies knowledge structures and research fronts, including HIV/AIDS, tribology, graphene, and information science.

Typical methods combine citation, co-citation, bibliographic coupling, author–paper, and journal–journal networks with community detection, centrality measures (including PageRank and the K-index), similarity measures, and institutional or technology maps. Percentiles, percentile classes, top-10/top-25 indicators, integrated impact measures, and fractional counting are proposed as alternatives or complements to the h-index and journal impact factor. RPYS and its interactive implementations reconstruct historical roots, while text analytics and MeSH enrich citation-based mappings.

Recent work emphasizes normalization, statistical and conceptual validity, conservation under aggregation, and fair attribution in large collaborations. It also compares major data sources—Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, and Dimensions—and examines weakening journal-impact-factor effects in the digital era. Interactive tools, network overlays, and frameworks for policy and R&D evaluation signal a trend toward more granular, computational, and responsible assessment.

3ed87ab8b652a9aa756e0c057e97e41526e37ca9.text:
## Community Structure in Complex and Dynamic Networks

This community centers on detecting, evaluating, and exploiting mesoscale structure in complex networks. Major themes include the lack of a universal community definition; multi-criteria and Pareto-based evaluation; overlapping, fuzzy, signed, attributed, bipartite, and multilayer communities; and core–periphery organization and global bridges.

Typical methods range from modularity and multislice modularity optimization to label propagation (including stabilized LabelRank), density-based clustering with manifold learning, clique percolation, local spectral clustering, personalized PageRank diffusion, and locally biased dynamical processes. Probabilistic approaches include generative models and variational Bayes for shared and layer-specific communities, conditional latent tree models, and survival or regression models for peer influence. Spectral analysis and random-matrix theory are used to study detectability limits, while axiomatic models formalize core–periphery structure. Other work develops generalized cores, structural correlation mining, and algorithm-selection frameworks.

Recent trends emphasize scalable, localized analysis for very large graphs; dynamic visualization, evolving PageRank, time-varying centrality, and bibliometric evolution; and richer representations incorporating multiple edge types, node attributes, weights, and positive or negative ties. Applications span social and mobile networks, Web services, biological and bibliometric systems, image segmentation, online activities, and prediction of adoption, churn, and risky behavior.

212c226748c567ed2da2a8eeaefb0fd30d9a7999.text:
### Dynamic Topic Discovery and Social Data Analytics

This community centers on extracting knowledge from large, evolving, and socially generated data. Major themes include topic modeling for hypertext, scientific literature, reviews, and temporal text streams; social-media analysis for events, trends, popularity, sentiment, misinformation, and user interests; and information retrieval tasks such as query expansion, summarization, question answering, and technology-assisted review. Applications span disease surveillance, disaster response, tourism, environmental warnings, scientific hypothesis generation, and knowledge-base timelines.

Typical methods combine probabilistic models—including LDA, hierarchical and dynamic topic models, multi-grain models, and topic-based networks—with statistical data mining, machine learning, ontology similarity, fuzzy logic, and graph analysis. Spatial and temporal structure is frequently exploited for burst detection, event retrieval, trend visualization, and location-based optimization. Neural approaches are emerging in recommendation and text representation, including CNN-based next-song prediction and character-level embeddings for multilingual tweet clustering.

Recent directions emphasize scalability and timeliness: parallel dynamic topic modeling, summarization-assisted learning, continuous stream processing, and analysis of massive geo-tagged or social datasets. The community also increasingly focuses on validation and operational impact, particularly ranking hypotheses, supporting decision makers, forecasting rare events, and turning noisy online data into actionable knowledge.

e8fdb65809a3e2345bdca7077d31ef33377fe1fe.text:
**Online Social Networks: Diffusion, Influence, and Risk**

This community studies how online and scholarly networks form, evolve, and transmit information, behavior, and risk. Major themes include information cascades and rumor propagation; influence, virality, popularity, and engagement; anomaly, malicious-URL, fake-news, and criminal-network detection; community structure, homophily, diversity, and tie strength; and applications in disasters, finance, health, and privacy.

Typical methods combine graph analysis—centrality, pair-dependency, modularity, community detection, structural balance, threshold diffusion, and vulnerability measures—with statistical learning and predictive modeling. Researchers analyze large-scale Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Yelp, citation, and enterprise datasets, using Hawkes processes, topic models, sentiment and affect analysis, multimodal content mining, and ranking or classification systems. Formal work also characterizes diffusion outcomes, equilibria, computational complexity, and influence-control strategies.

Recent directions extend beyond static network structure toward dynamic, heterogeneous, and exogenous processes: mass media and absent nodes in diffusion, network growth and decay, profile changes, and real-time event sensing. Multimedia analysis of images and video remixes, engagement-aware popularity prediction, crowd-based misinformation triage, visual risk analytics, and automated emergency-aid ranking highlight increasing operational use. Privacy-aware audience controls and socially informed studies of suicide ideation, diversity, and scientific memes broaden the social impact agenda.

d0884bf3aa34817662404204d23683e03687f88e.text:
## Scalable Data, Text, Graph, and Mathematical Information Systems

This community spans two closely related areas: intelligent information access and high-performance data management. Text research addresses clustering, classification, authorship analysis, topic diversity, active learning, and relevance feedback. Typical methods include probabilistic mixture models, vector-space and k-nearest-neighbor classifiers, association-rule pruning, hyperonymization, genetic feature selection, topic-model refinement, and user-guided metric learning.

A substantial strand concerns mathematical information retrieval and digital libraries. Systems combine textual keywords with formula representations, using formula preprocessing, canonicalization, semantic enrichment, query expansion, result merging, faceted interfaces, and MathML-based rendering. Related work extracts identifier definitions and namespaces from mathematical prose and notation.

Database and systems papers emphasize scalable analytics over heterogeneous data. Accumulo, D4M, Graphulo, BigSparse, and associative arrays support high-throughput ingestion, external graph processing, provenance storage, and GraphBLAS-style computation. Polystore and Lara algebra research seeks unified execution across relational, array, graph, and key-value systems, complemented by relational-lattice and relational-semantics foundations.

Query optimization and cloud management use memory-aware cost models, least-expected-cost planning, workload learning, reinforcement learning, feedback control, and dynamic scaling with performance guarantees. Recent directions favor integrated, interactive, and semantic infrastructure: learning-assisted workload management, autonomous high-recall review, heterogeneous data unification, and richer formula-aware search and publication platforms.

75338ae540815440a41b8431e1a7458ad53e92e3.text:
### Bibliometric Evaluation, Equity, and Research Performance

This community studies how scientific performance should be measured and how evaluation shapes universities, researchers, and national research systems. Major themes include productivity and impact indicators; comparisons across fields, institutions, regions, and countries; gender, age, seniority, nepotism, and geographic inequalities; collaboration, interdisciplinarity, internationalization, and editorial-board participation; and the design and critique of national assessment exercises, particularly Italy’s VQR.

Typical methods are large-scale bibliometric analyses using Web of Science or Google Scholar, citation and publication indicators, field-standardized measures, fractional and author-order counting, and proposed alternatives such as the FSS, impact measures, and stochastic multivariate models. Researchers apply regression and quantile regression, Granger causality, network analysis, clustering for author disambiguation, time-series comparisons, distributional and Gini analyses, funnel plots for uncertainty, and simulation of ranking distortions.

Recent work trends toward more responsible and statistically careful evaluation: accounting for uncertainty, disciplinary differences, collaboration patterns, gender effects, contribution order, and citation-distribution skewness rather than relying on journal impact factor or raw counts. The literature also examines fairer rankings, optimal assessment windows, research knowledge flows, scientific specialization, publication recommendation data, and the consequences of alternative recruitment and evaluation policies.

0caf0019c959887ebf048e42c958855696411c80.text:
## Social Media Networks, Misinformation, and Online Influence

This community centers on computational analysis of social-media ecosystems, especially Twitter, Facebook, and YouTube. Major themes include political polarization and voting behavior, community structure and echo chambers, misinformation and conspiracy narratives, extremist and state-sponsored campaigns, demographic inequality, and platform security. Several studies examine fringe communities such as Gab and the spread of ISIS- or Russia-linked content.

Typical methods combine network and signed-graph analysis, structural balance, community detection, random-walk sampling, and propagation modeling with machine learning. Nonnegative matrix factorization, sparse learning, LDA, regression, embeddings, stance and spam classification, image-based demographic inference, and metadata/network/temporal features are used to infer preferences, identities, credibility, and content adoption. Researchers also build operational systems, including real-time detectors, social bots for health interventions, crawlers, and defenses against Sybil devices and malicious applications.

Recent work increasingly addresses misinformation as a socio-technical process: how segregation, emotion, attention, verification, and recommendation shape diffusion. It also emphasizes real-time and cross-platform measurement, bias-aware evaluation, adversarial campaigns, automated bot-generated content, and interventions. Alongside empirical studies, papers explore decentralized search, personalized conversation generation, and improved tools for reproducible recommender-system experiments.

71fdc9eb480da0dd827d1882ceee58de87f47583.text:
### Data Integration, Entity Resolution, and Human-Guided Quality

This community centers on making heterogeneous, noisy, and conflicting data usable. Major themes include entity resolution and consolidation; data fusion and truth discovery across Web, linked, enterprise, and open-data sources; integrity constraints and data-quality discovery; crowdsourcing; and scalable similarity search and linkage.

Typical methods combine probabilistic models for source reliability, dependence, multiple truths, and unknown data; blocking and locality-sensitive hashing; graph and multipartite matching; deep representations; and optimization-based matching. String edit-distance joins use partitioning, hashing, and minimum-based sketches, while vector search employs compressed codes and reranking. Constraint discovery covers functional and order dependencies, ontology relationships, and syntactic patterns. Human involvement is formalized through worker-error confidence intervals, adaptive task assignment, quality-aware entity resolution, route evaluation, graph queries, and latency reduction.

Recent directions emphasize reducing expert effort through deep learning and automated blocking, while retaining quality guarantees via human–machine cooperation. Systems increasingly target web-scale and billion-vector workloads, exploit parallelism and recurrence, and incorporate prediction into spatial crowdsourcing. Other emerging concerns include source dependence and misinformation, structural variation in Web extraction, multiple valid truths, and estimating the effect of incomplete or unknown data on analytical results.

847c55f063127f13b293bd4c120b547529e8973a.text:
### Recommender Systems: Personalization, Robustness, and Richer Signals

This community centers on improving personalized recommendation across products, media, news, education, events, and tags. Core themes include collaborative filtering and ranking from explicit or implicit feedback; sequential and session-based prediction; and integration of content, social, geographic, and multimodal signals. Several works address practical weaknesses such as sparse interactions, cold-start users/items, long-tail artists and products, diverse user interests, missing modalities, and filter bubbles.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, slope-one predictors, nearest-neighbor and graph-based models to Markov chains, context trees, co-clustering, signed-network ranking, and Bayesian Personalized Ranking. Neural approaches increasingly use autoencoders, variational models, recurrent networks, factorization machines, deep feature-interaction architectures, and nonlinear user–item transformations. Text, subtitles, audio, visual features, tags, and short-text embeddings provide auxiliary representations.

Trustworthiness and system behavior are important complementary concerns: studies examine shilling and adversarial attacks, reputation estimation, rating reliability, popularity bias, social influence, and link prediction. Recent work trends toward hybrid and heterogeneous-signal models, multimodal and sequence-aware recommendation, mixture representations for multiple tastes, efficient cold-start inference, interpretable recommendations, and application-specific systems such as playlist, news, educational, and local-event recommendation.

908717e57dde1433d899c08442c830f31c4a3ea9.text:
## Network Representation Learning and Dynamic Graph Mining

This community studies complex, social, temporal, and knowledge networks, with emphasis on extracting structure, predicting missing or future relationships, and understanding communities and diffusion. Major themes include dynamic and continuous-time modeling (temporal event graphs, dynamic stochastic blockmodels, temporal graph reconstruction), heterogeneous and multi-relational networks, graph clustering, link prediction, and structural identity. Knowledge-graph applications address triple scoring, entity normalization, and fact checking, while social-network studies examine privacy, fraud de-anonymization, criminal and insider-trading anomalies, signed relations, and team formation.

Typical methods combine probabilistic models (stochastic blockmodels, Markov chains, maximum likelihood, graph grammars), machine learning (random forests, deep neural embeddings, ensemble scoring, and path-based prediction), and network algorithms such as random walks, min-cut, peeling, triangle counting, and centrality analysis. Sampling and systems research targets large-scale crawling, MapReduce, external-memory generation, and sampling with quality guarantees.

Recent trends move from static graphs toward temporal, heterogeneous, uncertain, and indirect interactions; from pairwise embeddings toward representations preserving triangles, parallelograms, and structural roles; and from descriptive analysis toward prediction, attribution, and actionable applications. Neural and deep embedding methods increasingly integrate node content with graph structure.

4f85c7e87986563bf2e7395b9ae975c3d4101d7c.text:
## Social Media as a Lens on Geography, Mobility, and Urban Life

This community studies how user-generated and network data can reveal human behavior across physical and digital spaces. Major themes include inferring locations from non-geotagged text, mapping mobility and visited places, identifying urban boundaries and functional regions, and characterizing neighborhoods through temporal activity. Other work examines group colocation, tourism-location networks, business-site selection, local advertising, event scheduling, and political or behavioral prediction. Urban perception is also prominent, including emotional routes, smellscapes, soundscapes, and the effects of parks on sentiment.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Reddit, Flickr, Facebook, Weibo, mobile-phone, check-in, and review data with machine learning and statistical modeling. Approaches include convolutional neural networks, Gaussian mixture models, heuristic labeling, sentiment and semantic analysis, low-rank approximation, density-based spatial clustering, network reconstruction, influence modeling, and graph indexing. Several studies emphasize validation, uncertainty calibration, bias correction, and comparisons with surveys or independent mobility data.

Recent trends move beyond simple geotag analysis toward multimodal and semantic geolocation, hyper-local inference, probabilistic confidence, population-representative mobility estimates, and fine-grained urban sensing. Research increasingly integrates spatial, temporal, social, and affective signals to support urban planning, public health, commerce, and personalized services.

838e366e6156add031d65fe106ecd75319664238.text:
## Information Retrieval: Neural Ranking, Semantic Search, and Evaluation

This community centers on improving information retrieval and search quality across web, email, mobile, personal-memory, news, image, and question-answering settings. Major themes include relevance ranking, query understanding and expansion, expert and entity search, passage retrieval, spam and content-quality detection, and temporal or credibility-aware retrieval.

Typical methods combine traditional IR signals such as BM25 with neural representations and matching. DeepRank, Match-Tensor, attention-based models, and parameterized neural language models capture local relevance, term dependencies, and vocabulary mismatch. Word2vec/query2vec embeddings support query expansion, clustering, entity decomposition, and heterogeneous-network expert finding. Other work uses CNNs, LSTMs, kernels, hashing, binary signatures, and dimensionality reduction for semantic matching, scalable indexing, and similarity search. Learning-to-rank methods include bipartite ranking, multitask learning, online policy learning, and counterfactual correction of click bias.

A strong supporting strand develops resources and evaluation: LETOR 4.0, WikiPassageQA, relevance and credibility measures, interpretable ranking, explainable search, and theoretically grounded multileaving. Systems also process streaming news and identify salient or linked entities.

Recent directions emphasize deep semantic retrieval, entity- and event-aware search, dynamic and conversational interaction, personalization, explainability, unbiased learning from implicit feedback, and scalable retrieval for massive or continuously changing collections.

f9797c37f6dc22adfd040750f67e878429667313.text:
### Graph Querying, Semantics, and Scalable RDF Management

This community studies the foundations and practical optimization of querying RDF, SPARQL, Linked Data, and increasingly property graphs. Major themes include SPARQL algebra and multiset semantics, OPTIONAL/left-outer joins, entailment under OWL, incomplete information, preferences, provenance, and path-query complexity. A parallel focus is distributed querying: federated SPARQL, SPARQL-LD, Linked Data navigation, heterogeneous relational/RDF sources, endpoint selection, replication, and heuristic query reordering.

Typical methods combine formal semantics and complexity analysis with algebraic rewriting, constraint-based optimization, Datalog, structural and partition-based summaries, cardinality estimation, incremental evaluation, and runtime plan adaptation. Systems research includes FedX, FEDRA, ROSIE, SGDQ, Gremlinator, GRAPHITE, and Gremlin-based traversal. Schema and quality concerns are addressed through relational-to-RDF mappings, ShEx, RDF descriptions, property-graph type systems, XML schema inference, and validation.

Recent directions emphasize interoperability between RDF/SPARQL and property graphs/Gremlin, scalable and resilient federations, provenance and explainability, and more accessible query interfaces such as keyword–SPARQL hybrids and example-based querying. Benchmarking and workload generation (gMark and Geographica), analytical RDF data cubes, geospatial querying, and graph summarization support systematic evaluation and practical deployment.

0b72ea6b7a6ecd289a0c7f20a3dfe4c4ebfb8847.text:
## Principles and Systems for Scalable Data Management

This community spans database theory, query processing, and practical data-intensive systems. Major themes include query optimization—join ordering via MILP, cardinality estimation with deep learning, adaptive indexing, materialized-view cleaning, and index tuning—as well as parallel query evaluation, communication complexity, correctness, and coordination-free computation. Conjunctive queries, inequalities, dynamic updates, metaquerying, provisioning, and sampling receive formal complexity and algorithmic treatment.

A second focus is integrating databases with analytics and machine learning. Systems such as AC/DC, ease.ml, and sparse-tensor approaches execute learning over relational data, while ModelHub addresses model and artifact lifecycle management. Graph workloads are translated into relational or Datalog-like processing through Vertica and EmptyHeaded. Other systems target fast-stream exploration, visual insight recommendation, revenue-aware recommendation, and urban spatiotemporal analysis.

Typical methods combine mathematical formulations, worst-case bounds, sketches and sampling, sparse representations, distributed algorithms, learned models, declarative languages, and workload-aware physical design. Cloud and distributed settings motivate work on OLTP coordination, MapReduce optimization and debugging, replication consistency, dataset versioning, and privacy-preserving outsourced queries.

Recent directions emphasize learned and automated optimization, high-level abstractions without performance loss, integrated data/ML platforms, collaborative data management, and scalable analytics over graphs, streams, and heterogeneous datasets.

528b52ed909eb13822f4d6d7a4ffa9060b241563.text:
## Network Dynamics, Influence, and Structural Analysis

This community studies how information, opinions, and influence evolve over complex, social, and communication networks. Major themes include consensus and polarization in DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, signed, biased, and multi-topic opinion models; the evolution and strategic modification of social power; and the role of centrality, navigability, communicability, PageRank, robustness, and discoverability in network structure. Other work addresses link prediction, missing edges, community and backbone discovery, network delays, and web crawling.

Typical methods combine graph theory, spectral and matrix analysis, dynamical-systems convergence and stability proofs, probabilistic/random-network models, and optimization for edge or node modifications. Empirical studies mine voting records, Twitter and other interaction data, often using motifs, topic and temporal coherence, traffic activity, or user-specific behavioral features. Scalable algorithms use spectral embeddings, local centralities, information-theoretic objectives, and fast subgraph or path procedures.

Recent directions emphasize dynamically changing and signed networks, heterogeneous individual thresholds and biases, logically interdependent topics, and feedback loops between opinions and personalized recommendations. There is also growing attention to incomplete or noisy data, scalable computation, network design for influence and delay reduction, and robustness under targeted disconnection.

882f84d070a938d6d043636f82e75d135edd5da3.text:
## Data Management Under Uncertainty, Inconsistency, and Structure

This community studies database systems that must reason beyond clean, deterministic relational data. A dominant theme is probabilistic and uncertain databases: query answering, aggregation, top‑\(k\) ranking, similarity search, joins, and scalable processing under tuple, attribute, and correlated uncertainty. Methods include lifted inference, knowledge compilation, decomposition trees, U‑relations, probabilistic pruning, structural decompositions, and relational query plans.

A second major theme is explanation and diagnosis. Provenance and data differencing support workflow reproducibility, auditing, debugging, and why/why-not explanations. Causality and responsibility for query answers and non-answers are connected to abductive diagnosis, view updates, repairs, and answer-set programs.

The papers also develop foundations for inconsistent and incomplete information: repair-based inconsistency measures, active integrity constraints, certain answers, conceptual dependencies, tuple-generating dependencies, finite controllability, and schema-mapping composition. Complexity and tractability frontiers are characterized using chase procedures, attack graphs, treewidth, circuit classes, and undecidability results.

Additional work addresses graph/tree query mining, utility-oriented and sequential episode mining, XML policy repair, web wrappers, interactive relational browsing, and peer-to-peer data exchange.

Recent directions emphasize making probabilistic processing practical and scalable, exploiting structural width and database engines, supporting richer correlations, and integrating uncertainty, provenance, inconsistency, and user interaction.

649ede21e99b597cec39b0cee12442cd6fa95736.text:
## Efficient, Flexible, and Fair Data Search

This community centers on high-performance data management and retrieval across relational, graph, web, textual, and multimedia systems. A major theme is compact representation: bitmap and Roaring indexes, variable-byte, Huffman, difference, and SIMD-based compression reduce storage and accelerate intersections, decoding, and multidimensional access. Hashing theory and compressed n-gram indexes address scalable string and language-model processing.

Query processing is another focus, including keyword search and concise object summaries, skyline and aggregate skyline joins, fuzzy and linguistic SQL, hidden-database crawling, query reranking services, workflow retrieval, and graph pattern search. Typical methods combine specialized indexes, ranking and top-k algorithms, cost-aware query planning, formal analysis, and empirical benchmarking.

Systems research emphasizes hardware and distributed acceleration through GPUs, multicore CPUs, SIMD instructions, in-memory databases, and Spark/Flink dataflows. Graph mining and graph-database planning extend these techniques to large heterogeneous networks.

Recent directions increasingly incorporate learning and user-centered objectives: learned graph query planning, recommendation and tag reranking, diversity, demographic fairness, and equitable attention in rankings. Overall, the work trends toward adaptive, highly parallel, storage-efficient retrieval while supporting imprecise data, complex preferences, and responsible ranking.

6c8eb275dba147e2f5eb066e06e7b5c38efda58c.text:
**Scholarly Data Mining, Discovery, and Recommendation**

This community develops infrastructure and methods for making scientific literature machine-readable, searchable, and reusable. Major themes include semantic publishing and Linked Open Data, metadata and citation extraction, citation matching, knowledge-graph construction, and quality assessment. Several studies address scholarly text reuse, plagiarism, copied or contradictory content, and author-contribution extraction.

A second strong theme is research-paper recommendation. Work spans recommender-as-a-service architectures (Mr. DLib), repository-scale systems such as CORE Recommender, user modeling with mind maps, and analyses of choice overload, position bias, and ranking quality. Researchers emphasize realistic deployment challenges, noisy data, reproducibility, and evaluation over time rather than relying on single aggregate metrics.

Typical methods combine rule-based and statistical information extraction, OCR, supervised learning, near-duplicate detection, MinHash, citation and network analysis, and hybrid textual/network models. Large-scale processing commonly uses Hadoop, MapReduce, distributed retrieval, and massive bibliographic corpora.

Recent trends include moving from isolated prototypes toward reusable APIs, production recommender services, and openly released datasets such as RARD II; automating continuously updated scholarly knowledge graphs; interlinking extracted data across the LOD cloud; and evaluating recommendation behavior with attention to temporal dynamics, presentation bias, and user choice.

eb68439d5baf6b5815b1e36e88988ff8213f4286.text:
## Rich Semantic Modeling for Structured Knowledge

This community develops semantic and model-oriented approaches for representing complex information beyond conventional documents. Core themes include ontologies for human activities and infrastructures, mechanisms, state changes, instances, scenarios, and highly structured scientific communication. Object-oriented modeling, frame semantics, upper ontologies, and hierarchies of aggregates and mechanisms are recurring design influences; the proposed Semantic Modeling Framework may be implemented in the XFO environment.

A major application area is digital history. Machine learning is used to construct people gazetteers for quantitative prosopography, while coordinated text-mining models and formative user-interface design support exploratory access to digitized historical newspapers. Work on a Norfolk, Nebraska, directory illustrates the integration of structured entities, richer attributes, and links between directory records and newspaper mentions.

The community’s repositories are envisioned as knowledgebases containing direct, richly modeled representations rather than document collections. In scientific communication, structured research reports explicitly represent research designs and support evaluation of internal and external validity. Overall, the papers show a trend from conceptual semantic frameworks toward practical, interactive historical tools and evolving, interlinked knowledgebases for scientific and cultural information.

e5a911dd8aeecf914d4f13c9b0e631b5da65f12d.text:
## Differential Privacy for Useful Data Release

This community focuses on privacy-preserving data publishing, analysis, and mining, with differential privacy as the dominant formal framework. Major application areas include histograms, sparse and high-dimensional data, range and marginal queries, clustering, decision trees, frequent-itemset mining, search logs, mobility data, social networks, and community detection. Complementary work examines provenance views, graph surrogates, anonymization of set-valued data, and attacks exploiting utility, background knowledge, or algorithm awareness.

Typical methods add calibrated noise to counts, wavelet coefficients, or query answers; privately construct hierarchical decompositions, partitions, bases, and synthetic datasets; and use matrix-mechanism or strategy-query approaches to answer workloads efficiently. Convex optimization, adaptive query selection, approximation algorithms, randomization, and constrained reconstruction are recurring techniques. Several papers explicitly optimize privacy–utility trade-offs, error metrics, computational efficiency, or workload-specific accuracy.

Recent trends emphasize data- and workload-aware mechanisms, near-optimal answers for correlated high-dimensional queries, local differential privacy for marginals, end-to-end private parameter tuning, and practical exploration or cleaning through noisy interfaces. The community also increasingly scrutinizes the limits of privacy: micro-reconstruction, inference despite anonymization, worst-case attacker knowledge, and the distinction between individual and population privacy.

85cdca8ea1ed1f0c693e01b72b0adf0a58b8ef2c.text:
## Network-Based Learning, Recommendation, and Health Discovery

This community studies how graph structure can support reasoning, recommendation, classification, and health surveillance. A central theme is the relationship between distance graphs and fuzzy or proximity graphs: alternative transitive closures produce different shortest-path and structural properties, motivating analysis of weighted, non-metric and semi-metric networks. These ideas are applied to document and co-occurrence networks, where highly semi-metric connections improve item- and user-based recommendations.

Typical methods include shortest-path and closure analysis, network representations of hyperlinks, citations, keywords, and user–item relations, and benchmark evaluation on MovieLens. Bio-inspired distributed systems use adaptive, community-driven algorithms for semantic and structural knowledge management. Agent-based T-cell cross-regulation models provide another self-organizing approach to document classification, while lightweight linear models, word-proximity networks, and uncertainty-based integration support protein-interaction extraction from biomedical text.

More recent work trends toward large-scale, real-world health applications: network analysis of Instagram timelines is used to detect drug interactions and adverse reactions, while city-wide electronic health-record and dispensing data reveal demographic biases in known drug–drug interactions. Overall, the research moves from foundational network geometry toward adaptive information systems and population-level biomedical monitoring.

a094e04f1de1a2f471205ad604826fac169658ca.text:
### Network Diffusion, Influence, and Epidemic Control

This community studies how information, influence, disease, and failures propagate through social, technological, biological, and cyber-physical networks.
