Recent trends include integrating graph structure with neural representation learning, combining sequential and non-consecutive semantic modeling, exploiting label taxonomies, and using attention, capsules, and ensembles to improve performance in noisy, imbalanced, or semantically complex settings.

d0d9d9834fc25f1ed5149b060945991f21c96094.text:
## Natural-Language Access to Structured Data

This community focuses on making structured databases and entity graphs accessible through natural-language or keyword queries. A central research theme is the semantic gap between users’ wording and database structure, especially keyword-to-schema/value mapping, intent preservation, and inference of valid join paths. The work also considers knowledge-rich queries over specialized domains such as biological databases and lightweight exploration of heterogeneous entity graphs.

Typical methods include translating natural-language questions into SQL or other structured queries, using query logs to improve mappings and joins, and developing end-to-end neural interfaces. For graph exploration, preview tables summarize important entity types and relationships within limited display space. Keyword-search systems address the tension between precise Boolean database semantics and ranked information-retrieval results, exemplified by queried units.

Evaluation and comparison are also prominent: a survey assesses 24 database NLIs against curated benchmark questions, highlighting differences in functionality and expressive power. Overall, recent trends move from manually engineered semantic mappings toward neural, end-to-end interfaces, while retaining emphasis on usability, exploratory browsing, domain knowledge, and systematic evaluation.

03bbba726d3eb101ee5b6f43999d60e7fb549e43.text:
### Multimodal and Interpretable Music Understanding

This community studies music representation, classification, retrieval, and semantic modeling through complementary modalities, especially lyrics, audio, and listener responses. A central theme is lyric-based genre classification: hierarchical attention networks model words, lines, segments, and songs, while self-attention identifies informative content features. These models support both large-scale genre prediction and more transparent music recommendation.

Another major theme is cross-modal retrieval between audio and lyrics. Proposed methods learn shared or canonical spaces using joint embeddings, deep two-branch neural networks, and canonical correlation analysis. Unlike approaches based only on global similarity, these studies emphasize temporal structure and sequential correlations across modalities.

The community also explores richer definitions of music semantics. An end-to-end two-view neural framework incorporates EEG signals alongside audio to model listener perception, addressing the limitations of fixed tags and audio-only representations.

Typical methods include recurrent networks, hierarchical and self-attention, deep multimodal architectures, correlation learning, and neural fusion of physiological and acoustic data. Recent trends move toward temporally aligned cross-modal representations, interpretable attention-based recommendations, larger datasets, and perception-grounded semantic models.

5ff767a7ea34c72a3849f3a81c42b68db966f355.text:
## Community Detection and Dynamic Network Structure

This community centers on defining, detecting, and evaluating cohesive structure in complex networks. Major themes include the lack of a universal community definition; comparisons of modularity, overlapping quality metrics, multi-criteria and Pareto-based evaluation; and algorithm selection for different network regimes. Methods range from modularity and multislice modularity optimization, stochastic and geometric block models, spectral and manifold-learning techniques, density-based clustering, label propagation, clique percolation, k-truss and core–periphery analysis, to local spectral and personalized-PageRank methods. Probabilistic inference, variational Bayes, maximum likelihood, survival models, and axiomatic approaches extend community analysis beyond purely structural graphs.

A strong trend is toward richer network representations: multilayer and multiplex interactions, node and edge attributes, uncertain networks, weighted and two-mode graphs, and private/public connections. Research also increasingly addresses overlapping, shared and layer-specific communities, as well as dynamic and continuous-time networks through tie decay, evolving teleportation, and temporally regularized visualization. Scalability motivates localized algorithms for billion-node graphs, distributed dynamics, and nearly linear-time recommendation or clustering methods. Applications span social influence and churn, smartphone adoption, online dating, bibliometrics, Web services, recommendations, biological systems, and image segmentation.

0b90ff6fb26633f3bb4fdcb5a551232740c29644.text:
## Probabilistic, Inconsistent, and Explainable Data Management

This community studies database systems beyond deterministic, perfectly consistent data. A major theme is probabilistic and uncertain databases: query answering, joins, aggregates, top-\(k\) ranking, similarity search, and scalable processing under tuple independence, exclusivity, correlations, and continuous uncertainty. Methods include knowledge compilation, decomposition trees, tree decompositions, lifted inference, relational representations such as U-relations, probabilistic pruning, and specialized join algorithms.

A second theme is explanation and responsibility. Provenance, data differencing, causality, responsibility, Shapley values, and provenance graphs support auditing, debugging, reproducibility, hypothetical reasoning, and understanding both query answers and non-answers. Answer-set programs connect causality with database repairs and abductive diagnosis.

Theoretical work characterizes tractability and complexity through attack graphs, bounded derivation depth, finite controllability, width parameters, chasing, and undecidability results. Related efforts address inconsistent databases, integrity constraints, repairs, inconsistency measures, active repairs, and XML policy consistency.

Other topics include schema mappings, peer data exchange, web wrappers, query testing, interactive relational browsing, and MapReduce performance explanations. Recent directions emphasize making probabilistic processing practical at scale, supporting richer correlations and aggregates, using approximate or randomized computation, and integrating explanations, repair, and uncertainty into usable database workflows.

7e2d34ca27e51c7a702ca23faa50711a2d2f6827.text:
## Mining Dynamic Web and Social Knowledge

This community centers on extracting, organizing, and exploiting latent information from large, evolving web and social-media collections. Major themes include probabilistic topic modeling—covering hypertext links, temporal topic birth/death, scientific-article bundling, reviews, event reports, and creative cross-domain discovery—and user-centered retrieval, recommendation, and summarization. A second strong focus is real-time event and anomaly detection from Twitter, geo-tagged streams, spatial objects, and other sensors, including sports, collective action, disease, misinformation, and environmental events.

Typical methods combine LDA and its dynamic, hierarchical, clustered, or multi-grain variants with graph and network models, density-based spatial algorithms, power-law analysis, named-entity and relation extraction, sentiment and content analysis, and statistical machine learning. Neural networks support next-song recommendation and character-based multilingual tweet clustering, while fuzzy ontology matching, provenance, and visualization improve interactive access and explanation.

Recent trends emphasize scalability and streaming operation: parallel topic learning, summarized inputs, massive geo-social datasets, and near-real-time detection and summarization. Research also increasingly integrates multimodal signals, social impulses and revisits for popularity prediction, automated hypothesis generation with candidate ranking and validation, and semantic/entity timelines and summaries for decision support.

a6476a6687ffe57c204507d54fbe859124d2311d.text:
## Scholarly Knowledge, Recommendation, and Evaluation

This community focuses on mining, organizing, and delivering scholarly information. Major themes include research-paper recommendation, scholarly knowledge graphs and semantic publishing, citation and bibliographic parsing, large-scale information retrieval, and fairness and quality assessment in rankings and online services.

Typical methods combine content and network signals: titles, abstracts, terms, keyphrases, document embeddings, co-citation, citation graphs, and author or venue metadata. Systems employ NLP information extraction, classification, near-duplicate and text-reuse detection, blocking and supervised matching, MapReduce/Hadoop, Neo4j, and automatically maintained knowledge graphs. Recommender research emphasizes hybrid models, meta-learning for per-instance algorithm selection, explanation-based tuning, user modeling, and recommender-as-a-service architectures. Evaluation uses online living labs, large-scale recommendation logs, active sampling, time-series metrics, and user preference elicitation.

Recent work increasingly addresses deployment and responsible evaluation: production-scale services such as Mr. DLib and CORE, datasets with tens of millions of recommendations, and portals such as NLPExplorer and CL Scholar. It also studies position bias, counterfactual learning-to-rank, partially randomized rankings, demographic disparities, attention equity, and choice overload. Overall, the trend is from isolated algorithms toward scalable, continuously evaluated, explainable, and fair scholarly infrastructures.

b38b3e2288235faf672b5fb0d80cf0f7258b46fa.text:
## Cognitive and Social Recommendation in Networked Platforms

This community studies recommender systems that combine behavioral, temporal, semantic, and social signals. A major theme is cognitive-inspired tag and hashtag recommendation: models based on ACT-R activation, frequency, recency, semantic context, and forgetting explain and predict tag reuse, improve sparse folksonomy performance, and support user acceptance. Related work models attention and interpretation dynamics in resource recommendation.

A second theme is social recommendation for marketplaces, music, jobs, and classifieds. Studies exploit friendships, trust, weak ties, location, transactions, ratings, and social influence to address sparsity, cold start, and consumer choice. Methods include collaborative filtering, social regularization, regular equivalence, hybrid content/tag models, graph and triadic analyses, and scalable service architectures.

Recent work increasingly uses neural item embeddings and deep learning, incorporating interaction frequency and recency while evaluating diversity, novelty, fairness, and real-time click-through performance—not only accuracy. Empirical online and user studies examine acceptance, friend versus crowd influence, and deployment effects. The community also contributes reusable infrastructure, notably the TagRec framework, and analyzes broader social phenomena such as rumor convergence and confirmation bias in hashtag usage.

b63e4e7a476055f61723a8540b642ab9078c67c9.text:
### Social Network Dynamics, Diffusion, and Risk Analytics

This community studies online social networks as dynamic systems of interaction, influence, information diffusion, and collective behavior. Major themes include cascade and meme propagation, virality and popularity growth, attention and engagement, competing-product adoption, and the roles of strong and weak ties. Other work focuses on community structure, homophily, gender and demographic inference, profile evolution, and the assembly and decay of social platforms.

Security and risk are prominent: researchers detect anomalous or malicious behavior, rank criminal intermediaries, assess network vulnerability, identify malicious URLs, and model cascading financial or social harms. Social media is also examined for crisis response, including multimodal disaster datasets and automatic ranking of emergency-aid information.

Typical methods combine graph centrality, pair-dependency, overlap measures, modularity-based community detection, threshold and diffusion models, Hawkes processes, statistical analysis of large platform datasets, and machine learning for popularity, engagement, demographic, and content prediction. Visual analytics supports risk monitoring, while embeddings fuse transaction and relational data.

Recent directions emphasize large-scale, multimodal, and temporally explicit analysis; content-agnostic and exogenous drivers of diffusion; early prediction of popularity and engagement; and models that integrate network structure with semantics, user heterogeneity, and external media.

757f28f6442719d442ebe1b3322473256265d63d.text:
**Mapping Scientific Communities and Urban Knowledge**

This community studies how scholarly fields form, evolve, and can be understood through computational and spatialized analysis. A major theme is bibliometric mapping of *Cybergeo*, tracing thematic change since 1996 and identifying readership, research areas, and semantic proximities. Related work examines interdisciplinarity by combining citation-based classifications with semantic classifications derived from article abstracts and keywords. Another focus is the emergence and restructuring of scientific communities, especially how co-authorship networks assemble around topics of different size and specificity.

Typical methods include citation-network and co-authorship-network analysis, text mining, keyword extraction, semantic-network construction, and machine-learning techniques for organizing and maintaining large academic corpora. Comparisons between self-declared keywords, citation relations, and full-text themes are used to provide complementary views of scholarly production. Interactive applications and spatialized indicators support reflexive exploration and open-science practices.

The community also connects computational mapping with substantive reflection on urban theories, drawing on interdisciplinary perspectives about urbanization. Recent trends move beyond simple publication counts toward integrated, scalable analyses of semantic, citation, collaboration, and spatial relations, enabling the detection of emerging fields and more coherent scholarly communities.

403286086b4c32d9a5a1b28690b18741a16af024.text:
### Information Retrieval, Ranking, and Semantic Search

This community centers on improving information retrieval through learned relevance modeling, ranking, and search over heterogeneous resources. Major themes include document, passage, entity, dataset, email, e-commerce, mobile-app, and expert retrieval; query understanding and clustering; web-quality and spam detection; and retrieval-based question answering.

Typical methods combine classical retrieval principles with machine learning: learning-to-rank, pointwise/pairwise/listwise and groupwise scoring, bipartite ranking, multi-stage retrieval, and axiomatic regularization. Neural approaches include BERT and multilingual BERT, convolutional and kernel models, word and query embeddings, semantic hashing, and generative models. Researchers also exploit heterogeneous bibliographic networks, knowledge-enriched entity representations, schema labels, graph structures, and temporal features. Efficient large-scale search motivates signatures, hashing, approximate k-nearest-neighbor graphs, and sketch-based indexing.

A strong emphasis is placed on benchmarks and evaluation, including LETOR, TREC Deep Learning, WikiPassageQA, and dataset-search collections. Recent trends include deep pretrained rankers, cross-lingual zero-shot relevance transfer, permutation-invariant and document-interaction-aware ranking, interpretable and post-hoc ranking analysis, dynamic and multi-stage retrieval, and direct optimization for question-answering objectives. The community increasingly targets practical, specialized, and conversational search settings while addressing latency, sparse labels, evolving information, and semantic mismatch.

d31826d27825098e4610e4cd35535a92cea974a7.text:
## Network Representation, Prediction, and Security

This community centers on computational analysis of complex, social, heterogeneous, and dynamic networks. Major themes include link and relationship prediction, community detection and clustering, graph similarity, network classification, anomaly and fraud detection, and modeling temporal change. Applications span online platforms, urban dynamics, criminal and covert networks, insider trading, privacy, collaboration, and knowledge graphs.

Typical methods combine structural heuristics with statistical, probabilistic, and machine-learning approaches. Local similarity and reliable-route indices predict links and weights; random walks, absorbing Markov chains, and graph sampling support search and scalable measurement. Neural and deep graph embeddings represent nodes, content, and evolving topology for clustering, prediction, recommendation, entity normalization, and fraud mitigation. Other work develops latent-space models, probabilistic graph grammars, MapReduce triangle counting, external-memory graph generation, and probabilistic graph-edit-distance search. Formal analyses address locality, convexity, clustering thresholds, and attack difficulty.

Recent trends emphasize temporal and continuous-time representations, dynamic embeddings aware of both global topology and recent changes, heterogeneous and multimodal urban modeling, and generative models for evolving graphs. Evaluation, benchmarking, sampling quality guarantees, privacy-preserving community deception, and attribution of online fraud are also increasingly prominent.

1264f6175fe84acf1415943ea66db299c919e95c.text:
### Data Integration, Entity Resolution, and Quality at Scale

This community focuses on making heterogeneous, noisy, and conflicting data usable. Major themes include entity resolution and record linkage; data fusion and truth discovery; data cleaning through integrity constraints, dependencies, and provenance; and human-in-the-loop quality control. Applications span scholarly metadata, government addresses, social and Web data, open-data platforms, linked data, and spatial crowdsourcing.

Typical methods combine blocking and similarity search (locality-sensitive hashing, partitioning, string/edit-distance joins, and compressed vector indexes) with matching, graph optimization, and collective inference. Truth-discovery models estimate source reliability, resolve conflicts, and can represent multiple valid truths. Crowdsourcing is used for labeling, worker assessment, route evaluation, and ER verification, with optimization for cost, latency, precision, recall, and confidence guarantees. Constraint discovery and enforcement include functional/order dependencies, ontology dependencies, syntactic-pattern mining, and temporal provenance queries.

Recent directions emphasize reducing expert effort through deep representations and embeddings for entities, columns, and relational data; schema-agnostic and progressive ER; scalable collective matching; and human–machine cooperation. Systems increasingly target web-scale or billion-vector workloads, adaptive and fault-tolerant algorithms, prediction-based spatial assignment, and data markets that improve data sharing and integration incentives.

25647042496f9eb766b2f609a6e706f5d118a73f.text:
### Scalable Intelligent Information and Data Systems

This community spans intelligent text and mathematical information retrieval alongside high-performance data management. Text-focused research develops probabilistic and topic models, clustering, supervised categorization, association-rule feature selection, genetic keyword optimization, and user-guided or active-learning methods for high-recall review. Evaluation emphasizes relevance, topical diversity, feedback efficiency, and document-quality estimation.

A substantial systems theme is scalable representation and processing of heterogeneous data. Associative arrays provide a common algebra for spreadsheets, databases, matrices, and graphs, supporting high-throughput streaming updates, provenance ingestion, and AI data wrangling. Accumulo, D4M, Graphulo, BigSparse, and BigDAWG demonstrate distributed, external-memory, polystore, and graph-analytic architectures.

Database work addresses in-memory and column-store query optimization, multi-join cost prediction, disjunctive predicates, relational-lattice algebra, and cloud workload management. Typical methods include cost models, algebraic transformations, logging and sorting for sequential storage, benchmarking on large clusters, feedback control, reinforcement learning, and supervised learning.

Recent trends emphasize autonomous systems with performance or reliability guarantees, cost-aware cloud scaling, and integration of machine learning into workload and review workflows. In mathematical search, systems increasingly combine text with formula structure, semantic enrichment, notation analysis, identifier-definition extraction, interactive faceted interfaces, and digital repositories.

5e858017e46f176152927debdea4b8e65e8cc8f2.text:
### Social Media Networks, Polarization, and Information Integrity

This community studies how online social networks shape political opinion, collective behavior, and information reliability. Major themes include community detection and ideological polarization; misinformation, rumors, fake news, and disinformation; computational propaganda and extremism; and security threats such as spam, bots, Sybil devices, malicious applications, and organizational surveillance. Several papers examine political events and elections, including U.S. primaries, the 2016 and 2017 Russian influence campaigns, Charlottesville, Italian disinformation, ISIS support, and anti-Latinx discourse.

Typical methods combine large-scale Twitter, Facebook, YouTube, Reddit, and search-engine data with network analysis, retweet and followership graphs, PCA-based ideological scoring, temporal analysis, and propagation modeling. Machine-learning approaches include nonnegative and structured matrix factorization, sparse learning, LDA with regression, semi-supervised and deep neural classifiers, and metadata, textual, temporal, and interaction features. Surveys, user studies, and simulation models complement computational analyses.

Recent work increasingly emphasizes early, message-level rumor detection; distinguishing data from ranking bias; modeling overlapping beliefs and intra-community conflict; inclusive community detection; and leveraging crowd signals or targeted social bots for intervention. Cross-platform studies and analyses of coordinated state-sponsored campaigns highlight the growing concern with algorithmic amplification, echo chambers, and scalable manipulation.

eac605d2d0f99dcbf5cd18473872bb0171173a3a.text:
### Scalable Similarity Search in High-Dimensional Data

This community studies efficient approximate and exact similarity search over large, high-dimensional datasets, especially for multimedia retrieval, image search, document retrieval, and machine learning. The central challenge is the curse of dimensionality, which limits traditional tree-based and linear indexing methods.

Locality Sensitive Hashing (LSH) is a major focus. The papers identify weaknesses in existing LSH systems—such as redundant work in top-*k* multimedia search and poor real-time behavior—and propose practical improvements, including MMLSH and cache-conscious QWLSH for query workloads. Multi-index hashing further reduces storage and supports cosine similarity search through compact binary codes.

Other work develops index-based cosine threshold querying with optimality guarantees, extending threshold-processing ideas through inverted indexes. HD-Index uses hierarchical RDB-trees built on Hilbert keys to improve the scalability–accuracy tradeoff for approximate *k*-nearest-neighbor search. Graph-based methods are also advancing: the Satellite System Graph addresses inefficiencies in sparse NSG-style structures and seeks greater search efficiency.

Overall, the research trends toward scalable, cache-aware, workload-conscious indexing; stronger accuracy or optimality guarantees; compact representations; and increasingly sophisticated hierarchical and graph-based structures for massive datasets.

45c799119f89e3f0028a31b0568f7a8cd3594deb.text:
## Network Diffusion, Influence, and Epidemic Control

This community studies how information, influence, infection, and failures propagate through social, technological, spatial, and interdependent networks. Major themes include influence maximization and marketing, epidemic modeling and containment, diffusion-source localization, hidden-network recovery, and cascade dynamics under temporal or adaptive structures.

Typical methods combine probabilistic diffusion models—independent cascade, linear threshold, SIS/SI, complex contagion, and continuous-time Markov processes—with optimization and learning. Submodularity and adaptive-submodularity support greedy seed selection, while mixed-integer programming, heuristics, random walks, particle swarm optimization, and lattice formulations address resource-constrained campaigns, recruitment, and revenue. Source detection uses Jordan centers/covers, candidate subgraphs, and two-stage inference; network recovery and cascade learning exploit partial, aggregate, or temporally ordered observations. Random-matrix, percolation, message-passing, and stability analyses provide theoretical guarantees.

Recent work increasingly reflects realistic settings: dynamic, temporal, and adaptive networks; myopic or full-adoption feedback; partial observations; competing influence; non-submodular cascades; and online decision-making. Applications broaden from advertising to epidemic costs and containment, malicious-information tracing, mobile crowd sensing, conservation, education, and cyber-physical self-healing. Efficiency and scalability remain central, including limited probing, sampling, trajectory coverage, and scalable estimators for large evolving data.

e8ec52d17780a00fc9971faa85d148745ce246f4.text:
## Multilayer Social Networks and Dynamic Social Analysis

This community centers on modeling and analyzing complex social systems beyond the single-layer graph. Major themes include multiplex and multilayer networks, where online, offline, semantic, professional, or interaction ties are jointly studied; community detection and group evolution; link prediction; identity linkage across platforms; and diffusion processes involving information, epidemics, opinions, and misinformation.

Typical methods include multilayer degree centrality, reciprocity and motif measures, clustering coefficients, structural and homophily similarity, association-rule mining, topic modeling, sentiment classification, and language models. Community studies use GED, SGCI, Louvain, and Infomap, including dynamic variants that update only regions affected by graph changes. Diffusion research applies independent-cascade, branching-process, epidemic, and mobility-based models, often with seed-selection strategies. Other work develops mixture sampling estimators, synthetic-network generators, factoid embeddings, and theoretical analyses of epidemic thresholds, triangles, and multiplex entanglement.

Recent trends emphasize unified representations of interconnected online identities, cross-platform deanonymization and privacy, missing-data effects, and realistic synthetic data. Research is increasingly data-driven, using Facebook, Twitter, blogs, mobile phones, and Web 2.0 observations. Applications are expanding toward personalized recommendation, human resources, health surveillance, vaccination campaigns, fact-checking, and information-campaign management.

6ea7322542149a95a105fe829a76db6b1bc1ce5c.text:
### Bibliometrics and Research Evaluation in Italy

This community centers on measuring and explaining scientific performance, especially within the Italian university and national research systems. Major themes include individual and institutional productivity, field and regional disparities, gender differences, academic careers, collaboration, internationalization, interdisciplinarity, and knowledge diffusion. Several studies critically assess national evaluation exercises, university rankings, publication periods, counting rules, and the use of journal impact factor or citation indicators as quality proxies.

Typical methods are large-scale bibliometric analyses of Web of Science publications and national researcher censuses, often standardized by field. Researchers use stochastic and multivariate models, quantile regression, Granger causality, gravity models, network analysis, Gini coefficients, Pareto tests, funnel plots, and field-normalized indicators such as FSS, MNCS, and scientific specialization indexes. Author disambiguation employs probabilistic clustering and semi-supervised learning.

Findings address persistent north–south and gender gaps, age and seniority effects, the durability of “top scientist” status, editorial-board influence, and the benefits of international or interdisciplinary collaboration. Recent directions emphasize uncertainty-aware evaluation, contribution-sensitive authorship and counting methods, methodological critiques of assessment rankings, geographic knowledge flows, gender-sensitive institutional comparisons, and data-driven tools for publication recommendation and author identification.

77e6c09152cf4f2be8240f218d7d191d002b1bc1.text:
### Social Media as a Lens on Place, Mobility, and Behavior

This community studies how large-scale social and location-based media can reveal human behavior, urban environments, and social influence. Major themes include geolocation inference from tweets and Reddit; mobility, commuting, visited places, and urban-boundary detection; spatial-temporal activity structures; and network analysis of contacts, tourism locations, recommendations, and malicious nodes. Applications span business-site selection, special offers, daily deals, political voting, sports outcomes, sexual-violence tracking, food culture, and the emotional qualities of urban spaces.

Typical methods combine user-generated text, profiles, hashtags, sentiment, check-ins, photographs, and mobility traces. Researchers use convolutional neural networks, supervised classifiers, Gaussian mixture models, heuristic labeling, low-rank approximation, graph-based feature extraction, network analysis, clustering, and large-scale aggregation. Several studies address sparse or biased data through inferred labels, population synthesis, benchmark comparison, quantified uncertainty, calibration, and standardized evaluation.

Recent directions emphasize scalable analysis of massive corpora and distributed trajectory mining; richer semantic mapping of sound, smell, beauty, happiness, and land use; deep learning and influence modeling; and multimodal or cross-platform data integration. The community increasingly links computational predictions with offline surveys, travel surveys, crowdsourced judgments, and real-world applications in planning, public health, commerce, and crisis response.

bfd95120a593d3e31e04b5cea219505291797b3a.text:
## Community Detection in Complex and Evolving Networks

This community focuses on defining, detecting, and evaluating community structure beyond the classical disjoint, static graph. Major themes include the lack of a universal community definition; comparative and multi-criteria evaluation; overlapping, fuzzy, signed, attributed, uncertain, weighted, multiplex, and multilayer communities; and relationships between communities, cores, bridges, polarization, and influence.

Typical methods range from modularity and multislice modularity optimization to stochastic block and geometric block models, spectral and local spectral clustering, density-based clustering with manifold learning, clique percolation, label propagation, and locally biased diffusion. Probabilistic inference—including maximum likelihood and variational Bayes—is used for uncertain and heterogeneous networks. Several works emphasize analytical guarantees, detectability thresholds, metastability, and efficient algorithms for large graphs. Evaluation commonly uses synthetic benchmarks, real social, web, bibliometric, biological, and communication networks, and algorithm-selection frameworks.

Recent trends favor scalable and interpretable local methods for discovering communities in massive graphs, explicit treatment of multiple interaction layers and node or edge attributes, and dynamic analysis that preserves temporal structure. Applications increasingly connect community structure to peer influence, churn, adoption, recommendations, visualization, centrality persistence, and polarization. Core–periphery organization and multi-objective optimization are recurring alternatives to single modularity-based views.

819767f1fb425c7ce3dc8a1b8f29ae0896637847.text:
## Scholarly Impact, Discovery, and Evaluation in the Web Era

This community examines how scholarly work is discovered, disseminated, assessed, and represented across journals, books, repositories, social platforms, and academic websites. Major themes include the validity and interpretation of altmetrics; relationships among citations, readership, downloads, tweets, Mendeley saves, and peer assessments; open-access and arXiv citation advantages; and bibliometric evaluation of books, publishers, and research performance. Other work addresses scholarly recommendation, venue classification, conference paper–reviewer matching, citation behavior, hyperlink motivations, and digitized bibliographic infrastructure.

Typical methods combine large-scale bibliographic, usage, and social-media datasets with statistical analysis, including correlation, regression, principal-component and factor analysis, ranking indicators, and comparative studies. Researchers also use surveys, interviews, expert judgments, visualization evaluation, machine learning for hyperlink classification and reference resolution, and optimization through integer programming.

Recent trends emphasize moving beyond citation counts toward multidimensional and faster indicators of impact, while stressing heterogeneity, data quality, disciplinary differences, and confounding factors. Preprints, open access, repository readership, and web activity are treated as both communication mechanisms and possible predictors of later citation impact. The community also increasingly develops recommendation and assistance systems to manage information overload, improve peer-review allocation, and support navigation of expanding scholarly ecosystems.

e9939281121ec04cc89c096d025cab887e0765a3.text:
### Scientometrics, Citation Networks, and Fair Research Evaluation

This community centers on measuring, mapping, and evaluating science through bibliometric data. Major themes include field-normalized citation indicators, percentiles and percentile rank classes, h-index extensions, centrality measures, journal impact, institutional reputation, and author-level performance. Many studies question whether conventional metrics are comparable across disciplines, time periods, publication venues, or collaboration scales.

Typical methods combine citation and co-citation networks, bibliographic coupling, journal and publication profiling, clustering, network maps, similarity measures, and visualization. Researchers use Web of Science, Scopus, Microsoft Academic, Dimensions, PubMed, and patent databases, often comparing coverage and linked-reference quality. Fractional counting, conservation rules, randomized baselines, precision/recall tests, correlation analysis, and statistical or mathematical indicator design are common.

Applications include reconstructing HIV/AIDS research fronts, delineating nanotechnology, mapping universities and journals, tracing influential works with RPYS, and analyzing collaboration diversity. Recent work trends toward online and interactive tools, database interoperability, field- and time-normalized impact assessment, fairer credit allocation in large collaborations, and examination of policy effects such as national evaluation systems. The literature increasingly emphasizes metric validity, conceptual limitations, and unintended consequences rather than simply proposing new rankings.

504b9e21caa50190c1ad0b55b7cab892d648613f.text:
**Mining Topics, Events, and Social Signals at Scale**

This community studies computational methods for extracting structure, meaning, and actionable signals from large, dynamic information collections. A central theme is topic modeling: LDA- and PLSA-based approaches are extended to hypertext links, temporal topic evolution, multi-grain opinion aspects, scientific-article classification, and cross-domain “bisociative” discovery. Other work focuses on social-media intelligence, including event detection and retrieval, real-time summaries, collective-action analysis, sentiment sensing, misinformation monitoring, and inference of user interests and retweet motivations.

Typical methods combine probabilistic and neural models with stream processing, clustering, ranking, and information extraction. Character-based neural embeddings address noisy multilingual tweets, while CNNs support sequential song recommendation. Spatial and temporal analysis identifies bursty regions, geo-tagged events, and popularity or revisitation dynamics. Knowledge-oriented systems generate entity timelines, summarize semantic entities, support ontology- and fuzzy-logic question answering, and validate hypothesis-generation candidates. Visualization and provenance connect extracted events and analytical interactions to interpretable results.

Recent directions emphasize scalable and online processing of massive streams, parallel or summarized topic learning, multimodal and geo-temporal event understanding, and practical real-time services. Applications increasingly target decision support in health, tourism, environmental monitoring, science, and crisis or public-event analysis.

5faba51bf5a4b74a9d0e42a6a46654fca4e40016.text:
## Recommender Systems: From Preference Modeling to Responsible Personalization

This community centers on improving recommendation quality across collaborative, content-based, hybrid, and sequential settings. Core themes include modeling long- and short-term preferences, anonymous sessions, playlist continuation, news and local-event discovery, and complex contexts such as cross-domain behavior and shared accounts. Addressing cold start, sparsity, missing modalities, popularity bias, long-tail exposure, diversity, and user heterogeneity is a recurring concern.

Typical methods range from matrix factorization, slope-one predictors, nearest-neighbor and graph-based ranking to latent-variable models, metric learning, context trees, ontologies, and multimodal content representations. Neural approaches increasingly dominate, including variational autoencoders, nonlinear collaborative filtering, recurrent and graph neural networks, factorization-machine hybrids, attention models, and deep CTR prediction. Reinforcement learning is applied to advertising and dynamic recommendations, while determinantal point processes support efficient diversification.

Recent work emphasizes session-aware and sequential recommendation, richer graph and multimodal modeling, mixtures of user tastes, and personalization under incomplete information. The community also expands beyond accuracy toward robustness against shilling attacks and noisy ratings, reputation modeling, unbiased offline evaluation, social influence, interpretability, long-tail and popularity-bias management, and explicit revenue–user-experience tradeoffs.

f05e941f47fbeebbaa63543fe9fd142eccd1d1c6.text:
### Network Analytics for Scholarly and Knowledge Infrastructures

This community studies large-scale information networks, especially Wikipedia, scholarly communication, coauthorship, citation, patent, and research-data networks. Major themes include ranking people, papers, universities, and technologies; detecting communities and emerging fields; resolving author-name ambiguity; enriching bibliographic metadata; and improving information retrieval and knowledge organization.

Typical methods are graph-theoretic and bibliometric: PageRank, CheiRank, weighted and reduced Google matrices, centrality measures, spectral analysis, modularity and stochastic block models, graphons, and network sampling. Studies also use machine learning and statistical models, including LSTMs for citation-growth prediction, PCA, sentiment and statistical features for summarization, and mouse-fixation signals for user-interest modeling. Evaluation commonly relies on labeled datasets, triangulated benchmarks, agreement measures, simulations, and comparisons with established rankings.

Recent trends emphasize longitudinal and multilingual analysis of Wikipedia, dynamic prediction of technology and community growth, and finer distinctions between popularity and prestige. The literature also moves toward linked-data enrichment, semantic-web knowledge systems, integrated digital libraries, visual scientometric mapping, and reproducible open-science workflows using Jupyter. Privacy, stewardship, and sampling bias increasingly appear as methodological and governance concerns.

d0b44986a4a06a5fc91a20f61d5bc747931fd66a.text:
## Dynamic Graphs, Narrative Networks, and Utility Mining

This community spans three main themes. First, it develops scalable graph algorithms for shortest paths, reachability, distance and latency queries, using landmark labeling, hop-doubling indices, distance sketches, pruning, hub acceleration, and vertex-centric parallelism. Temporal graphs and link/stream graphs receive particular attention, with models and algorithms for time-respecting paths, temporal centrality, and weighted, directed, or bipartite interactions.

Second, many works analyze social and narrative networks. Character-interaction graphs support genre classification, plot summarization, role and event prediction, and analysis of television series and films. Methods include network centralities, multilayer and dynamic modeling, automatic extraction from co-occurrence or machine learning, signed-edge inference, and link prediction.

Third, the community advances sequential and utility-oriented pattern mining. Episode and sequential-pattern methods address closedness, simultaneous events, complex sequences, projection, parallelization, occupancy, and item-specific utility. Surveys and formal work address association-rule representations and privacy-preserving mining.

Recent directions emphasize temporal and streaming representations, efficient processing of massive scale-free graphs, parallel and hardware-aware indexing, and richer notions of pattern value incorporating utility, privacy, recency, trends, and occupancy. Narrative analysis is likewise moving from static character graphs toward dynamic, multilayer, and predictive models.

821a34275c007e00868d2fcc71f433a7d9ec3c18.text:
### Probabilistic, Explainable, and Reliable Data Management

This community focuses on querying and reasoning over data that is uncertain, inconsistent, distributed, or richly structured. A major theme is probabilistic databases: exact and approximate query evaluation, aggregates, top-*k* ranking, similarity search, uncertain joins, and correlated models such as Markov views. Related work studies possible-world and repair semantics, certain answers, integrity constraints, and quantitative inconsistency.

Explainability is another central theme. Provenance, lineage, data differencing, causality, responsibility, Shapley values, and “why/why-not” explanations support auditing, debugging, hypothetical reasoning, and workflow reproducibility. Database repairs, active integrity constraints, belief annotations, and peer-to-peer exchange address inconsistent knowledge and conflicting views.

Typical methods include relational rewritings, chase procedures, knowledge compilation, OBDDs and decomposition trees, tree- and width-based structural decompositions, answer-set programming, probabilistic bounds and pruning, and complexity analysis. Graph-oriented methods mine tree queries and predicate paths, while ensembles and discriminative link prediction support triple scoring and knowledge-graph fact checking.

Recent directions emphasize scalable approximate inference inside standard database engines, richer correlation and uncertainty models, practical performance debugging, benchmark-driven knowledge-graph evaluation, and selective data cleaning for trustworthy fact checking. Fundamental work continues to map tractability frontiers and establish undecidability and lower-bound results.

366a3c7b17674a44b1b61220211a5c21a79e5112.text:
## Flexible, Efficient, and Responsible Data Retrieval

This community explores how to make data systems more expressive, scalable, and socially responsible. Major themes include flexible querying over imprecise or incomplete data, including fuzzy summaries, linguistic SQL, incomplete-data skylines, and aggregate skyline joins. Search and recommendation research addresses reranking, user-specific preferences, tag consistency, expert discovery, social content, and fairness across demographic groups, including antidote data and representation-aware diversification.

A second strong theme is high-performance indexing and retrieval. Papers develop set-intersection algorithms, bitmap indexes and Roaring bitmaps, compressed inverted lists, n-gram indexes, hashing schemes, and low-overhead database indexes. Compression and query execution are accelerated using SIMD, GPUs, hybrid CPU–GPU systems, and transaction engines. Other work targets efficient spatial matching, hidden-web crawling, third-party reranking services, and workflow or graph-database search.

Typical methods combine formal query models with algorithmic analysis, data structures, factorization and embeddings, association-rule reranking, distributed in-memory dataflow, and empirical benchmarking. Recent directions emphasize learning-assisted query planning, scalable graph mining, GPU/SIMD acceleration, and fairness-aware ranking—reflecting a shift toward systems that are simultaneously faster, more adaptive, and more accountable.

71472f9d6799e055e2f144ba39a53a1e864d014a.text:
**Graph Data Management, Querying, and Interoperability**

This community focuses on efficient, expressive querying and management of RDF, knowledge graphs, and property graphs. A major theme is SPARQL optimization: join and OPTIONAL/left-outer-join reordering, runtime and incremental optimization, federated source selection, replicated fragments, summary graphs, and OWL entailment. Researchers also extend SPARQL with preferences, keywords, provenance, incomplete information, and example-based querying, improving expressiveness, trust, and accessibility.

A second theme is interoperability and data integration. Formal direct mappings connect relational databases, RDF/OWL, and property graphs, while Gremlinator and G2GML enable translation between SPARQL, Gremlin, and graph representations. Work on property-graph type systems, view updates, and incremental view maintenance addresses schema, evolution, and update management.

Methods range from cost-based and heuristic optimization, adaptive storage, indexing, partitioning, and graph traversal to Datalog semantics, formal complexity and decidability analysis, approximation algorithms, graph parsing, and topological similarity. Provenance graphs are summarized through segmentation, while surveys characterize graph systems and real-world workloads.

Recent trends emphasize very large and distributed graphs, federated and cloud settings, RDF–property-graph convergence, controllable benchmarking with gMark, richer analytical/path queries, and practical usability and reliability.

9a7ecc380fce4728a78bc22598636c74d86592d0.text:
### Preserving and Making Sense of Evolving Digital Knowledge

This community focuses on durable, interoperable preservation and discovery of digital objects, especially web resources, scholarly artifacts, and linked data. Core themes include modeling scientific and cultural information as related life-cycle components; repository architectures for heterogeneous, distributed objects; and preservation of evolving datasets, web pages, annotations, and “scholarly orphans.” Web-archive research addresses acquisition, freshness, temporal search, collection drift, missing resources, timestamping, and user behavior.

Typical methods combine standards-based data modeling (OAIS, MPEG-21, RDF, SPARQL, Open Annotation, PROV-O, PAV, SharedCanvas), persistent identifiers, modular repositories, and virtual machines for durable decoding. Researchers build crawlers, aggregators, caches, semantic layers, query languages, and browser-facing services, and evaluate them through large-scale logs, longitudinal web collections, archival holdings, and annotation datasets. Ranking and retrieval exploit links, tags, social-bookmarking evidence, lexical signatures, titles, and entity relatedness; network-flow methods assign dataset credit.

Recent trends emphasize real-time and context-aware collection using social media, machine-learning optimization of archival access, linked-data versioning, provenance and quality, interoperable annotations, and richer semantic querying of archived documents.

18d800ceea5f5b784a7c0c485aa6953b1146bd15.text:
### Cross-Modal Hashing and Shared Semantic Retrieval

This community focuses on efficient similarity search across heterogeneous modalities, especially images, text, video, tags, and events. The central goal is to learn compact, comparable representations that preserve semantic relationships while reducing storage and query costs.

Typical methods include shallow matrix factorization, latent-factor models, semantic projections, correlation alignment, and shared embedding spaces. A strong emphasis is placed on binary hashing: discrete code optimization, unified or isomorphic codes, decorrelated bits, triplet and unary losses, and correlation-aware or asymmetric quantization. Several works address practical retrieval through probability-based indexing and improved Hamming-distance ranking, including multi-view search.

Deep learning increasingly integrates feature extraction and hash-code learning, using convolutional and fully connected networks, fusion supervision, and joint optimization of hashing functions and unified codes. Graph convolutional modeling improves textual representations, while coupled CycleGAN-based hashing supports unsupervised learning across modalities.

Recent trends move from handcrafted features and pairwise/triplet-heavy objectives toward scalable unary losses, discrete and quantization-aware learning, end-to-end deep architectures, and methods that handle weak or absent labels. Overall, the research shifts toward more accurate cross-modal alignment, richer semantic modeling, and efficient large-scale indexing.

00ac1bbdfe0f71c7662db91f87263ed873f7331b.text:
## Principles and Systems for Modern Data Management

This community spans foundational query processing and practical data-intensive systems. A central theme is efficient relational computation: join ordering via MILP, worst-case-optimal and projected joins, conjunctive queries with inequalities, parallel correctness, communication complexity, and dynamic query evaluation. Query optimization increasingly incorporates learning, including deep models for cardinality estimation and plan generation, while approximate query processing uses sampling, maximum-entropy summaries, and deep generative models.

A second major theme is extending database technology to graph, video, sensor, and streaming data. Relational engines and join algorithms support graph analytics and pattern matching; visual and video systems use learned filters and hierarchical representations to reduce expensive CNN-based extraction; model-based compression manages correlated time series. Systems research emphasizes declarative, high-level engines, integrated machine-learning pipelines, collaborative dataset versioning, and automated data-structure or index design.

Typical methods combine theoretical complexity and communication analyses with executable engines, sketches, samplers, probabilistic summaries, neural networks, matrix multiplication, and specialized hardware. Distributed data management also covers OLTP execution, replication and staleness, secure outsourced queries, coordination-free computation, and blockchain protocols and emulation. Overall trends favor learned and approximate optimization, unified analytics workflows, hardware-conscious execution, and scalable support for nontraditional data.

d3c60eba95c289dbcb8f3fab188a6c5e99e5d0fe.text:
## Network Dynamics, Influence, and Social Opinion

This community studies how network structure, relationships, and information flows shape collective behavior. A dominant theme is opinion dynamics: DeGroot, Friedkin–Johnsen, bounded-confidence, Bayesian, and multi-topic models examine consensus, disagreement, polarization, fragmentation, social power, and the effects of bias, susceptibility, antagonism, and homophily. Signed networks receive particular attention through structural balance, negative ties, boomerang effects, and political voting applications.

A second theme concerns influence and network design. Studies optimize PageRank, node discoverability, communicability, opinion maximization, influence spread, and fairness across socially salient groups, often by modifying links, selecting seeds, or designing network topologies. Related work analyzes centrality-maximization games and dynamic relative interaction matrices.

Typical methods include graph Laplacians, spectral and random-walk techniques, stability and asymptotic analysis, mean-field and game-theoretic models, optimization, motif-based analysis, and empirical validation on Twitter, parliamentary votes, and other interaction data. Scalable algorithms address link prediction, graph labeling, backbone discovery, and web crawling.

Recent directions emphasize dynamic, topic- and time-dependent networks; feedback between opinions and personalized recommendation; data-driven inference from partial observations; controversy and partisan structure; and algorithmic fairness, including fragmentation mitigation and bias in influence and cyberbullying detection.

c0860357aa53f0b545ee27f7bd3e58844052d424.text:
### Collaborative Knowledge, Tagging, and Semantic Search

This community studies how user-generated knowledge can be structured, enriched, and exploited across Wikipedia, Wiktionary, social tagging systems, and professional networks. Major themes include collaborative classification and folksonomies; vocabulary and tag evolution; semantic relatedness and ontology matching; Wikipedia categories, links, and edits as knowledge structures; and expertise, talent, and entity discovery.

Typical methods combine large-scale platform data analysis with graph-based modeling. Researchers use power-law and growth models to explain tagging behavior, clustering and community detection to analyze users and folksonomies, and centrality, HITS, PageRank-like measures, and network indicators for ranking pages, entities, and influential users. NLP pipelines transform Wiktionary into relational or machine-readable resources, extract entities and relations, and perform multilingual entity linking. Search applications employ query expansion, collaborative filtering, matrix factorization, learning-to-rank, semantic navigation, and group-profile signals.

Recent directions emphasize multilingual and language-agnostic resources, densely annotated Wikipedia corpora, scalable processing of user-generated data, and richer personalization. Professional-network research increasingly applies behavioral and social signals to expertise search, ideal-candidate retrieval, talent-flow analysis, and intent-sensitive ranking. Overall, the work moves from describing emergent social structures toward operational systems for semantic interoperability, recommendation, and personalized information access.

a765f8431369469c18e4f46c2558dc7817db16d7.text:
## Scalable, Scientific, and Resilient Data Management

This community focuses on building database systems that remain performant, reliable, and usable at modern scale. A major theme is multicore and distributed OLTP: work addresses high-contention concurrency control, snapshot isolation, transaction repair, actor-oriented execution, synchronization tradeoffs, automatic application partitioning, and parallel or adaptive recovery. Related studies examine consistency checking, isolation testing, transaction debugging, provenance, replication, and blockchain layers.

Scientific data management is another strong theme. Astronomy, finite-element analysis, simulations, and social-network studies motivate petabyte-scale warehouses, array and metadata support, spatial and multidimensional indexing, continuous stream processing, and full data life-cycle services. Query batching, data sharing, relational spatial algebra, and public data platforms are used to improve throughput and accessibility.

Typical methods combine new storage or execution architectures with analytical models, indexing schemes, scheduling and optimization algorithms, and evaluations on real or representative workloads. Systems are frequently assessed through throughput, latency, scalability, recovery cost, I/O, cache utilization, and energy consumption.

Recent directions emphasize heterogeneous and distributed infrastructures, NUMA-aware multicore processing, immutable and tamper-evident data, blockchain integration, autonomous timestamping, energy-efficient clusters, streaming-plus-historical analytics, and infrastructure durability. A parallel trend is making complex data analysis accessible through generated SQL and interoperable relational backends.

a10b833daca2b2c24cf0428deee33bcc2a9a9c30.text:
### Scholarly Search, Metrics, and Networked Science

This community studies how scholarly information is discovered, ranked, evaluated, and disseminated. A dominant theme is bibliometric assessment: Google Scholar, Web of Science, Scopus, and Google Scholar Metrics are compared for coverage, citation counts, journal rankings, highly cited documents, research-unit benchmarking, and relationships between citations and peer assessment. Studies also examine Google Scholar’s scale, data quality, profile-management burden, citation manipulation, and the decline of Microsoft Academic Search.

A second theme concerns open science and scholarly publishing, including open-access availability, green mandates, repository deposits, gold-OA cost sharing, self-archiving, and indicators combining heterogeneous data sources. Citation aging and the increasing visibility of older documents are also investigated.

Methods typically combine large-scale database queries, longitudinal and cross-sectional citation analysis, correlation and benchmarking, automated web extraction, and comparisons across fields and countries. Network analysis is applied to science-park link structures, airline motifs, online communities, Wikipedia norms, and patterns of disagreement.

Information-retrieval work develops learning-to-rank topic selection, deep-versus-shallow judging strategies, query expansion, and improved library-catalog ranking. Recent directions emphasize low-cost evaluation, open-access policy effectiveness, platform coverage and obsolescence, metric reliability, and the gaming or manipulation of scholarly indicators.

988f84912240c8fb9aec4e1e509a7ca79534c08c.text:
### Privacy-Preserving Data Publishing and Analysis

This community centers on releasing and analyzing sensitive structured data while balancing formal privacy, accuracy, efficiency, and practical usefulness. Major themes include differential privacy for histograms, range and high-dimensional counting queries, marginals, frequent itemsets, clustering, classification, data exploration, and hierarchical population statistics. Other work studies anonymization beyond differential privacy—including \(k\)-anonymity for relational and set-valued data, slicing, transparent anonymization, background-knowledge attacks, reconstruction risk, and privacy-preserving provenance and graphs.

Typical methods add calibrated noise, use hierarchical decompositions, wavelet transforms, matrix mechanisms, linear query strategies, convex optimization, adaptive workload selection, and data/workload-aware partitioning. Applications include search-log sanitization, mobility and transportation data, recommendation and location data, data cleaning, social networks, and private data federations using trusted hardware. Several papers explicitly optimize privacy–utility tradeoffs, computational scalability, or query-specific error rather than applying generic perturbation.

Recent trends move toward stronger local differential privacy, accurate high-dimensional and batch query answering, automated and accuracy-aware exploration, and efficient implementations. The scope also broadens from confidentiality alone to fairness, bias-aware synthetic mobility data, adversaries with algorithm or background knowledge, and protecting functionality or inference patterns in graphs and workflows.

728250c66fc0a66f47d4b7f8377a2a960730f157.text:
## Data Management, XML Warehousing, and Dynamic Analytics

This community centers on scalable management and analysis of complex, heterogeneous data. A dominant theme is XML databases and warehouses: tree-pattern querying, structural preferences, XOLAP rollups, summarizability, fragmentation, benchmarking, and architectures for multimedia, multisource, multistructure, and multimodal data. Business-intelligence research addresses lightweight systems for smaller enterprises and domain-specific warehouses, including medicine and archaeology.

A second major theme is automated database and warehouse optimization. Work studies dynamic index and materialized-view selection, workload clustering, frequent-itemset mining, attribute dependencies, query-driven fragmentation, and joint view-index design. Object-oriented database performance is examined through clustering policies and simulation frameworks that model changing access patterns.

Typical methods include data mining and clustering (frequent itemsets, k-means, query clustering), pattern-tree and algebraic query models, workload- and threshold-aware fragmentation, simulation-based evaluation, and benchmark construction. Text research introduces scalable document architectures and large-scale classification datasets; social-media studies detect events using mention anomalies, temporal entity clustering, and community formation.

Recent directions emphasize complex XML warehousing at scale, dynamic and workload-adaptive optimization, realistic benchmarks for changing behavior and complex hierarchies, and learning-based prediction— notably deep reinforcement learning for hierarchical classification. Social and epidemiological applications increasingly exploit real-time online data streams.

64ec7423a2ef9d20f406f38877f3ff44321e3e46.text:
### Scholarly Discovery, Recommenders, and Quality-Aware Knowledge Graphs

This community focuses on mining, organizing, and recommending scientific literature. Major themes include research-paper and citation recommendation, scholarly search and exploration, semantic publishing, citation matching, author-contribution extraction, and assessing the quality, fairness, and impact of rankings and scholarly content.

Typical methods combine content and network signals: term-based information retrieval, topic models, keyphrases, document embeddings, co-citation, citation graphs, and hybrid ranking pipelines. Recent systems use pretrained and domain-adapted language models such as BERT, candidate generation followed by reranking, meta-learning for per-instance algorithm selection, and explanation-based tuning of opaque models. Large-scale processing commonly relies on Hadoop, MapReduce, distributed retrieval, and graph databases such as Neo4j. Information extraction and text-reuse detection support linked open datasets and knowledge graphs, including GrapAL, CL Scholar, and NLPExplorer.

Evaluation is increasingly conducted in realistic settings through recommender-as-a-service deployments, online living labs, large recommendation datasets, and time-sensitive metrics. Recent work also emphasizes user choice overload, cold-start and incomplete citations, active evaluation sampling, position bias, counterfactual learning-to-rank, partially randomized rankings, and demographic fairness. Overall, the field is moving toward scalable, continuously updated, explainable, and socially responsible scholarly discovery systems.
